docs.title: Version
docs.text:
Semantic versioning for commands, tasks, and plugins:

use app_shell::app_engine::Version;

let v1 = Version::new(1, 2, 3);
assert_eq!(v1.major(), 1);
assert_eq!(v1.minor(), 2);
assert_eq!(v1.patch(), 3);

assert_eq!(v1.to_string(), "1.2.3");

docs.title: Version Compatibility
docs.text:
Same major version = compatible:

let v1 = Version::new(1, 0, 0);
let v2 = Version::new(1, 5, 3);
let v3 = Version::new(2, 0, 0);

assert!(v1.is_compatible_with(&v2));   // Same major
assert!(!v1.is_compatible_with(&v3));  // Different major

docs.title: Version Ordering
docs.text:
let v1 = Version::new(1, 0, 0);
let v2 = Version::new(1, 1, 0);
let v3 = Version::new(2, 0, 0);

assert!(v1 < v2);
assert!(v2 < v3);
assert!(v1 < v3);

docs.title: Version At Least
docs.text:

assert!(v.is_at_least(&Version::new(1, 2, 0)));   // Yes — 1.2.3 >= 1.2.0
assert!(!v.is_at_least(&Version::new(1, 3, 0)));  // No — 1.2.3 < 1.3.0

docs.title: Complete Test Example
docs.text:
use app_shell::app_engine::*;

struct CountingHandler {
    order: Arc<Mutex<Vec<usize>>>,
    tag: usize,
}

impl EventHandler for CountingHandler {
    fn handle(&self, _: &Event) {
        self.order.lock().unwrap().push(self.tag);
    }
}

#[test]
fn full_test_with_mocks_and_metadata() {
    // --- Setup ---
    let test_engine = TestEngine::new();
    let engine_ref = test_engine.engine_ref();

    let mut exec = MockCommandExecutor::new();
    let def = CommandDefinition::new("app.test", "Test", "Test command")
        .with_version(Version::new(1, 0, 0))
        .with_input_schema(PayloadSchema::of::<String>());

    exec.register(def, Box::new(EchoHandler)).unwrap();

    // --- Execute ---
    let cmd = Command::with_empty_input("app.test", CommandContext::new(ExecutionId::new()));
    let result = exec.execute(&cmd, &engine_ref).unwrap();

    // --- Assertions ---
    assert!(result.is_success());
    assert_command_executed(&exec, "app.test");
    assert_eq!(exec.executed_count(), 1);

    // --- Verify metadata ---
    let def = exec.list().first().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(def.version(), &Version::new(1, 0, 0));
    assert!(def.input_schema().unwrap().matches::<String>());
}

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The plugin security system controls what plugins can access and do within the App Engine. It consists of two layers:

flowchart TD
    PP["PluginPermissions<br/>(bitflags on manifest)"] --> Q1["'Can this plugin register commands?'"]
    PC["PermissionCheckedEngineRef<br/>(runtime enforcement wrapper)"] --> Q2["'try_load_resource()? → Err if no permission'"]
  • PluginPermissions — declared in the manifest, queried by the manager
  • PermissionCheckedEngineRef — wraps EngineRef with try_* methods that return Result

Default permissions are FULL_ACCESS — backward compatible.

docs.title: All Permissions
docs.text:
use app_shell::app_engine::PluginPermissions;
use app_shell::app_engine::{
    REGISTER_COMMANDS,
    REGISTER_TASKS,
    LOAD_RESOURCES,
    REGISTER_SERVICES,
    SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS,
    PUBLISH_EVENTS,
    READ_CONFIG,
    WRITE_CONFIG,
    FULL_ACCESS,
};
Flag Permission REGISTER_COMMANDS Can register command handlers REGISTER_TASKS Can register task handlers LOAD_RESOURCES Can load resources via ResourceManager REGISTER_SERVICES Can register services SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS Can subscribe to events PUBLISH_EVENTS Can publish events READ_CONFIG Can read configuration WRITE_CONFIG Can write configuration FULL_ACCESS All permissions (default)

docs.title: Creating Permissions
docs.text:
// No permissions
let none = PluginPermissions::new(0);
assert!(!none.can_register_commands());
assert!(!none.can_load_resources());

// Full access
let full = PluginPermissions::FULL;
assert!(full.can_register_commands());
assert!(full.can_load_resources());

// Default = full access (backward compatible)
let default = PluginPermissions::default();
assert!(default.can_load_resources());
assert!(default.can_write_config());

// Combined permissions
let limited = PluginPermissions::new(
    REGISTER_COMMANDS | SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS,
);
assert!(limited.can_register_commands());
assert!(limited.can_subscribe_events());
assert!(!limited.can_load_resources());
assert!(!limited.can_write_config());

docs.title: Bitwise Operations
docs.text:
let combined = PluginPermissions::new(REGISTER_COMMANDS)
    | PluginPermissions::new(SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS);

assert!(combined.can_register_commands());
assert!(combined.can_subscribe_events());
assert!(!combined.can_publish_events());

docs.title: Display
docs.text:
let perms = PluginPermissions::new(REGISTER_COMMANDS);
assert!(perms.to_string().contains("00000001"));

let full = PluginPermissions::FULL;
assert!(full.to_string().contains("11111111"));

docs.title: Declaring Permissions in Manifest
docs.text:
use app_shell::app_engine::{PluginManifest, PluginPermissions};

// Full access (default — backward compatible)
let manifest = PluginManifest::new("full_plugin", "Full Plugin");
assert_eq!(manifest.permissions(), PluginPermissions::FULL);

// Limited permissions
let manifest = PluginManifest::new("limited", "Limited Plugin")
    .with_permissions(PluginPermissions::new(
        REGISTER_COMMANDS | SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS,
    ));
let perms = manifest.permissions();
assert!(perms.can_register_commands());
assert!(perms.can_subscribe_events());
assert!(!perms.can_load_resources());
assert!(!perms.can_write_config());

// No permissions
let manifest = PluginManifest::new("restricted", "Restricted Plugin")
    .with_permissions(PluginPermissions::new(0));
let perms = manifest.permissions();
assert!(!perms.can_register_commands());
assert!(!perms.can_load_resources());
assert!(!perms.can_publish_events());

let mgr = PluginManager::new();

let id = mgr.register(

        .with_permissions(PluginPermissions::new(REGISTER_COMMANDS)),
    Box::new(StubPlugin),

assert!(!mgr.can_load_resources(id));
assert!(!mgr.can_register_tasks(id));
assert!(!mgr.can_publish_events(id));

docs.title: What It Is
docs.text:
A wrapper around EngineRef that checks permissions before allowing access to restricted operations. Read-only access is always allowed.

use app_shell::app_engine::PermissionCheckedEngineRef;

let engine = TestEngine::new();
let engine_ref = engine.engine_ref();

let checked = PermissionCheckedEngineRef::new(
    &engine_ref,
    PluginPermissions::new(LOAD_RESOURCES | SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS),
    "limited_plugin",
);

docs.title: Read-Only Access (Always Allowed)
docs.text:
Regardless of permissions, these are always accessible:

let _ = checked.config_store();      // &ConfigStore (read)
let _ = checked.preferences();       // &Preferences (read)
let _ = checked.state_manager();     // &StateManager (read)
let _ = checked.history_store();     // &HistoryStore (read)
let _ = checked.scheduler();         // &Scheduler (read)
let _ = checked.event_bus();         // &EventBus (read)
let _ = checked.signal_bus();        // &SignalBus (read)
let _ = checked.command_executor();  // &CommandExecutor (read)
let _ = checked.resource_manager();  // &ResourceManager (read)

docs.title: Permission-Checked Access
docs.text:
Each try_* method returns Result — Ok if permission granted, Err(PluginSecurityError) if denied:

// With LOAD_RESOURCES permission
let result = checked.try_load_resource()?;
assert!(result.is_ok());
let mgr = result.unwrap();
assert_eq!(mgr.resource_count(), 0);

// Without WRITE_CONFIG permission
let result = checked.try_write_config();
assert!(result.is_err());
let err = result.unwrap_err();
assert!(matches!(err, PluginSecurityError::PermissionDenied { .. }));
assert!(err.to_string().contains("WRITE_CONFIG"));
assert!(err.to_string().contains("limited_plugin"));

docs.title: Part 5: Using the Wrapper in Plugins
docs.text:
The Plugin trait still receives &EngineRef (not PermissionCheckedEngineRef) for backward compatibility. Domain plugins that want enforcement construct the wrapper themselves:

use app_shell::app_engine::*;

struct MyPlugin {
    permissions: PluginPermissions,
}

impl Plugin for MyPlugin {
    fn id(&self) -> &str { "my_plugin" }

    fn initialize(&mut self, ctx: &PluginContext, engine: &EngineRef) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        // Wrap engine with permission checking
        let checked = PermissionCheckedEngineRef::new(
            engine,
            self.permissions,
            "my_plugin",
        );

        // Use try_* methods for restricted operations
        let config = checked.try_write_config()
            .map_err(|e| PluginError::InitializeFailed {
                id: 0,
                reason: e.to_string(),
            })?;

        config.set("plugin.initialized", "true").map_err(|e| {
            PluginError::InitializeFailed {
                id: 0,
                reason: e.to_string(),
            }
        })?;

        Ok(())
    }

    fn start(&mut self, engine: &EngineRef) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let checked = PermissionCheckedEngineRef::new(
            engine,
            self.permissions,
            "my_plugin",
        );

        // Try to load a resource
        if let Ok(mgr) = checked.try_load_resource() {
            let _handle = mgr.load("config", "file:///plugin_config.json")
                .map_err(|e| PluginError::StartFailed {
                    id: 0,
                    reason: e.to_string(),
                })?;
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    fn stop(&mut self) -> Result<(), PluginError> { Ok(()) }
    fn dispose(&mut self) -> Result<(), PluginError> { Ok(()) }
}

// Register with limited permissions
let manifest = PluginManifest::new("my_plugin", "My Plugin")
    .with_permissions(PluginPermissions::new(
        LOAD_RESOURCES | WRITE_CONFIG | SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS,
    ));

engine.plugin_manager_mut().register(manifest, Box::new(MyPlugin {
    permissions: PluginPermissions::new(LOAD_RESOURCES | WRITE_CONFIG | SUBSCRIBE_EVENTS),
}))?;

docs.title: Part 6: Plugin Lifecycle Is Not Blocked by Permissions
docs.text:
A plugin with no permissions still has a normal lifecycle:

let id = engine.plugin_manager_mut().register(
    PluginManifest::new("restricted", "Restricted")
        .with_permissions(PluginPermissions::new(0)),
    Box::new(StubPlugin),
)?;

// Lifecycle works — permissions don't block lifecycle
engine.plugin_manager_mut().initialize(id, &engine_ref)?;
assert_eq!(engine.plugin_manager().state(id), Some(PluginState::Initialized));

engine.plugin_manager_mut().start(id, &engine_ref)?;
assert_eq!(engine.plugin_manager().state(id), Some(PluginState::Started));

engine.plugin_manager_mut().stop(id)?;
engine.plugin_manager_mut().dispose(id)?;

Permissions only affect runtime capabilities (what the plugin can do with EngineRef), not whether the plugin itself can be initialized/started/stopped/disposed.

docs.title: Part 7: Error Messages
docs.text:
Permission denied errors contain the plugin ID and permission name:

let checked = PermissionCheckedEngineRef::new(
    &engine_ref,
    PluginPermissions::new(0),
    "my_plugin",
);

let err = checked.try_load_resource().unwrap_err();
let msg = err.to_string();

assert!(msg.contains("my_plugin"));
assert!(msg.contains("LOAD_RESOURCES"));

docs.title: PluginSecurityError
docs.text:
use app_shell::app_engine::PluginSecurityError;

// PermissionDenied variant
let err = PluginSecurityError::PermissionDenied {
    plugin_id: "limited".to_string(),
    permission: "LOAD_RESOURCES".to_string(),
};
assert!(err.to_string().contains("limited"));
assert!(err.to_string().contains("LOAD_RESOURCES"));

// Implements std::error::Error
fn assert_std_error<E: std::error::Error>(_: E) {}
assert_std_error(PluginSecurityError::PermissionDenied {
    plugin_id: "x".to_string(),
    permission: "y".to_string(),
});

docs.title: DynamicPluginLoader

A contract stub for loading plugins from shared libraries:

use app_shell::app_engine::DynamicPluginLoader;

let loader = DynamicPluginLoader::new();

// Detect shared libraries
assert!(DynamicPluginLoader::is_shared_library("plugin.so"));
assert!(DynamicPluginLoader::is_shared_library("plugin.dll"));
assert!(DynamicPluginLoader::is_shared_library("plugin.dylib"));
assert!(!DynamicPluginLoader::is_shared_library("plugin.rs"));

assert!(matches!(result, Err(PluginError::LoadFailed { .. })));

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
fn do_work(engine: &mut AppEngine) -> Result<(), EngineError> {
    engine.service_manager_mut().start_all(&engine.engine_ref())?;
    // ServiceError auto-converts to EngineError via From impl
    Ok(())
}

match engine.initialize() {
    Ok(()) => {},
    Err(EngineError::AlreadyInitialized) => { /* continue */ },
    Err(EngineError::InvalidLifecycleTransition { from, to }) => {
        eprintln!("Invalid: {} -> {}", from, to);
    },
    Err(EngineError::SubsystemFailure { subsystem, reason }) => {
        eprintln!("{} failed: {}", subsystem, reason);
    },
    Err(e) => eprintln!("Unexpected: {}", e),
}

docs.title: Top-Level Error Handling
docs.text:
use app_shell::app_engine::*;

fn main() {
    let mut engine = Bootstrap::create()
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| {
            eprintln!("Bootstrap failed: {}", e);
            std::process::exit(1);
        });

    if let Err(e) = engine.initialize() {
        match e {
            EngineError::AlreadyInitialized => {
                // Continue — already initialized
            },
            EngineError::SubsystemFailure { subsystem, reason } => {
                eprintln!("{} subsystem failed: {}", subsystem, reason);
                // A service or plugin failed during initialization
                // Engine continues — panic was caught
            },
            _ => {
                eprintln!("Initialization failed: {}", e);
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.text:
// Command execution
match engine.execute_command(&cmd) {
    Ok(result) => { /* handle result */ },
    Err(CommandError::UnknownCommand { id }) => {
        eprintln!("No command: {}", id);
    },
    Err(CommandError::ExecutionFailed(msg)) => {
        // Could be handler error OR handler panic (Phase 24)
        eprintln!("Failed: {}", msg);
    },
    Err(e) => eprintln!("{}", e),
}

// Task execution
match engine.start_task(task_id) {
    Ok(result) => { /* handle result */ },
    Err(TaskError::NotFound { id }) => eprintln!("Task {} not found", id),
    Err(TaskError::InvalidState { current, requested, .. }) => {
        eprintln!("Can't {}: {} -> {}", requested, current, requested);
    },
    Err(TaskError::ExecutionFailed { reason, .. }) => {
        // Could be handler error OR handler panic (Phase 24)
        eprintln!("Failed: {}", reason);
    },
    Err(e) => eprintln!("{}", e),
}

docs.title: Converting to EngineError
docs.text:
fn do_work(engine: &mut AppEngine) -> Result<(), EngineError> {
    // All subsystem errors auto-convert via From
    engine.service_manager_mut().start_all(&engine.engine_ref())?;
    // ServiceError → EngineError::SubsystemFailure

    engine.execute_command(&cmd)?;
    // CommandError → EngineError::SubsystemFailure

    engine.start_task(task_id)?;
    // TaskError → EngineError::SubsystemFailure

    Ok(())
}

docs.title: Panic-Isolated Errors (Phase 24)
docs.text:
When a handler panics, the error message contains "handler panicked: " prefix:

// Task handler panic → TaskError::ExecutionFailed
// Message: "handler panicked: task handler crashed!"

// Command handler panic → CommandError::ExecutionFailed
// Message: "handler panicked: command handler crashed!"

// Service lifecycle panic → ServiceError::*Failed
// Message: "service panicked: service init crashed!"

// Plugin lifecycle panic → PluginError::*Failed
// Message: "plugin panicked: plugin init crashed!"

docs.title: Detecting Panic-Origin Errors
docs.text:
match engine.start_task(task_id) {
    Err(TaskError::ExecutionFailed { reason, .. }) if reason.contains("handler panicked") => {
        eprintln!("Handler panicked: {}", reason);
        // Can retry, log, or escalate
    },
    Err(TaskError::ExecutionFailed { reason, .. }) => {
        eprintln!("Handler failed: {}", reason);
    },
    Ok(result) => { /* ... */ },
    Err(e) => eprintln!("{}", e),
}

docs.text: Error Type Owned By Subsystem EngineError App Engine Top-level CommandError Commands Command execution TaskError Tasks Task execution ResourceError Resources Resource operations ServiceError Services Service lifecycle PluginError Plugins Plugin lifecycle SchedulingError Scheduling Job operations HistoryError History Undo/redo/replay ConfigurationError Configuration Config validation PersistenceError Persistence Storage backend SerializationError Serialization Serializer PluginSecurityError Plugins Permission enforcement ContextError Context Context creation StateError State State transitions CommunicationError Events/Signals Handler/subscription AsyncError Concurrency Async runtime (feature)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This guide takes you from zero to a working App Engine in 5 minutes. By the end, you'll have: - Created an AppEngine - Registered and executed a command - Created and executed a task - Published and subscribed to events - Loaded a resource - Done undo/redo - Shut down cleanly

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Engine
docs.text:
use app_shell::app_engine::{AppEngine, Bootstrap, Lifecycle};

let mut engine: AppEngine = Bootstrap::create().expect("bootstrap failed");

That's it. All subsystems are wired and ready.

docs.title: Step 2: Register a Command
docs.text:
Define a handler, register it:

use app_shell::app_engine::*;
use std::any::Any;

// Your domain input type
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct GreetInput {
    name: String,
}

// Your command handler
struct GreetCommand;

impl CommandHandler for GreetCommand {
    fn execute(
        &self,
        input: &CommandInput,
        _context: &CommandContext,
        _engine: &EngineRef,
    ) -> Result<CommandResult, CommandError> {
        let input: &GreetInput = input.get::<GreetInput>()
            .ok_or_else(|| CommandError::InvalidArguments("expected GreetInput".to_string()))?;

        Ok(CommandResult::success_with(format!("Hello, {}!", input.name)))
    }
}

// Register
engine.command_executor_mut().register(
    CommandDefinition::new("app.greet", "Greet", "Greet someone by name"),
    Box::new(GreetCommand),
)?;

docs.title: Step 3: Execute the Command
docs.text:
// Start the engine
engine.initialize()?;
engine.start()?;

// Create and execute the command
let cmd = Command::new(
    "app.greet",
    CommandContext::new(ExecutionId::new()),
    CommandInput::new(GreetInput { name: "World".to_string() }),
);

let result = engine.execute_command(&cmd)?;

assert!(result.is_success());
assert_eq!(result.output::<String>(), Some(&"Hello, World!".to_string()));

docs.title: Step 4: Register and Execute a Task
docs.text:
For longer operations with lifecycle:

// Your task handler
struct CountTask;

impl TaskHandler for CountTask {
    fn execute(
        &self,
        _input: &TaskInput,
        ctx: &TaskContext,
        _engine: &EngineRef,
    ) -> Result<TaskResult, TaskError> {
        // Check cancellation (Phase 14)
        if ctx.is_cancelled() {
            return Ok(TaskResult::cancelled());
        }

        // Report progress (Phase 14 — emits signal)
        ctx.output().progress(0.5);

        // Do work
        let count = 42;

        ctx.output().progress(1.0);

        Ok(TaskResult::completed_with(count))
    }
}

// Register
engine.task_manager_mut().register(
    TaskDefinition::new("app.count", "Count", "Count to 42")
        .with_cancel_support(),
    Box::new(CountTask),
)?;

// Create and execute
let task_id = engine.task_manager_mut().create(
    "app.count",
    TaskContext::new(ExecutionId::new()),
    TaskInput::empty(),
)?;

let result = engine.start_task(task_id)?;
assert!(result.is_completed());
assert_eq!(result.output::<i32>(), Some(&42));

docs.title: Step 5: Publish and Subscribe to Events
docs.text:
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

let received = Arc::new(Mutex::new(false));
let r = received.clone();

// Subscribe BEFORE publishing
engine.event_bus_mut().subscribe(
    "task.completed",
    event_handler(move |_event: &Event| {
        *r.lock().unwrap() = true;
    }),
);

// Publish (from a handler or directly)
engine.event_bus().publish(
    &Event::new("task.completed").with_source("QuickStart")
);

assert!(*received.lock().unwrap());

docs.title: Closure Wrapper for Events
docs.text:
If you want to use closures (not just EventHandler impl):

struct ClosureEventHandler<F: Fn(&Event) + Send + Sync + 'static> { f: F }
impl<F: Fn(&Event) + Send + Sync + 'static> EventHandler for ClosureEventHandler<F> {
    fn handle(&self, event: &Event) { (self.f)(event); }
}
fn event_handler<F: Fn(&Event) + Send + Sync + 'static>(f: F) -> Box<dyn EventHandler> {
    Box::new(ClosureEventHandler { f })
}

// Usage:
engine.event_bus_mut().subscribe("my.event", event_handler(|event| {
    println!("Got: {}", event.event_type());
}));

docs.title: Step 6: Load a Resource
docs.text:
// Define a resource loader
struct TextLoader;
impl ResourceLoader for TextLoader {
    fn resource_type(&self) -> &str { "text" }
    fn load(&self, source: &str) -> Result<Box<dyn Any + Send>, ResourceError> {
        Ok(Box::new(format!("content:{}", source)))
    }
}

// Register the loader
engine.resource_manager().register_loader(Box::new(TextLoader));

// Load (RAII handle auto-releases on drop — Phase 25)
let handle = engine.resource_manager().load("text", "file:///welcome.txt")?;

// Access the data
let data = engine.resource_manager()
    .with_resource(handle.resource_id(), |r| {
        r.data::<String>().map(|s| s.clone())
    })
    .flatten();

assert_eq!(data.as_deref(), Some("content:file:///welcome.txt"));
// Handle drops here → ref count = 0, resource stays in cache

docs.title: Step 7: Undo / Redo
docs.text:
// Record a history entry
engine.history_store().append(
    HistoryEntry::new("object.create")
        .undoable()
        .with_data("rect_1".to_string())
        .with_source("QuickStart")
);

engine.history_store().append(
    HistoryEntry::new("object.move")
        .undoable()
        .with_data("moved".to_string())
        .with_inverse("unmoved".to_string())
);

assert_eq!(engine.history_store().active_count(), 2);

// Undo
let undo_result = engine.history_store().undo();
assert_eq!(undo_result.count(), 1);
assert_eq!(engine.history_store().position(), 1);

// Redo
let redo_result = engine.history_store().redo();
assert_eq!(redo_result.count(), 1);
assert_eq!(engine.history_store().position(), 2);

docs.title: Step 8: Shut Down Cleanly
docs.text:
// Stop — cancels all running tasks (Phase 26)
engine.stop()?;

// Dispose — unloads all non-in-use resources (Phase 26)
engine.dispose()?;

assert_eq!(engine.state(), RuntimeState::Disposed);

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
use app_shell::app_engine::*;
use std::any::Any;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

// --- Stubs ---

struct GreetCommand;

impl CommandHandler for GreetCommand {
    fn execute(&self, input: &CommandInput, _: &CommandContext, _: &EngineRef) -> Result<CommandResult, CommandError> {
        let name: &String = input.get::<String>()
            .ok_or_else(|| CommandError::InvalidArguments("expected name".to_string()))?;
        Ok(CommandResult::success_with(format!("Hello, {}!", name)))
    }
}

struct TextLoader;
impl ResourceLoader for TextLoader {
    fn resource_type(&self) -> &str { "text" }
    fn load(&self, source: &str) -> Result<Box<dyn Any + Send>, ResourceError> {
        Ok(Box::new(format!("content:{}", source)))
    }
}

// --- Closure wrapper for events ---

struct ClosureEventHandler<F: Fn(&Event) + Send + Sync + 'static> { f: F }
impl<F: Fn(&Event) + Send + Sync + 'static> EventHandler for ClosureEventHandler<F> {
    fn handle(&self, event: &Event) { (self.f)(event); }
}
fn event_handler<F: Fn(&Event) + Send + Sync + 'static>(f: F) -> Box<dyn EventHandler> {
    Box::new(ClosureEventHandler { f })
}

// --- Main ---

fn main() {
    // 1. Create the engine
    let mut engine: AppEngine = Bootstrap::create().expect("bootstrap failed");

    // 2. Register a command
    engine.command_executor_mut().register(
        CommandDefinition::new("app.greet", "Greet", "Greet someone"),
        Box::new(GreetCommand),
    ).unwrap();

    // 3. Register a resource loader
    engine.resource_manager().register_loader(Box::new(TextLoader));

    // 4. Subscribe to events
    let received = Arc::new(Mutex::new(false));
    let r = received.clone();
    engine.event_bus_mut().subscribe(
        "greet.done",
        event_handler(move |_event: &Event| { *r.lock().unwrap() = true; }),
    );

    // 5. Start the engine
    engine.initialize().unwrap();
    engine.start().unwrap();

    // 6. Execute a command
    let cmd = Command::new(
        "app.greet",
        CommandContext::new(ExecutionId::new()),
        CommandInput::new("World".to_string()),
    );
    let result = engine.execute_command(&cmd).unwrap();
    println!("{}", result.output::<String>().unwrap());

    // 7. Publish an event
    engine.event_bus().publish(&Event::new("greet.done").with_source("main"));
    assert!(*received.lock().unwrap());

    // 8. Load a resource (RAII handle auto-releases on drop)
    let handle = engine.resource_manager()
        .load("text", "file:///welcome.txt").unwrap();
    let data = engine.resource_manager()
        .with_resource(handle.resource_id(), |r| r.data::<String>().map(|s| s.clone()))
        .flatten();
    println!("Loaded: {}", data.unwrap());

    // 9. Undo/redo
    engine.history_store().append(
        HistoryEntry::new("greet").undoable().with_source("main"),
    );
    engine.history_store().undo();
    engine.history_store().redo();

    // 10. Shut down (cancels tasks, unloads resources)
    engine.stop().unwrap();
    engine.dispose().unwrap();

    println!("Done! State: {:?}", engine.state());
}

Output: 

Hello, World!
Loaded: content:file:///welcome.txt
Done! State: Disposed

docs.title: What Domain Foundation Is
docs.text:
The Domain Foundation is a reusable domain capability library. It provides headless models for common domain organization patterns — 2D/3D spatial editing, timelines, layer hierarchies, node graphs, tables, text editing — plus a relation system for property propagation and optional utilities for filtering, tagging, querying, and more.

It sits between the generic App Engine (runtime infrastructure) and application-specific Domain Engines (domain meaning). The foundation defines how objects are organized and how changes propagate; it never defines what the objects mean.

flowchart TD
    subgraph DF[DOMAIN FOUNDATION]
        direction TB
        subgraph ENV[Environments]
            C2D[Canvas2D]
            TLM[Timeline]
            LYR[Layers]
            NG[NodeGraph]
            V3D[Viewport3D]
            TBL[Table]
            TXT[TextEditor]
        end
        subgraph REL[Relations]
            DEF[Definitions]
            EVAL[Evaluation]
            PROP[Propagation]
        end
        subgraph UTIL[Utilities]
            FLT[Filtering]
            QRY[Querying]
            TAG[Tagging]
            SRT[Sorting]
            GRP[Grouping]
            VAL[Validation]
            BTCH[Batch]
        end
    end
    DF -->|composes| DE[DOMAIN ENGINE<br/>(app meaning)]
    DE -->|integration| API[API / MCP / UI]

Zero external dependencies by default. Optional serde for serialization.

docs.title: Environments
docs.text: Environment Purpose Canvas2D Arbitrary 2D spatial organization with objects, transforms, z-ordering, and spatial queries. Timeline Temporal organization with tracks, clips, keyframes, interpolation modes, and overlap constraints. Layers Hierarchical organization with parent-child relationships, visibility inheritance, and reparenting. NodeGraph Graph connectivity with ports, edges, type matching, connection limits, and topological sort. Composes Canvas2D for spatial placement. Viewport3D 3D spatial organization with Euler angles, parent-child transform hierarchy, and spatial queries. Table Tabular data with rows, columns, cells, merged cells, ordering, and swap operations. TextEditor Headless text editing with Unicode scalar value positions, ranges, search/replace, and line/column mapping.

docs.title: Relations
docs.text: Feature Purpose Definitions Declarative relation metadata: endpoints, trigger, propagation mode, priority. Evaluation Apply developer-supplied effect closures when source properties change. Propagation Direct or cascading propagation with cycle protection and max depth. Batch Accumulate multiple property changes and propagate them together. Value Source/Sink Traits for bridging environment state to the relation evaluation engine.

docs.title: Utilities
docs.text: Utility Purpose Filtering Composable predicates (AND/OR/NOT) over any data type. Querying Named, reusable queries built on filtering. Tagging Tags and tag sets with deterministic iteration order (BTreeSet). Sorting Criteria-based ordering, in-place or non-mutating. Grouping Group by key, with deterministic sorted output. Validation Rules and results, multi-rule validation, collect all failures. Batch Multi-object operations via trait or closure.

docs.title: What Domain Foundation Does NOT Provide
docs.text:
Concern Who owns it Application meaning (what "export project" means) Domain Engine Domain state (which document is open, what's selected) Domain Engine UI (rendering, widgets, input handling, windows) UI Layer API/MCP (HTTP endpoints, AI agent contracts) Integration Layer Execution infrastructure (commands, tasks, scheduling) App Engine Persistence (file I/O, database) App Engine / External Rendering (GPU, OpenGL, Vulkan, Wayland) UI Layer Syntax highlighting Domain Engine (if needed) Formula evaluation Domain Engine (via Relations) Graph evaluation/dataflow Domain Engine (depends on port types)

The Domain Foundation is deliberately semantic-agnostic. It knows that a Canvas has Objects with Transforms, but it does not know whether those objects are rectangles, images, or text.

docs.title: No Universal Abstractions
docs.text:
The Domain Foundation deliberately does not introduce:

  • A universal Environment trait
  • An OrderedEnvironment base for Timeline, Layers, Table
  • A Geometry Foundation or Selection Foundation
  • A Graph Foundation or Ordering Foundation

Each environment owns its own types, errors, and operations. This is a deliberate design choice: composition over artificial generalization.

flowchart TD
    ENV[Environment<br/>(category, not a trait)]
    ENV --> C2D[Canvas2D<br/>objects, transforms, z-order]
    ENV --> TLM[Timeline<br/>tracks, clips, keyframes]
    ENV --> LYR[Layers<br/>hierarchy, visibility]
    ENV --> NG[NodeGraph<br/>nodes, ports, edges]
    ENV --> V3D[Viewport3D<br/>3D transforms, hierarchy]
    ENV --> TBL[Table<br/>rows, columns, cells]
    ENV --> TXT[TextEditor<br/>document, positions, ranges]

A concept should become reusable only when it has a real, meaningful boundary — not because two environments look superficially similar in their UI representation.

docs.title: App Engine vs Domain Foundation vs Domain Engine
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph DE[Domain Engine]
        EP[ExportProject]
        CC[CreateCard]
        RS[RenderScene]
    end
    subgraph DF[Domain Foundation]
        ENV[Environments]
        REL[Relations]
        UTI[Utilities]
    end
    subgraph AE[App Engine]
        TM[TaskManager]
        SCH[Scheduler]
        EB[EventBus]
        RES[Resources]
        HIST[History]
    end
    DE -->|composes| DF
    DF -->|uses contracts| AE
Layer Responsibility Knows about Domain Engine What the application does (domain objects, rules, operations) Foundation + App Engine Domain Foundation How objects are organized and how changes propagate App Engine (history, events) App Engine How work is managed, scheduled, communicated Nothing above it

Dependency direction: Domain Engine → Domain Foundation → App Engine (never the reverse).

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: Feature Domain Foundation bevy_ecs iced tauri 2D Canvas ✅ headless ❌ ❌ ❌ Timeline ✅ headless ❌ ❌ ❌ Layers ✅ hierarchy + inheritance ❌ ❌ ❌ NodeGraph ✅ + Canvas2D composition ❌ ❌ ❌ Viewport3D ✅ headless ❌ ❌ ❌ Table ✅ + merged cells ❌ ❌ ❌ TextEditor ✅ Unicode-aware ❌ ❌ ❌ Relations ✅ priority + batch + cascading ❌ ❌ ❌ Filtering ✅ composable AND/OR/NOT ❌ ❌ ❌ Undoable operations ✅ all operations ❌ ❌ ❌ Thread-safe ✅ Send + Sync ✅ ❌ ❌ Headless ✅ no UI ✅ ❌ ❌ Serde support ✅ optional feature ❌ ❌ ❌ Dependencies zero by default many many many

docs.title: Minimal Example
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_engine::DomainEngine;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::*;

let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();

// Create a canvas object
let id = engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create {
    transform: Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(100.0, 200.0)),
}).unwrap();

// Move it
engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Move {
    id,
    translation: Vec2::new(50.0, 50.0),
}).unwrap();

// Undo — restores the original position
engine.undo().unwrap();
assert_eq!(
    engine.canvas().get(id).unwrap().transform.translation,
    Vec2::new(100.0, 200.0),
);

No UI, no rendering, no input handling — just the headless domain model with undo/redo.

docs.title: Core Vocabulary
docs.text: Term Definition Environment A headless domain model for a particular kind of organization (Canvas2D, Timeline, etc.). No shared base trait. Operation A value-type enum describing a single environment-level change. Carries undo data in its outcome. Outcome The result of applying an operation. Contains enough state to construct the inverse. Relation A declarative description of how a change in one property affects another. RelationDefinition Metadata: source/target endpoints, trigger, propagation mode, priority, effect closure. PropagationMode Direct (stop after one hop) or Cascading (re-evaluate transitively). PropertyValueSource Trait for bridging Domain Engine state to the relation evaluation engine. Utility An optional capability (filtering, tagging, etc.) that operates over generic types. DomainEngine The composition root that wraps environments with App Engine history, events, and signals. Compound operation A cross-environment undoable unit using transactions. SignalBus Real-time notification channel. DomainEngine emits signals on every operation.

docs.title: Architecture at a Glance
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    APP[Application]
    APP --> DE[Domain Engine — application meaning]
    APP --> DF[Domain Foundation — reusable domain models]
    APP --> AE[App Engine — runtime infrastructure]
    APP --> UI[UI / API / MCP — external access]

    DE --> DF
    DF --> AE

The Domain Foundation is the middle layer — it provides reusable domain models that Domain Engines compose, and it uses the App Engine's history, events, and signals for execution infrastructure.

docs.title: Key Properties
docs.text: Property Status Dependency-free ✅ Zero external crates by default Optional serde ✅ serde feature for serialization Thread-safe ✅ All environments are Send + Sync Headless ✅ No UI, rendering, or input handling Composable ✅ Environments compose concretely (NodeGraph + Canvas2D) Optional utilities ✅ Utilities are not mandatory dependencies Undoable operations ✅ Every operation carries undo data Unicode-aware ✅ TextEditor uses Unicode scalar value positions Priority-sorted relations ✅ Higher priority relations fire first Cycle-safe ✅ Propagator breaks cycles; Layer/Viewport3D reject cyclic parents Testable ✅ 414 tests + proptest + benchmarks

docs.title: Layered Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    UI[UI / API / MCP / CLI] --> DE[Domain Engine]
    DE --> DF[Domain Foundation]
    DF --> AE[App Engine]

Each layer knows only the layer below it.

docs.title: Dependency Direction
docs.text:
Domain Engine  ──→  Domain Foundation  ──→  App Engine  ──→  (nothing)
App Engine     ✗→   Domain Foundation
Domain Engine  ✗→   App Engine (directly)
App Engine     ✗→   UI / API / MCP

The App Engine never imports domain types. The Domain Foundation never imports UI types. The Domain Engine never imports App Engine internals — it uses only the public contracts (HistoryStore, EventBus, SignalBus, TransactionManager).

docs.title: Three Categories
docs.text:
The Domain Foundation is organised into three independent categories:

flowchart LR
    subgraph DF[DOMAIN FOUNDATION]
        ENV[Environments]
        REL[Relations]
        UTIL[Utilities]
    end
Category Question it answers Depends on Environments How are these objects organized/edited here? App Engine (history, events) Relations How does a change in one thing affect another? Nothing (standalone) Utilities What optional reusable capability do I want? Nothing (generic)

A Domain Engine composes the categories it needs. A simple text editor might use only TextEditor + Relations. A vector editor might use Canvas2D + Layers + Relations + Filtering. The categories are independently meaningful.

docs.title: No Universal Abstractions
docs.text: The most important design principle in the Domain Foundation: do not create abstractions based on superficial similarity.

docs.title: What we don't do
docs.text: Abstraction Why not Environment trait Environments have nothing in common except the operation pattern (which is a convention, not a trait). OrderedEnvironment base Timeline, Layers, and Table all involve "ordering," but their ordering semantics are completely different. SpatialEnvironment base Canvas2D and Viewport3D both have "transforms," but 2D and 3D transforms are different types. Geometry Foundation Geometry is rendering-adjacent and application-specific. Selection Foundation Selection is a UI concern.

docs.title: What we do instead
docs.text:
Each environment owns its own types:

flowchart TD
    ENV[Environment<br/>(category, not a trait)]
    ENV --> C2D[Canvas2D<br/>Canvas, Object, ObjectId, Transform, Vec2<br/>CanvasError, CanvasOperation, CanvasOutcome]
    ENV --> TLM[Timeline<br/>Timeline, Track, Clip, Keyframe, Time, Duration<br/>TimelineError, TimelineOperation, TimelineOutcome]
    ENV --> LYR[Layers<br/>Layers, Layer, LayerId<br/>LayersError, LayersOperation, LayersOutcome]
    ENV --> NG[NodeGraph<br/>NodeGraph, Node, Port, Edge<br/>NodeGraphError, NodeGraphOperation, NodeGraphOutcome]
    ENV --> V3D[Viewport3D<br/>Scene, Object3D, Transform3D, Vec3<br/>Viewport3DError, Viewport3DOperation, Viewport3DOutcome]
    ENV --> TBL[Table<br/>Table, Row, Column, CellId, CellValue<br/>TableError, TableOperation, TableOutcome]
    ENV --> TXT[TextEditor<br/>Document, Position, Range<br/>TextEditorError, TextEditorOperation, TextEditorOutcome]

A concept should become reusable only when it has a real, meaningful boundary:

Actual shared semantics → real reuse → extract abstraction
Theoretical similarity → no reuse → don't abstract

docs.title: Composition Between Environments
docs.text:
Environments may compose other environments when their semantics genuinely require it. The only composition in the foundation is:

flowchart LR
    NG[NodeGraph] -->|owns| C2D[Canvas]
    NG -->|owns| GRAPH[Graph state<br/>nodes, ports, edges]

    MOVE[move_node] -->|spatial only| C2D
    CONNECT[connect] -->|graph only| GRAPH

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
NodeGraph owns a Canvas instance. When creating a node, it creates a canvas object for spatial placement. When moving a node, it moves the canvas object. When connecting ports, it creates edges — this has nothing to do with the canvas.

Graph connectivity and spatial state are separate concerns. Moving a node doesn't affect edges; connecting ports doesn't affect positions. This is the composition principle in action.

// NodeGraph owns a Canvas internally
pub struct NodeGraph {
    nodes: HashMap<NodeId, Node>,
    ports: HashMap<PortId, Port>,
    edges: HashMap<EdgeId, Edge>,
    canvas: Canvas,              // ← composition
    next_node_id: u64,
    // ...
}

// Each Node links to its spatial representation
pub struct Node {
    pub id: NodeId,
    pub name: String,
    pub canvas_object: Option<ObjectId>,  // ← link to Canvas2D
    // ...
}

docs.title: Operation Pattern
docs.text:
Every environment follows the same operation convention (but not a shared trait):

flowchart LR
    OP[MyOperation] -->|apply| ENV[MyEnvironment]
    ENV --> OUT[MyOutcome]
    OUT -->|carries undo data| UNDO[undo]
    OUT -->|carries redo data| REDO[redo]
// Operation enum — value-type intent
pub enum CanvasOperation {
    Create { transform: Transform },
    Move { id: ObjectId, translation: Vec2 },
    Remove { id: ObjectId },
    // ...
}

// Outcome enum — result with undo data
pub enum CanvasOutcome {
    Created { id: ObjectId },
    Moved { id: ObjectId, previous: Transform },
    Removed { object: Object },
    // ...
}

// Apply method
impl CanvasOperation {
    pub fn apply(self, canvas: &mut Canvas) -> Result<CanvasOutcome, CanvasError>;
}

Each outcome carries enough state to construct the inverse:

Outcome Undo action Created { id } Remove the created object Moved { previous } Restore the previous transform Removed { object } Re-insert the removed object (via insert_object) MovedForward { previous_index } canvas.reorder(id, previous_index) Duplicated { new_id } Remove the duplicate

The redo method re-applies the original operation. For Create, it uses insert_object (not create_object) to preserve the original id.

docs.title: Relations Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    DEF[RelationDefinition<br/>source, target, trigger, priority, effect] --> REG[RelationRegistry<br/>priority-sorted]
    REG --> EVAL[EvaluationEngine<br/>mutable value store]
    EVAL --> PROP[Propagator<br/>Direct or Cascading<br/>cycle protection]
    PROP --> OUTCOME[EffectOutcome<br/>Apply, NoChange, Invalidate]

docs.title: Key design decisions
docs.text: Decision Rationale Priority-sorted Higher priority relations fire first when multiple share the same source. Mutable value store Outcomes are applied during evaluation so cascading relations see updated values. Cycle protection Each relation is evaluated at most once per propagation pass. Batch propagation Accumulate changes, propagate deduplicated, or rollback without propagating. Effect closures The foundation calls the closure but never inspects what it does. Meaning stays in the Domain Engine. Value Source/Sink traits Bridge Domain Engine state to the evaluation engine without manual sync.

docs.title: Independence from environments
docs.text: The relation system has no knowledge of any environment's concrete types. All addressing is via opaque PropertyId values (ObjectId + property index). The relation system can relate properties on Canvas2D objects, Timeline clips, or any other domain object — it doesn't know or care.

docs.title: Utilities Architecture
docs.text:
Utilities are orthogonal to environments and relations:

flowchart TD
    UTIL[Utilities] --> FLT[Filtering]
    UTIL --> TAG[Tagging]
    UTIL --> VAL[Validation]

    FLT --> C2D[Canvas2D]
    FLT --> TLM[Timeline]
    FLT --> TBL[Table]

docs.title: Key rules
docs.text:
1. Utilities operate over generic T — no imports from environments or relations.
  2. Environments do not import utilities — a Canvas2D doesn't know filtering exists.
  3. Utilities are individually usable — a Domain Engine chooses which to compose.
  4. Utilities do not own data meaning — they process data supplied to them.
// Filtering works over ANY type
pub fn filter<'a, T, C: FilterCriteria<T>>(
    items: &'a [T],
    criteria: &C,
) -> Vec<&'a T> {
    items.iter().filter(|item| criteria.matches(item)).collect()
}

// Can filter Canvas2D objects, Timeline clips, Table rows, integers, strings...

docs.title: DomainEngine Architecture
docs.text:
The DomainEngine is the composition root that wraps all environments with App Engine infrastructure:

flowchart TD
    DE[DomainEngine] --> ENV[7 Environments<br/>Canvas, Timeline, Layers, NodeGraph, Table, Document, Scene]
    DE --> HIST[HistoryStore<br/>undo/redo, transactions]
    DE --> TX[TransactionManager<br/>begin/commit/rollback]
    DE --> EVT[EventBus<br/>publish events]
    DE --> SIG[SignalBus<br/>emit signals]
    DE --> DIRTY[Dirty Tracking<br/>mark_saved, is_dirty]
    DE --> COMP[Compound Operations<br/>cross-environment undo]

docs.title: What the DomainEngine does
docs.text:
1. Executes operations on any environment (execute_canvas, execute_timeline, etc.)
  2. Records history entries with transaction ids for compound undo
  3. Publishes events via EventBus (for logging, history, plugins)
  4. Emits signals via SignalBus (for real-time UI updates)
  5. Tracks dirty state (mark_saved() / is_dirty())
  6. Auto-rolls back on error during a transaction
  7. Supports compound operations (cross-environment undoable units)
  8. Registers command handlers with the App Engine's CommandExecutor

docs.title: What the DomainEngine does NOT do
docs.text:
• Define application-specific object types (that's the Domain Engine's job)
  • Define domain rules (e.g., "width must be positive")
  • Render anything
  • Handle user input

docs.title: Serde Support
docs.text:
All serializable types have conditional serde derives behind a feature flag:

#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(transparent))]  // for newtypes
pub struct ObjectId(u64);

Enable with:

[dependencies]
app_shell = { path = "...", features = ["serde"] }

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text: Limitation Reason RelationDefinition::effect deserializes as no-op Closures can't be serialized. default_effect() returns Arc::new(\|_\| EffectOutcome::NoChange). Table's HashMap<CellId, _> can't serialize to JSON serde_json requires string keys. Would need a custom serializer. Viewport3D::world_transform only composes translations Proper 3D transform composition requires matrix multiplication. HistoryStore can't truncate old entries App Engine's HistoryStore has no truncate_old method. Undo limit checks but can't trim.

docs.title: Environments
docs.text: An Environment is a reusable, headless model for a particular kind of domain organization or editing context. It is not a UI component — it defines the semantic model behind the interactions.

docs.title: Operation Convention
docs.text:
Every environment follows the same value-type operation pattern:

flowchart LR
    OP[MyOperation] -->|apply| ENV[MyEnvironment]
    ENV --> OUT[MyOutcome]
    OUT -->|undo data| UNDO[undo]
    OUT -->|redo data| REDO[redo]
// Operation enum — value-type intent
pub enum CanvasOperation {
    Create { transform: Transform },
    Move { id: ObjectId, translation: Vec2 },
    Remove { id: ObjectId },
}

// Outcome enum — result with undo data
pub enum CanvasOutcome {
    Created { id: ObjectId },
    Moved { id: ObjectId, previous: Transform },
    Removed { object: Object },
}

// Apply method
impl CanvasOperation {
    pub fn apply(self, canvas: &mut Canvas) -> Result<CanvasOutcome, CanvasError>;
}

Each outcome carries enough state to construct the inverse:

Outcome Undo action Created { id } Remove the created object Moved { previous } Restore the previous transform Removed { object } Re-insert the removed object MovedForward { previous_index } reorder(id, previous_index) Duplicated { new_id } Remove the duplicate

docs.title: No Shared Base Trait
docs.text:
Environments do not share a common base trait. Each owns its own types, errors, and operations.

Environment (category, not a trait)
   ├── Canvas2D        (Canvas, CanvasError, CanvasOperation, CanvasOutcome)
   ├── Timeline        (Timeline, TimelineError, TimelineOperation, TimelineOutcome)
   ├── Layers          (Layers, LayersError, LayersOperation, LayersOutcome)
   ├── NodeGraph       (NodeGraph, NodeGraphError, NodeGraphOperation, NodeGraphOutcome)
   ├── Viewport3D     (Scene, Viewport3DError, Viewport3DOperation, Viewport3DOutcome)
   ├── Table           (Table, TableError, TableOperation, TableOutcome)
   └── TextEditor     (Document, TextEditorError, TextEditorOperation, TextEditorOutcome)

This is deliberate. Forcing a universal Environment trait would create an abstraction based on superficial similarity, not genuine reuse. See 02-architecture.md for the full rationale.

docs.title: Composition
docs.text:
NodeGraph composes Canvas2D for spatial placement:

flowchart LR
    subgraph NG[NodeGraph]
        GRAPH[Graph state<br/>nodes, ports, edges]
        C2D[Canvas<br/>objects, transforms]
    end

    MOVE[move_node] -->|spatial only| C2D
    CONNECT[connect] -->|graph only| GRAPH

Graph connectivity and spatial state are separate concerns:

  • Moving a node changes spatial state only — edges are untouched.
  • Connecting ports changes graph state only — positions are untouched.
  • Removing a node cascades to its ports, connected edges, and the canvas object.

Each Node stores a canvas_object: Option<ObjectId> linking its graph identity to its spatial representation.

docs.title: Traits on Environments
docs.text:
All environments derive:

Trait Purpose Debug Standard debug output Clone Full deep clone PartialEq Value-based equality (for tests) Default Empty construction IntoIterator for item in &env syntax

Additionally:

Environment Extra traits Canvas2D Extend<Object> (batch insert) TextEditor Document: IntoIterator<Item = char> TagSet IntoIterator<Item = &Tag> (BTreeSet, sorted)

All serializable types also have conditional serde::Serialize / serde::Deserialize derives behind the serde feature flag.

docs.title: Clear Method
docs.text:
Every environment has a clear() method that removes all contents while preserving the id counter (so previously-issued ids remain unique):

let mut canvas = Canvas::new();
let id = canvas.create_object(Transform::identity());
canvas.clear();

let new_id = canvas.create_object(Transform::identity());
assert_ne!(id, new_id);  // Ids don't collide

docs.title: Headless by Construction
docs.text:
No environment imports or depends on:

  • Rendering engines (GPU, OpenGL, Vulkan)
  • UI frameworks (Tauri, iced, egui)
  • Input handling (mouse, keyboard, touch)
  • Window management
  • Animation systems
  • Camera or viewport logic

The UI owns all of these. The environment owns the semantic model behind the interactions.

docs.title: Canvas2D
docs.text: Headless 2D spatial editing model. Provides objects, transforms, z-ordering, and spatial queries without imposing any UI layout, coordinate-system orientation, or rendering.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph C2D[Canvas2D]
        CANVAS[Canvas<br/>objects + draw_order + next_id]
        OBJ[Object<br/>id + transform]
        TF[Transform<br/>translation + rotation + scale]
        V2[Vec2<br/>x + y]
    end
    C2D -->|operations| OPS[CanvasOperation]
    OPS -->|apply| OUT[CanvasOutcome]
    OUT -->|undo| UNDO[undo]

docs.title: Key Types
docs.text: Type Fields Purpose Canvas objects: HashMap<ObjectId, Object>, draw_order: Vec<ObjectId>, next_id: u64 Container owning all objects Object id: ObjectId, transform: Transform Spatial entity ObjectId u64 (opaque) Stable, opaque identifier Transform translation: Vec2, rotation: f64, scale: Vec2 Decomposed 2D transform Vec2 x: f64, y: f64 2D vector CanvasError ObjectNotFound { id } Error type CanvasOperation 11 variants Value-type operation intent CanvasOutcome 11 variants Result with undo data

docs.title: Object management
docs.text: Method Returns Description create_object(transform) ObjectId Create a new object, append to draw order insert_object(object) () Restore an object with its original id (for undo) remove_object(id) Result<Object, CanvasError> Remove an object from storage and draw order duplicate_object(id, offset) Result<ObjectId, CanvasError> Create a copy at an offset clear() () Remove all objects (id counter preserved)

docs.text: Method Returns Description get(id) Option<&Object> Look up by id get_mut(id) Option<&mut Object> Mutable lookup contains(id) bool Existence check len() usize Object count is_empty() bool Whether canvas is empty iter() impl Iterator<Item = &Object> Iterate (unordered) iter_ordered() impl Iterator<Item = &Object> Iterate in draw order (back to front) draw_order() &[ObjectId] Z-order slice (back to front) objects_in_bounds(min, max) Vec<&Object> Spatial query by translation bounds

docs.title: Transform mutations
docs.text: Method Returns Description set_transform(id, transform) Result<Transform, CanvasError> Replace whole transform, returns previous set_translation(id, translation) Result<Transform, CanvasError> Set translation only, preserve rotation/scale

docs.title: Z-ordering
docs.text: Method Returns Description move_to_front(id) Result<(), CanvasError> Move to topmost (end of draw order) move_to_back(id) Result<(), CanvasError> Move to bottommost (start of draw order) move_forward(id) Result<(), CanvasError> Swap with next (toward front) move_backward(id) Result<(), CanvasError> Swap with previous (toward back) reorder(id, new_index) Result<(), CanvasError> Move to specific draw-order index

docs.title: Z-Ordering
docs.text:
The canvas maintains a draw_order: Vec<ObjectId> separate from the HashMap storage. This allows O(1) lookup by id while preserving a defined render order.

draw_order: [ObjectId(0), ObjectId(2), ObjectId(1)]
                 ↑ back              ↑ front
              rendered first     rendered last
  • create_object appends to the front (topmost).
  • remove_object removes from both storage and draw order.
  • insert_object (for undo) restores to draw order if not already present.
  • move_to_front / move_to_back / move_forward / move_backward / reorder manipulate the draw order.

docs.title: Vec2 Math
docs.text:
Method Returns Description dot(other) f64 Dot product length() f64 Euclidean magnitude normalize() Vec2 Unit vector (zero if length is zero) lerp(other, t) Vec2 Linear interpolation (t=0 = self, t=1 = other) rotate(angle) Vec2 Rotate by radians (counter-clockwise) angle_to(other) f64 Signed angle to other (radians)

Operators: Add, Sub, Mul<f64>, AddAssign, SubAssign, MulAssign.

docs.title: Transform
docs.text:
Method Description identity() No translation, no rotation, unit scale from_translation(v) Translation only from_rotation(r) Rotation only (radians) from_scale(v) Scale only with_translation(v) Builder: set translation with_rotation(r) Builder: set rotation with_scale(v) Builder: set scale

The foundation does not perform matrix composition or apply_to_point. Domain Engines that need world transforms from local transforms implement composition externally.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Operation Outcome Undo Create { transform } Created { id } Remove the created object Move { id, translation } Moved { id, previous } Restore previous transform Transform { id, transform } Transformed { id, previous } Restore previous transform Remove { id } Removed { object } Re-insert via insert_object MoveToFront { id } MovedToFront { id, previous_index } reorder(id, previous_index) MoveToBack { id } MovedToBack { id, previous_index } reorder(id, previous_index) MoveForward { id } MovedForward { id, previous_index } reorder(id, previous_index) MoveBackward { id } MovedBackward { id, previous_index } reorder(id, previous_index) Reorder { id, new_index } Reordered { id, previous_index } reorder(id, previous_index) Duplicate { id, offset } Duplicated { source, new_id } Remove new_id Clear Cleared { count } (limited — no stored objects to restore)

docs.title: IntoIterator and Extend
docs.text:
// Iterate over objects
for obj in &canvas {
    println!("{:?}", obj.transform.translation);
}

// Batch insert
let objects = vec![obj1, obj2, obj3];
canvas.extend(objects);

docs.title: Spatial Queries
docs.text:
// Find all objects whose translation falls within bounds
let found = canvas.objects_in_bounds(
    Vec2::new(0.0, 0.0),
    Vec2::new(100.0, 100.0),
);
assert_eq!(found.len(), 3);

Bounds are inclusive min, exclusive max on each axis. The query is O(n) — a spatial index (quadtree/BVH) would be needed for large-scale performance.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::*;

let mut canvas = Canvas::new();

// Create objects
let a = canvas.create_object(Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(0.0, 0.0)));
let b = canvas.create_object(Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(100.0, 0.0)));
let c = canvas.create_object(Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(200.0, 0.0)));

// Z-ordering: c is frontmost
assert_eq!(canvas.draw_order(), &[a, b, c]);

// Move b to front
canvas.move_to_front(b).unwrap();
assert_eq!(canvas.draw_order(), &[a, c, b]);

// Spatial query: objects with x in [0, 150)
let right = canvas.objects_in_bounds(
    Vec2::new(0.0, 0.0),
    Vec2::new(150.0, 100.0),
);
assert_eq!(right.len(), 2); // a and c

// Duplicate a
let dup = canvas.duplicate_object(a, Vec2::new(10.0, 10.0)).unwrap();
assert_eq!(canvas.len(), 4);
assert_ne!(dup, a);

// Vec2 math
let v = Vec2::new(3.0, 4.0);
assert_eq!(v.length(), 5.0);
assert!((v.normalize().length() - 1.0).abs() < 1e-10);

docs.text: Concern Owner Application-specific data (color, shape type, name) Domain Engine Rendering (drawing, hit testing, selection) UI Layer Parent-child spatial transforms (group transforms) Domain Engine (via Layers) Matrix composition Domain Engine Bounding box computation per object Domain Engine

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text: Headless temporal editing model. Provides tracks, clips, keyframes, and time-based operations without imposing any playback engine, media decoding, or UI.

docs.title: Overview

flowchart TD

        TL[Timeline<br/>tracks + track_order + id counters]
        TR[Track<br/>id + clips (sorted)]
        CL[Clip<br/>id + start + duration + keyframes]
        KF[Keyframe<br/>id + time + value + interpolation]
    end

    OPS -->|apply| OUT[TimelineOutcome]

docs.text:

docs.title: Overlap Constraints
docs.text:
Clips within the same track must not overlap. The timeline enforces this on insert and move:

Track A: [Clip 1: 0-5s] [Clip 2: 5-10s] [Clip 3: 10-15s]
                                          ↑ Clip 4 cannot start at 8s — overlaps Clip 3
  • insert_clip checks overlap against all existing clips on the track.
  • move_clip temporarily removes the clip, checks overlap at the new position, re-inserts if safe, or restores the original position and returns ClipOverlap error.

Clips on different tracks are independent and may overlap freely.

docs.title: Clip Split
docs.text:
split_clip(id, at_time) divides a clip into two at the specified time:

Before:  [Clip: 0-10s]
                  split at 4s
After:   [Left: 0-4s] [Right: 4-10s]

The left clip keeps the original ClipId; the right clip gets a new id. Keyframes are not moved — they stay on whichever clip contains their time.

docs.title: Track Ordering
docs.text:
Tracks have a defined order via track_order: Vec<TrackId>. move_track(id, new_index) reorders tracks. This is separate from clip ordering (which is by start time within each track).

let mut timeline = Timeline::new();
let a = timeline.create_track();
let b = timeline.create_track();
let c = timeline.create_track();

assert_eq!(timeline.track_ids(), &[a, b, c]);

timeline.move_track(c, 0).unwrap();
assert_eq!(timeline.track_ids(), &[c, a, b]);

docs.title: Keyframe Interpolation
docs.text:
let kf = Keyframe::new(id, Time::new(2.0), KeyframeValue::Float(1.0))
    .with_interpolation(Interpolation::Smooth);
Mode Behavior Step Hold the value until the next keyframe (no blending) Linear Linear interpolation between this keyframe and the next Smooth Cubic ease-in/ease-out

The foundation stores the interpolation mode but does not perform interpolation. A Domain Engine or UI reads the mode and computes interpolated values as needed.

docs.text: Operation Outcome Undo CreateTrack TrackCreated { id } Remove the track RemoveTrack { id } TrackRemoved { track } Re-insert the track InsertClip { track_id, start, duration } ClipInserted { id } Remove the clip RemoveClip { id } ClipRemoved { clip } Re-insert the clip MoveClip { id, new_start } ClipMoved { id, previous_start } Move back to previous start AddKeyframe { clip_id, time, value } KeyframeAdded { id, clip_id } Remove the keyframe RemoveKeyframe { clip_id, kf_id } KeyframeRemoved { keyframe, clip_id } Re-add the keyframe TrimClip { id, new_duration } ClipTrimmed { id, previous_duration } Restore previous duration SplitClip { id, at_time } ClipSplit { original_id, new_id } Remove new clip, restore original duration ClearTimeline TimelineCleared (limited — no stored tracks to restore) SetKeyframeValue { clip_id, kf_id, value } KeyframeValueChanged { previous_value } Restore previous value

docs.title: Clips At Time
docs.text:
Query all clips active at a given time across all tracks:

let active = timeline.clips_at(Time::new(7.0));
for clip in &active {
    println!("Active: {} - {}", clip.start, clip.end());
}

A clip is active at time if clip.start <= time < clip.start + clip.duration.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: Headless hierarchy model. Provides layers with parent-child relationships, visibility inheritance, lock inheritance, and reparenting with cycle detection — without imposing compositing properties (opacity, blend mode) or rendering.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph LYR[Layers]
        LS[Layers<br/>layers + roots + next_id]
        L[Layer<br/>id + name + visible + locked + parent + children]
    end
    LYR -->|operations| OPS[LayersOperation]
    OPS -->|apply| OUT[LayersOutcome]

docs.title: Key Types
docs.text: Type Fields Purpose Layers layers: HashMap<LayerId, Layer>, roots: Vec<LayerId>, next_id: u64 Container owning all layers Layer id, name, visible, locked, parent: Option<LayerId>, children: Vec<LayerId> Hierarchy node LayerId u64 (opaque) Stable, opaque identifier LayersError LayerNotFound, InvalidSiblingIndex, CycleDetected Error type LayersOperation 10 variants Value-type operation intent LayersOutcome 10 variants Result with undo data

docs.text: Method Returns Description set_visibility(id, visible) Result<bool, LayersError> Set visible flag, returns previous set_locked(id, locked) Result<bool, LayersError> Set locked flag, returns previous rename(id, name) Result<String, LayersError> Set name, returns previous

docs.text: Method Returns Description reorder_sibling(id, new_index) Result<usize, LayersError> Move within siblings, returns previous index move_up(id) Result<bool, LayersError> Move forward one position (returns false if at front) move_down(id) Result<bool, LayersError> Move backward one position (returns false if at back)

docs.title: Hierarchy
docs.text: Method Returns Description reparent(id, new_parent) Result<Option<LayerId>, LayersError> Move to different parent (None = root), returns previous parent is_descendant(maybe_descendant, ancestor) bool Check if one layer is a descendant of another descendants(id) Vec<LayerId> All descendants (BFS, not including self) depth() usize Maximum hierarchy depth layer_path(id) Vec<LayerId> Path from root to this layer (root first, leaf last)

docs.title: Inheritance
docs.text: Method Returns Description effective_visibility(id) bool Visible only if self AND all ancestors are visible effective_locked(id) bool Locked if self OR any ancestor is locked

docs.title: Visibility (AND semantics)
docs.text:
A layer is effectively visible only if it AND all its ancestors are visible. Hiding a parent hides all children.

Root (visible=true)
  └── Child (visible=true)
        └── Grandchild (visible=true)

effective_visibility(Grandchild) = true

Set Root.visible = false

effective_visibility(Grandchild) = false  ← inherited
effective_visibility(Child) = false       ← inherited
effective_visibility(Root) = false

docs.title: Locked (OR semantics)
docs.text:
A layer is effectively locked if it OR any ancestor is locked. Locking a parent locks all children.

Root (locked=false)
  └── Child (locked=false)
        └── Grandchild (locked=false)

effective_locked(Grandchild) = false

Set Child.locked = true

effective_locked(Grandchild) = true   ← inherited
effective_locked(Child) = true
effective_locked(Root) = false

docs.title: Reparenting with Cycle Detection
docs.text:
reparent(id, new_parent) moves a layer to a different parent. It rejects:

  1. Self-parenting: id == new_parent
  2. Cycles: new_parent is a descendant of id
let root = layers.create_layer("Root".into());
let child = layers.create_child(root, "Child".into()).unwrap();

// This would create a cycle: root becomes a child of its own child
let err = layers.reparent(root, Some(child)).unwrap_err();
assert!(matches!(err, LayersError::CycleDetected { .. }));

docs.title: Remove Cascade
docs.text:
Removing a layer removes it AND all its descendants:

Before: Root → Child → Grandchild

remove_layer(Root) → returns [Root, Child, Grandchild]

After: (empty)

The returned Vec<Layer> contains all removed layers in BFS order (parent before children). For undo, re-insert them in order via insert_layer().

docs.title: Sibling Ordering
docs.text:
Each parent maintains an ordered children: Vec<LayerId>. Root layers are tracked in roots: Vec<LayerId>.

  • reorder_sibling(id, new_index) — move to a specific position
  • move_up(id) — swap with the previous sibling (toward front)
  • move_down(id) — swap with the next sibling (toward back)

Both move_up and move_down return Ok(false) if already at the boundary.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Operation Outcome Undo CreateLayer { name } LayerCreated { id } Remove the layer CreateChild { parent, name } LayerCreated { id } Remove the layer RemoveLayer { id } LayerRemoved { layers } Re-insert all layers via insert_layer RenameLayer { id, name } LayerRenamed { previous_name } Restore previous name SetVisibility { id, visible } VisibilityChanged { previous_visible } Restore previous SetLocked { id, locked } LockedChanged { previous_locked } Restore previous ReorderSibling { id, new_index } SiblingReordered { previous_index } Restore previous index Reparent { id, new_parent } Reparented { previous_parent } Restore previous parent DuplicateLayer { id } LayerDuplicated { source, new_id } Remove the duplicate Clear Cleared (limited — no stored layers to restore)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::layers::*;

let mut layers = Layers::new();

// Create hierarchy
let root = layers.create_layer("Scene".into());
let child_a = layers.create_child(root, "Background".into()).unwrap();
let child_b = layers.create_child(root, "Foreground".into()).unwrap();
let grandchild = layers.create_child(child_b, "Overlay".into()).unwrap();

assert_eq!(layers.layer(root).unwrap().child_count(), 2);
assert_eq!(layers.layer_path(grandchild), vec![root, child_b, grandchild]);

// Hide the root — all descendants become effectively invisible
layers.set_visibility(root, false).unwrap();
assert!(!layers.effective_visibility(grandchild));

// Lock child_b — grandchild becomes effectively locked
layers.set_visibility(root, true).unwrap();
layers.set_locked(child_b, true).unwrap();
assert!(layers.effective_locked(grandchild));
assert!(!layers.effective_locked(child_a));

// Move child_b to front
layers.move_up(child_b).unwrap();
assert_eq!(layers.layer(root).unwrap().children(), &[child_b, child_a]);

// Duplicate root as a new root
let dup = layers.duplicate_layer(root).unwrap();
assert!(layers.layer(dup).unwrap().is_root());
assert_eq!(layers.layer(dup).unwrap().name, "Scene");

docs.title: What Layers Does NOT Own
docs.text:
Concern Owner Compositing properties (opacity, blend mode, masks) Domain Engine Rendering (draw order, compositing pipeline) UI Layer Layer thumbnails UI Layer Blend modes Domain Engine Layer effects (drop shadow, glow) Domain Engine Drag-and-drop reordering UI Layer

Visibility and locked state are included because they affect whether operations are meaningful (e.g., you shouldn't move objects on a hidden layer). Compositing properties are excluded because they affect how things look, which is a rendering concern.

docs.title: NodeGraph
docs.text: Headless graph editing model with spatial placement composed from Canvas2D. Provides nodes, input/output ports, edges, connection validation, and graph traversal — without any rendering or dataflow evaluation.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph NG[NodeGraph]
        GRAPH[Graph state<br/>nodes + ports + edges]
        C2D[Canvas<br/>spatial placement]
    end

    NG -->|operations| OPS[NodeGraphOperation]
    OPS -->|apply| OUT[NodeGraphOutcome]

docs.title: Composition with Canvas2D
docs.text:
NodeGraph owns a Canvas instance for spatial placement. This is the only cross-environment composition in the foundation:

flowchart LR
    subgraph NG[NodeGraph]
        NODES[Graph connectivity<br/>nodes, ports, edges]
        CANVAS[Canvas2D<br/>objects, transforms]
    end

    CREATE[create_node] -->|creates canvas object| CANVAS
    CREATE -->|creates graph node| NODES
    MOVE[move_node] -->|spatial only| CANVAS
    CONNECT[connect] -->|graph only| NODES
    REMOVE[remove_node] -->|removes from| CANVAS
    REMOVE -->|removes from| NODES

Graph connectivity and spatial state are separate concerns:

  • Moving a node changes spatial state only — edges are untouched.
  • Connecting ports changes graph state only — positions are untouched.
  • Removing a node cascades to its ports, connected edges, and the canvas object.

Each Node stores canvas_object: Option<ObjectId> linking its graph identity to its spatial representation.

docs.title: Key Types
docs.text: Type Fields Purpose NodeGraph nodes, ports, edges, canvas, id counters Container owning graph state + Canvas2D Node id, name, canvas_object: Option<ObjectId>, input_ports, output_ports Graph entity with optional spatial placement Port id, node, direction, name, type_name, max_inputs Connection point on a node Edge id, source: PortId, target: PortId Directed connection from output to input PortDirection Input, Output Direction of data flow NodeId u64 (opaque) Stable node identifier PortId u64 (opaque) Stable port identifier EdgeId u64 (opaque) Stable edge identifier NodeGraphError 12 variants Error type NodeRemovedData node, ports, edges, canvas_object Undo data for node removal PortRemovedData port, edges Undo data for port removal

docs.text: Method Returns Description edges_on_port(port) impl Iterator<Item = &Edge> Edges connected to a port (as source or target) edges_between(src_node, tgt_node) impl Iterator<Item = &Edge> Edges from one node to another is_connected(source, target) bool Whether a direct edge exists input_edge_count(port) usize Number of edges targeting this port

docs.title: Graph traversal
docs.text: Method Returns Description topological_sort() Result<Vec<NodeId>, NodeGraphError> Nodes in dependency order (sources first) has_cycles() bool Whether the graph contains any cycles

docs.title: Connection Validation
docs.text:
connect(source, target) validates the following rules before creating an edge:

Rule Error Description Both ports exist PortNotFound Source and target must be in the registry Source is output SourceNotOutput The source port must have PortDirection::Output Target is input TargetNotInput The target port must have PortDirection::Input Different nodes SameNode Source and target must be on different nodes Type match TypeMismatch source.type_name must equal target.type_name No duplicate DuplicateEdge An edge with the same source + target must not already exist Connection limit MaxInputsExceeded If target.max_inputs > 0, existing connections must be below the limit

Type matching is exact string comparison. The foundation does not support type hierarchies or conversions. A Domain Engine that needs "float → double" compatibility implements it externally.

docs.title: Connection Policy
docs.text:
Each input port has a max_inputs: u32 field:

Value Behavior 0 Unlimited connections (default) 1 Single connection only (fan-in = 1) N Maximum N connections

Set via the builder:

let port = Port::new(id, node, PortDirection::Input, "value".into(), "float".into())
    .with_max_inputs(1);  // Only one edge can target this port

Or mutate directly:

graph.port_mut(port_id).unwrap().max_inputs = 1;

docs.title: Topological Sort
docs.text:
let sorted = graph.topological_sort()?;
// sorted[0] = first node (no dependencies)
// sorted[last] = last node (depends on everything above)

Uses Kahn's algorithm (BFS from zero-in-degree nodes). Returns CycleInGraph error if the graph contains a cycle.

has_cycles() is a convenience that calls topological_sort() and checks for an error.

docs.title: Remove Cascade
docs.text:
Removing a node cascades to:

  1. All its ports (input and output)
  2. All edges connected to any of those ports
  3. The canvas object (spatial representation)
Node A (out_port_1, in_port_1)
  ├── Edge: out_port_1 → Node B.in_port
  └── Edge: Node C.out_port → in_port_1

remove_node(A) → removes: Node A, out_port_1, in_port_1, both edges, canvas object

NodeRemovedData carries all removed items for undo.

docs.text: Operation Outcome Undo CreateNode { name, transform } NodeCreated { id } Remove node + canvas object RemoveNode { id } NodeRemoved(data) Re-insert node, ports, edges, canvas object RenameNode { id, name } NodeRenamed { previous_name } Restore previous name MoveNode { id, translation } NodeMoved { previous_transform } Restore previous transform SetNodeTransform { id, transform } NodeTransformSet { previous_transform } Restore previous transform AddInputPort { node, name, type_name } PortAdded { id } Remove the port AddOutputPort { node, name, type_name } PortAdded { id } Remove the port RemovePort { id } PortRemoved(data) Re-insert port + edges Connect { source, target } Connected { id } Disconnect the edge Disconnect { id } Disconnected { edge } Re-insert the edge RenamePort { id, name } PortRenamed { previous_name } Restore previous name DuplicateNode { id } NodeDuplicated { source, new_id } Remove the duplicate Clear Cleared { node_count } (limited — no stored nodes to restore)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::node_graph::*;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::{Transform, Vec2};

let mut graph = NodeGraph::new();

// Create nodes with spatial placement
let source = graph.create_node("Source".into(), Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(0.0, 0.0)));
let sink = graph.create_node("Sink".into(), Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(200.0, 0.0)));

// Add ports
let out_port = graph.add_output_port(source, "value".into(), "float".into()).unwrap();
let in_port = graph.add_input_port(sink, "value".into(), "float".into()).unwrap();

// Connect (type "float" matches)
let edge_id = graph.connect(out_port, in_port).unwrap();

// Graph has 2 nodes, 2 ports, 1 edge
assert_eq!(graph.node_count(), 2);
assert_eq!(graph.port_count(), 2);
assert_eq!(graph.edge_count(), 1);

// Spatial state: 2 canvas objects
assert_eq!(graph.canvas().len(), 2);

// Move source — spatial only, graph untouched
graph.move_node(source, Vec2::new(50.0, 50.0)).unwrap();
assert_eq!(graph.node_transform(source).unwrap().translation, Vec2::new(50.0, 50.0));
assert_eq!(graph.edge_count(), 1); // Still 1 edge

// Topological sort: source before sink
let sorted = graph.topological_sort().unwrap();
assert_eq!(sorted[0], source);
assert_eq!(sorted[1], sink);

// No cycles
assert!(!graph.has_cycles());

docs.title: What NodeGraph Does NOT Own
docs.text:
Concern Owner Graph evaluation / dataflow (pushing values through edges) Domain Engine (depends on port data types) Port default values Domain Engine Subgraphs / node groups Domain Engine Rendering (node boxes, edge curves, port circles) UI Layer Input handling (drag nodes, draw edges) UI Layer Type hierarchies (float → double) Domain Engine Graph layout algorithms (auto-arrange) Domain Engine / External

The foundation provides the structure (nodes, ports, edges, validation, traversal). The Domain Engine provides the evaluation (what values flow through the edges).

docs.title: Viewport3D
docs.text: Headless 3D spatial editing model. Provides objects, transforms (Euler angles), parent-child hierarchy, and spatial queries — without any renderer, camera, or projection.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph V3D[Viewport3D]
        SCENE[Scene<br/>objects + next_id]
        OBJ[Object3D<br/>id + transform + parent]
        TF[Transform3D<br/>translation + rotation + scale]
        V3[Vec3<br/>x + y + z]
    end
    V3D -->|operations| OPS[Viewport3DOperation]
    OPS -->|apply| OUT[Viewport3DOutcome]

docs.title: Key Types
docs.text: Type Fields Purpose Scene objects: HashMap<ObjectId3D, Object3D>, next_id: u64 Container owning all 3D objects Object3D id, transform: Transform3D, parent: Option<ObjectId3D> 3D spatial entity with optional parent Transform3D translation: Vec3, rotation: Vec3, scale: Vec3 Decomposed 3D transform Vec3 x: f64, y: f64, z: f64 3D vector ObjectId3D u64 (opaque) Stable, opaque identifier Viewport3DError ObjectNotFound, CannotBeOwnParent, ParentNotFound Error type Viewport3DOperation 8 variants Value-type operation intent Viewport3DOutcome 8 variants Result with undo data

docs.text: Method Returns Description create_object(transform) ObjectId3D Create a new root object insert_object(object) () Restore an object with its original id (for undo) remove_object(id) Result<Object3D, Viewport3DError> Remove an object clear() () Remove all objects (id counter preserved)
