docs.text: Method Returns Description set_transform(id, transform) Result<Transform3D, Viewport3DError> Replace whole transform, returns previous set_translation(id, translation) Result<Transform3D, Viewport3DError> Set translation only, preserve rotation/scale set_rotation(id, rotation) Result<Transform3D, Viewport3DError> Set rotation only, preserve translation/scale set_scale(id, scale) Result<Transform3D, Viewport3DError> Set scale only, preserve translation/rotation

docs.title: Hierarchy
docs.text: Method Returns Description set_parent(id, parent) Result<(), Viewport3DError> Set parent (None = root), rejects cycles world_transform(id) Result<Transform3D, Viewport3DError> Compose transforms up the parent chain children(id) Vec<&Object3D> Direct children of an object root_objects() Vec<&Object3D> All root objects (parent == None)

docs.title: Spatial queries
docs.text: Method Returns Description objects_in_bounds(min, max) Vec<&Object3D> Objects whose translation falls in 3D bounds

docs.title: Parent-Child Hierarchy
docs.text:
Objects can have a parent for transform inheritance:

flowchart TD
    ROOT[Root Object<br/>translation: (10, 0, 0)] --> CHILD[Child Object<br/>translation: (5, 0, 0)]
    CHILD --> GRANDCHILD[Grandchild Object<br/>translation: (1, 0, 0)]

set_parent(id, parent) establishes the hierarchy. It rejects:

  1. Self-parenting: id == parent → CannotBeOwnParent
  2. Cycles: parent is a descendant of id → CannotBeOwnParent
  3. Missing parent: parent doesn't exist → ParentNotFound

docs.title: World Transform
docs.text:
world_transform(id) composes transforms by walking up the parent chain:

let world = scene.world_transform(grandchild)?;
// world.translation = root.translation + child.translation + grandchild.translation
//                  = (10, 0, 0) + (5, 0, 0) + (1, 0, 0) = (16, 0, 0)

Known limitation

world_transform currently composes translations only. Proper 3D transform composition requires matrix multiplication (including rotation and scale), which is rendering-adjacent and intentionally excluded. A Domain Engine that needs full 3D transform composition implements it externally.

docs.title: Vec3 Math
docs.text:
Method Returns Description dot(other) f64 Dot product cross(other) Vec3 Cross product length() f64 Euclidean magnitude normalised() Vec3 Unit vector (zero if length is zero) lerp(other, t) Vec3 Linear interpolation (t=0 = self, t=1 = other) distance_to(other) f64 Euclidean distance to other

Operators: Add, Sub, Mul<f64>, AddAssign, SubAssign, MulAssign.

docs.title: Transform3D
docs.text:
Method Description identity() No translation, no rotation, unit scale from_translation(v) Translation only from_rotation(v) Rotation only (Euler angles: pitch, yaw, roll in radians) from_scale(v) Scale only with_translation(v) Builder: set translation with_rotation(v) Builder: set rotation with_scale(v) Builder: set scale

Rotation is stored as Euler angles (Vec3 of pitch, yaw, roll in radians). The foundation does not provide quaternion support. A Domain Engine that needs quaternion interpolation (to avoid gimbal lock) adds it externally.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Operation Outcome Undo Create { transform } Created { id } Remove the created object Move { id, translation } Moved { previous } Restore previous transform Rotate { id, rotation } Rotated { previous } Restore previous transform Scale { id, scale } Scaled { previous } Restore previous transform Transform { id, transform } Transformed { previous } Restore previous transform Remove { id } Removed { object } Re-insert via insert_object SetParent { id, parent } ParentSet { previous_parent } Restore previous parent Clear Cleared { count } (limited — no stored objects to restore)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::viewport_3d::*;

let mut scene = Scene::new();

// Create hierarchy
let root = scene.create_object(Transform3D::from_translation(Vec3::new(10.0, 0.0, 0.0)));
let child = scene.create_object(Transform3D::from_translation(Vec3::new(5.0, 0.0, 0.0)));
let grandchild = scene.create_object(Transform3D::from_translation(Vec3::new(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)));

scene.set_parent(child, Some(root)).unwrap();
scene.set_parent(grandchild, Some(child)).unwrap();

// World transform composes translations
let world = scene.world_transform(grandchild).unwrap();
assert_eq!(world.translation, Vec3::new(16.0, 0.0, 0.0));

// Children and roots
assert_eq!(scene.children(root).len(), 1);
assert_eq!(scene.root_objects().len(), 1); // only root

// Cycle detection
let err = scene.set_parent(root, Some(grandchild)).unwrap_err();
assert!(matches!(err, Viewport3DError::CannotBeOwnParent { .. }));

// Spatial query
let found = scene.objects_in_bounds(
    Vec3::new(-10.0, -10.0, -10.0),
    Vec3::new(20.0, 10.0, 10.0),
);
assert_eq!(found.len(), 3); // all three objects

// Vec3 math
let a = Vec3::new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
let b = Vec3::new(3.0, 4.0, 0.0);
assert!((a.distance_to(b) - 5.0).abs() < 1e-10);

docs.title: CellId Design
docs.text:
CellId is a composite struct carrying both RowId and ColumnId:

pub struct CellId {
    pub row: RowId,
    pub column: ColumnId,
}

This means given a CellId, you can immediately find both its row and column without a separate lookup. This is used by remove_row (which scans cells by CellId.row) and merge_cells (which constructs CellIds from the row/column ordering).

docs.title: Row and Column Ordering
docs.text:
Rows and columns have a defined order via row_order: Vec<RowId> and column_order: Vec<ColumnId>, separate from the HashMap storage. This allows:

  • O(1) lookup by id (HashMap)
  • Defined iteration order (Vec)
  • Reordering (move_row, move_column)
  • Swapping (swap_rows, swap_columns)
let mut table = Table::new();
let r1 = table.insert_row(Some("Header".into()));
let r2 = table.insert_row(Some("Data 1".into()));
let r3 = table.insert_row(Some("Data 2".into()));

assert_eq!(table.row_ids(), &[r1, r2, r3]);

table.swap_rows(0, 2); // swap by position
assert_eq!(table.row_ids(), &[r3, r2, r1]);

docs.title: Merged Cells
docs.text:
Merge a rectangular region from from (top-left) to to (bottom-right). The top-left cell becomes the master; all others are marked as merged:

Before merge:          After merge_cells(from=(r1,c1), to=(r2,c2)):
┌───┬───┬───┐         ┌───┬───┬───┐
│ A │ B │ C │         │       │ C │
├───┼───┼───┤   →     ├───────┼───┤
│ D │ E │ F │         │       │ F │
└───┴───┴───┘         └───────┴───┘
  ↑   ↑   ↑             ↑       ↑
 r1c1 r1c2 r1c3       master   r1c3
  • is_merged(r1c2) → true
  • is_merged(r1c1) → false (master is not "merged")
  • master_cell(r2c2) → r1c1

unmerge_cells(master) frees all cells merged into that master.

docs.title: CellValue
docs.text:
pub enum CellValue {
    None,           // Empty / unset
    Text(String),   // Text content
    Int(i64),       // Integer
    Float(f64),     // Floating point
    Bool(bool),     // Boolean
}

Every cell accepts any CellValue. The Table does not enforce per-column type constraints. A Domain Engine that needs "column A only accepts Int" uses the validation utility to enforce that rule.

Cell formulas and calculation dependencies are not part of the Table environment. A Domain Engine can define cell dependencies using the Relations system.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::table::*;

let mut table = Table::new();

// Create structure
let header = table.insert_row(Some("Name".into()));
let row1 = table.insert_row(Some("Alice".into()));
let row2 = table.insert_row(Some("Bob".into()));
let name_col = table.insert_column(Some("Name".into()));
let age_col = table.insert_column(Some("Age".into()));

// Set cell values
table.set_cell_value(header, name_col, CellValue::Text("Name".into())).unwrap();
table.set_cell_value(header, age_col, CellValue::Text("Age".into())).unwrap();
table.set_cell_value(row1, age_col, CellValue::Int(30)).unwrap();
table.set_cell_value(row2, age_col, CellValue::Int(25)).unwrap();

assert_eq!(table.cell_count(), 4);
assert_eq!(table.cell(row1, age_col), &CellValue::Int(30));

// Merge cells
table.merge_cells(
    CellId { row: header, column: name_col },
    CellId { row: header, column: age_col },
).unwrap();
assert!(table.is_merged(CellId { row: header, column: age_col }));

// Swap rows
table.swap_rows(1, 2);
assert_eq!(table.row_ids(), &[header, row2, row1]);

docs.title: TextEditor
docs.text: Headless text editing model with Unicode scalar value positions, ranges, search/replace, and line/column mapping — without any editor widget, syntax highlighting, or input handling.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph TXT[TextEditor]
        DOC[Document<br/>text + char_count (cached)]
        POS[Position<br/>u32 (Unicode scalar value offset)]
        RNG[Range<br/>start + end (half-open)]
    end
    TXT -->|operations| OPS[TextEditorOperation]
    OPS -->|apply| OUT[TextEditorOutcome]

docs.title: Indexing Convention: Unicode Scalar Values
docs.text:
Positions are character offsets, not UTF-8 byte offsets. The document's len() returns the count of Unicode scalar values (code points), matching Rust's str::chars().

Document: "héllo"
Positions: 0  1  2  3  4  5
            h  é  l  l  o
  • Position 0 is before the first character.
  • Position len() is after the last character.
  • Valid positions are 0..=len().
  • Multibyte characters (é, emoji, CJK) each occupy exactly one position.

é is 2 bytes in UTF-8 but counts as 1 position. 😀 is 4 bytes in UTF-8 but also 1 position.

docs.title: O(1) Length
docs.text:
Document caches char_count: u32 alongside text: String. All mutating methods keep the cache in sync:

Method Cache update insert(pos, text) char_count += inserted.chars().count() delete(range) char_count -= range.len() replace(range, text) char_count = char_count - removed + added clear() char_count = 0 replace_all(...) char_count = text.chars().count() (recompute)

len() returns char_count directly — no chars().count() traversal.

docs.text: Method / Trait Description new(u32) Construct zero() Position 0 as_u32() Read value Add<u32> pos + 3 → new position Sub<u32> pos - 2 → new position PartialOrd, Ord Comparison Display "pos5"

docs.title: Range
docs.text: Method / Trait Description new(start, end) Construct (start <= end) at(pos) Zero-length range at a position len() end - start is_empty() start == end contains(pos) start <= pos < end (half-open) overlaps(other) Whether two ranges share any position intersect(other) Intersection, or None if no overlap shift(n) Move both start and end forward by n From<(Position, Position)> (start, end).into() PartialOrd, Ord Sort by start, then end

docs.title: Line / Column Mapping
docs.text:
line_col_at(pos) converts a character position to (line, column):

let doc = Document::from_str("hello\nworld\nfoo");
assert_eq!(doc.line_count(), 3);

assert_eq!(doc.line_col_at(Position::new(0)),  Some((0, 0))); // 'h' in "hello"
assert_eq!(doc.line_col_at(Position::new(5)),  Some((0, 5))); // before \n
assert_eq!(doc.line_col_at(Position::new(6)),  Some((1, 0))); // 'w' in "world"
assert_eq!(doc.line_col_at(Position::new(11)), Some((1, 5))); // before \n
assert_eq!(doc.line_col_at(Position::new(12)), Some((2, 0))); // 'f' in "foo"

Line 0 is the first line. Column 0 is the start of each line. Newline characters are not counted as part of the next line.

docs.title: Search and Replace
docs.text:
let mut doc = Document::from_str("foo bar foo baz foo");

// Find all occurrences
let matches = doc.find_all("foo");
assert_eq!(matches.len(), 3);

// Find from a position
let range = doc.find("foo", Position::new(5)).unwrap();
assert_eq!(range, Range::new(Position::new(8), Position::new(11)));

// Replace all
let count = doc.replace_all("foo", "XXX");
assert_eq!(count, 3);
assert_eq!(doc.text(), "XXX bar XXX baz XXX");

Search works on the byte level internally (via str::find) but returns character-position ranges. Empty needles return an empty match at the start position.

docs.text: Operation Outcome Undo Insert { position, text } Inserted { range } Delete the inserted range Delete { range } Deleted { range, text } Re-insert the deleted text Replace { range, text } Replaced { range, previous_text } Delete new text, insert previous_text Clear Cleared { previous_text } Re-insert previous text Append { text } Appended { range } Delete the appended range DeleteLine { pos } LineDeleted { text } Re-insert the deleted line ReplaceLine { pos, new_text } LineReplaced { previous_text } Delete new text, insert previous line

docs.title: IntoIterator
docs.text:
// Iterate over characters
for ch in &doc {
    print!("{}", ch);
}

IntoIterator for &Document yields char via str::chars().

docs.title: DeleteLine
docs.text:
Deletes the entire line containing pos, including the trailing newline:

Before: "line1\nline2\nline3"
                       ↑ pos = 6
After:  "line1\nline3"

Deleted text: "line2\n"

docs.title: ReplaceLine
docs.text:
Replaces the line containing pos with new text (preserves the trailing newline):

Before: "line1\nline2\nline3"
                       ↑ pos = 6
Replace with: "replaced"
After:  "line1\nreplaced\nline3"

Previous text: "line2"

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::text_editor::*;

let mut doc = Document::new();

// Type some text
doc.append("Hello").unwrap();
doc.append(" World").unwrap();
assert_eq!(doc.text(), "Hello World");
assert_eq!(doc.len(), 11);

// Insert at position
doc.insert(Position::new(5), ",").unwrap();
assert_eq!(doc.text(), "Hello, World");

// Search
let matches = doc.find_all("o");
assert_eq!(matches.len(), 2);

// Replace a range
let range = Range::new(Position::new(0), Position::new(5));
doc.replace(range, "Goodbye").unwrap();
assert_eq!(doc.text(), "Goodbye, World");

// Line operations
let doc2 = Document::from_str("line1\nline2\nline3");
assert_eq!(doc2.line_count(), 3);
assert_eq!(doc2.line_col_at(Position::new(7)), Some((1, 1)));

// Unicode handling
let doc3 = Document::from_str("a😀b");
assert_eq!(doc3.len(), 3); // a, 😀, b — each one position
assert_eq!(doc3.char_at(Position::new(1)), Some('😀'));

docs.title: Relations
docs.text: Relations describe how changes in one object or property affect other objects or properties. This is more specific than "relations connect objects" — a relation represents propagation, dependency, derivation, or invalidation semantics between endpoints.

docs.title: Mechanism vs Meaning
docs.text:
Layer Responsibility Foundation Relation identity, endpoints, registration, evaluation, propagation, batch, value source/sink Domain Engine Which relations exist, what property changes, what effect occurs, when, how the result is calculated

The relation system never inspects what an effect closure does — it just calls it.

flowchart LR
    SRC[Object A<br/>property X changes] --> REL[Relation]
    REL -->|effect closure| TGT1[Object B<br/>property Y]
    REL -->|effect closure| TGT2[Object C<br/>property Z]
    REL -->|effect closure| TGT3[Object D<br/>property Q]

The foundation provides the mechanism. The Domain Engine provides the meaning:

Reusable Relation System
          +
Domain-defined relation definitions (effect closures)
          =
Application-specific behavior

docs.title: Key Types
docs.text: Type Purpose PropertyId Opaque address: ObjectId + property index Endpoint Source or target endpoint with role EndpointRole Source or Target RelationId Opaque identifier for a registered relation RelationDefinition Declarative metadata + effect closure RelationDefinitionBuilder Builder for definitions Trigger OnChange, OnInitialSet, OnInvalidation PropagationMode Direct or Cascading EffectFn Arc<dyn Fn(&EffectContext) -> EffectOutcome + Send + Sync> EffectContext Read-only context passed to effect closures EffectOutcome Apply(value), NoChange, Invalidate PropertyValue None, Bool, Int, Float, Text, Bytes RelationRegistry Stores definitions, priority-sorted lookup EvaluationEngine Evaluates individual relations, applies outcomes EvaluationContext External handle: set values, propagate, batch Propagator Drives cascading propagation with cycle protection ValueStore Mutable property value store PropertyValueSource Trait: bridge Domain Engine state to evaluation PropertyValueSink Trait: receive property value updates from evaluation SourcedValueStore Adapter wrapping a PropertyValueSource DependencyGraph Fast source/target lookup for cascade traversal RelationError RelationNotFound, SourceMismatch, MaxPropagationDepthReached

docs.title: Relation Definition
docs.text:
let src = Endpoint::source(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0));
let tgt = Endpoint::target(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0));

let def = RelationDefinitionBuilder::new(src, tgt)
    .trigger(Trigger::OnChange)
    .propagation(PropagationMode::Cascading)
    .priority(100)
    .effect(Arc::new(|ctx: &EffectContext| {
        EffectOutcome::Apply(ctx.source_value.clone())
    }))
    .build();
Field Type Default Description source Endpoint (required) Source endpoint (triggers evaluation) target Endpoint (required) Target endpoint (receives effect) trigger Trigger OnChange When the relation fires propagation PropagationMode Direct Whether to cascade after applying priority i32 0 Higher fires first when multiple share a source effect EffectFn NoChange The closure to call during evaluation

docs.title: Propagation Modes
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    SRC[Source changes] --> REL1[Relation A]
    REL1 -->|Direct| TGT1[Target A<br/>stop]
    REL1 -->|Cascading| TGT1
    TGT1 --> REL2[Relation B<br/>source = Target A]
    REL2 -->|Cascading| TGT2[Target B]
    TGT2 --> REL3[Relation C<br/>source = Target B]
    REL3 -->|Cascading| TGT3[Target C]
Mode Behavior Direct Apply effect to immediate target, stop Cascading Apply effect, then re-evaluate any relations whose source is the target, transitively

docs.title: Cycle protection
docs.text:
Each relation is evaluated at most once per propagation pass. If a cycle exists (A→B→A), the propagator's visited set prevents infinite loops:

A → B → A (cycle)
  ↑         ↑
  visited   visited — skip, cycle broken

Maximum cascade depth is 256 (configurable via Propagator::with_max_depth()).

docs.title: Priority
docs.text:
When multiple relations share the same source property, higher priority fires first:

// Priority 100 fires before priority 0
RelationDefinitionBuilder::new(src, tgt1)
    .priority(100)
    .effect(Arc::new(|ctx| EffectOutcome::Apply(ctx.source_value.clone())))
    .build();

RelationDefinitionBuilder::new(src, tgt2)
    .priority(0)
    .effect(Arc::new(|ctx| EffectOutcome::Apply(PropertyValue::Int(0))))
    .build();

The RelationRegistry stores relations in a priority-sorted by_source map. The Propagator iterates in priority order (highest first) via EvaluationEngine::relations_with_source().

If relation A (priority 100) sets target to 10 and relation B (priority 0) sets the same target to 20, the result is 20 (B fires last). Use priorities to control evaluation order when relations compete for the same target.

docs.title: Effect Outcomes
docs.text:
Outcome Behavior Apply(value) Write value to the target property in the value store NoChange Do nothing — no step recorded, no cascade Invalidate Record a step (target was invalidated), cascade if Cascading mode, but don't change the target's value

Invalidate is useful for marking a target as "dirty" without computing a new value. A later relation with Trigger::OnInvalidation can then compute the value lazily.

docs.title: Single propagation
docs.text:
let mut ctx = EvaluationContext::new(&registry);
ctx.set_value(source_property, PropertyValue::Int(42));
let steps = ctx.propagate_from(source_property)?;
// steps: Vec<PropagationStep> — each has relation_id, target, outcome

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. EvaluationContext::propagate_from(source) creates an EvaluationEngine borrowing the registry and value store.
  2. A Propagator is created with the engine.
  3. propagate_recursive(source) finds all relations whose source is source (priority-sorted).
  4. For each relation, evaluate_one() is called: - Reads source and target values from the store (cloned to avoid borrow conflicts) - Constructs EffectContext with the values - Calls the effect closure - Applies the outcome to the value store immediately (so cascading relations see updated values)
  5. If the outcome is Apply or Invalidate and the propagation mode is Cascading, recurse from the target.
  6. Each relation is visited at most once (cycle protection).

docs.title: Value store is mutable during evaluation
docs.text: Outcomes are applied inside evaluate_one(), not after propagation. This ensures cascading relations see the effects of earlier relations in the same chain.

docs.title: Batch Propagation
docs.text:
Accumulate multiple property changes and propagate them together:

ctx.begin_batch();
ctx.set_value(prop_a, PropertyValue::Int(42));
ctx.set_value(prop_b, PropertyValue::Text("hello".into()));

// Changes are accumulated, not propagated yet
assert!(ctx.is_in_batch());

let steps = ctx.commit_batch()?;
// All changes propagated, deduplicated (each source property fires once)
Method Description begin_batch() Start accumulating changes without propagating commit_batch() Propagate all accumulated changes (deduplicated), return all steps rollback_batch() Discard accumulated changes without propagating is_in_batch() Whether currently in batch mode

Deduplication: if the same source property is set multiple times during a batch, it propagates only once.

docs.title: Value Source / Sink
docs.text:
Bridge Domain Engine state to the evaluation engine without manual sync to a separate ValueStore:

pub trait PropertyValueSource {
    fn get_property_value(&self, property: PropertyId) -> PropertyValue;
}

pub trait PropertyValueSink {
    fn set_property_value(&mut self, property: PropertyId, value: PropertyValue);
}

SourcedValueStore<S: PropertyValueSource> wraps a source and provides: - get(property) — reads from the source, or from local overrides - set(property, value) — writes a local override - apply_outcome(property, outcome) — applies an effect outcome as an override

This lets the evaluation engine read from the Domain Engine's actual state while applying outcomes as temporary overrides during propagation.

docs.title: Independence from Environments
docs.text:
The relation system has no knowledge of any environment's concrete types:

Relations system          ←→    Canvas2D
                         ←→    Timeline
                         ←→    Layers
                         ←→    NodeGraph
                         ←→    Table
                         ←→    Any Domain Engine state

All addressing is via opaque PropertyId values (ObjectId + property index). The relation system can relate properties on Canvas2D objects, Timeline clips, Table cells, or any other domain object — it doesn't know or care.

A Domain Engine that wants to use relations:

  1. Maps its environment objects to ObjectId values
  2. Maps its object properties to PropertyId values
  3. Defines RelationDefinitions with appropriate effect closures
  4. Calls EvaluationContext::propagate_from() when a property changes
  5. Reads results back from the value store (or implements PropertyValueSink)

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: Error When Recoverable? RelationNotFound { id } Relation id not in registry during evaluation No — the relation was unregistered SourceMismatch { expected, actual } Source property doesn't match the relation's definition No — wrong property passed MaxPropagationDepthReached { depth, property } Cascade exceeded 256 hops No — cycle or excessively deep chain

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_foundation::relations::*;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::relations::definition::*;
use std::sync::Arc;

// 1. Create registry
let mut registry = RelationRegistry::new();

// 2. Define endpoints (opaque — no knowledge of Canvas2D, Timeline, etc.)
let src = Endpoint::source(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0));
let mid = Endpoint::target(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0));
let tgt = Endpoint::target(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(3), 0));

// 3. A → B (cascading, copy value)
registry.register(
    RelationDefinitionBuilder::new(src, mid)
        .propagation(PropagationMode::Cascading)
        .priority(10)
        .effect(Arc::new(|ctx: &EffectContext| {
            EffectOutcome::Apply(ctx.source_value.clone())
        }))
        .build(),
);

// 4. B → C (cascading, add 1)
registry.register(
    RelationDefinitionBuilder::new(mid, tgt)
        .propagation(PropagationMode::Cascading)
        .effect(Arc::new(|ctx: &EffectContext| {
            if let PropertyValue::Int(v) = ctx.source_value {
                EffectOutcome::Apply(PropertyValue::Int(*v + 1))
            } else {
                EffectOutcome::NoChange
            }
        }))
        .build(),
);

// 5. Propagate
let mut ctx = EvaluationContext::new(&registry);
ctx.set_value(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0), PropertyValue::Int(100));
ctx.set_value(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0), PropertyValue::Int(0));
ctx.set_value(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(3), 0), PropertyValue::Int(0));

let steps = ctx.propagate_from(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0)).unwrap();
assert_eq!(steps.len(), 2); // A→B and B→C

// 6. Verify results
assert_eq!(ctx.get_value(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0)), &PropertyValue::Int(100));
assert_eq!(ctx.get_value(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(3), 0)), &PropertyValue::Int(101));

docs.text: Concern Owner What properties mean (width, visibility, position) Domain Engine What the effect does (copy, add, multiply, invalidate) Domain Engine (via effect closure) When to evaluate (on every change? on commit?) Domain Engine (controls when to call propagate_from) Type compatibility between source and target Domain Engine (effect closure handles conversion) Relation lifecycle (active/inactive toggle) Domain Engine (register/unregister) Conditional triggers (fire only if value increased) Domain Engine (effect closure returns NoChange)

docs.title: Utilities
docs.text: Optional reusable capabilities that a Domain Engine explicitly chooses to compose. Utilities are orthogonal to environments and relations — they operate over generic types, not domain-specific types.

docs.title: Orthogonality
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    UTIL[Utilities] --> FLT[Filtering]
    UTIL --> QRY[Querying]
    UTIL --> TAG[Tagging]
    UTIL --> SRT[Sorting]
    UTIL --> GRP[Grouping]
    UTIL --> VAL[Validation]
    UTIL --> BTCH[Batch]

    FLT --> C2D[Canvas2D]
    FLT --> TLM[Timeline]
    FLT --> TBL[Table]
    FLT --> ANY[Any T]

docs.title: Three rules
docs.text:
1. Utilities operate over generic T — no imports from environments or relations.
  2. Environments do not import utilities — a Canvas2D doesn't know filtering exists.
  3. Utilities do not own data meaning — they process data supplied to them.

A Domain Engine chooses which utilities to compose. A simple text editor might use no utilities. A vector editor might use filtering + tagging. A spreadsheet might use sorting + grouping + validation.

docs.title: Available Utilities
docs.text: Utility Key Types Purpose Filtering FilterCriteria, criteria(), And, Or, Not Composable predicates Querying Query, evaluate() Named, reusable queries Tagging Tag, TagSet Tags with deterministic order Sorting SortCriteria, by(), sort(), sorted() Criteria-based ordering Grouping GroupCriteria, group_by(), group_sorted() Group by key Validation ValidationRule, ValidationResult, validate_all(), validate_with_rules() Rules and results Batch BatchOperation, operation(), apply_batch() Multi-object operations

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
Composable predicates with AND/OR/NOT composition:

use app_shell::domain_foundation::utilities::filtering::*;

let items = vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

// Simple filter
let result = filter(&items, &criteria(|x: &i32| *x > 3));
assert_eq!(result, vec![&4, &5]);

// Composed: (x > 1) AND (x < 5)
let c = criteria(|x: &i32| *x > 1).and(criteria(|x| *x < 5));
let result = filter(&items, &c);
assert_eq!(result, vec![&2, &3, &4]);

// OR composition: x == 1 OR x == 5
let c = criteria(|x: &i32| *x == 1).or(criteria(|x| *x == 5));
let result = filter(&items, &c);
assert_eq!(result, vec![&1, &5]);

// NOT: NOT(x > 3)
let c = criteria(|x: &i32| *x > 3).not();
let result = filter(&items, &c);
assert_eq!(result, vec![&1, &2, &3]);

docs.title: Key types
docs.text: Type Description FilterCriteria<T> Trait: matches(&self, item: &T) -> bool criteria(f) Create from closure And<C1, C2> Logical AND wrapper Or<C1, C2> Logical OR wrapper Not<C> Logical NOT wrapper FnCriteria<F> Closure-based criteria

docs.title: Helper functions
docs.text: Function Returns Description filter(items, criteria) Vec<&T> Filtered items count(items, criteria) usize Count matching any(items, criteria) bool Whether any match all(items, criteria) bool Whether all match

docs.title: Filtering environment data
docs.text:
// Filter Canvas2D objects by position
let objects: Vec<Object> = canvas.iter().copied().collect();
let right_half = filter(&objects, &criteria(|obj: &Object| {
    obj.transform.translation.x > 50.0
}));

The Canvas2D environment doesn't know filtering exists — the Domain Engine bridges the two.

docs.title: Querying
docs.text:
Named, reusable queries built on filtering:

use app_shell::domain_foundation::utilities::filtering::{criteria, FilterCriteria};
use app_shell::domain_foundation::utilities::querying::*;

let query = Query::new(
    "positive_numbers".to_string(),
    criteria(|x: &i32| *x > 0),
);

let items = vec![1, -2, 3, -4, 5];
let result = evaluate(&query, &items);
assert_eq!(result, vec![&1, &3, &5]);

// Check individual items
assert!(query.matches(&5));
assert!(!query.matches(&-1));

docs.title: Key types
docs.text:
Type Description Query<T> Named query with boxed FilterCriteria<T> evaluate(query, items) Evaluate query against items

Query requires T: 'static (the criteria are type-erased via Box<dyn FilterCriteria<T>>). The only cross-utility dependency: Querying depends on Filtering (both within utilities/).

docs.title: Tagging
docs.text:
Tags and tag collections with deterministic iteration order (BTreeSet):

use app_shell::domain_foundation::utilities::tagging::*;

let mut set = TagSet::new();
set.add(Tag::new("visible"));
set.add(Tag::new("locked"));
set.add(Tag::new("selected"));

// Deterministic iteration (sorted alphabetically)
let names: Vec<&str> = (&set).into_iter().map(|t| t.as_str()).collect();
assert_eq!(names, vec!["locked", "selected", "visible"]);

// Set operations
let mut other = TagSet::new();
other.add(Tag::new("visible"));
other.add(Tag::new("archived"));

let inter = set.intersection(&other);
assert_eq!(inter.len(), 1); // "visible"

let union = set.union(&other);
assert_eq!(union.len(), 4);

assert!(set.contains_all(&other)); // false — "archived" not in set
assert!(set.contains_any(&other)); // true — "visible" in both

docs.title: Key types
docs.text: Type Description Tag String newtype (PartialEq, Eq, Ord, Hash) TagSet BTreeSet<Tag> wrapper

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Description add(tag) Insert (returns false if already present) remove(tag) Remove contains(tag) Existence check intersection(other) Tags in both sets union(other) All tags from both sets contains_any(other) Whether any tag from other is present contains_all(other) Whether all tags from other are present into_iter() Sorted iteration via IntoIterator

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text:
Criteria-based ordering:

use app_shell::domain_foundation::utilities::sorting::*;

let mut items = vec![3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6];

// In-place sort (ascending)
sort(&mut items, &by(|a: &i32, b: &i32| a.cmp(b)));
assert_eq!(items, vec![1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9]);

// Non-mutating (descending)
let items = vec![3, 1, 4, 1, 5];
let refs = sorted(&items, &by(|a: &i32, b: &i32| b.cmp(a)));
assert_eq!(refs, vec![&5, &4, &3, &1, &1]);
// Original unchanged
assert_eq!(items, vec![3, 1, 4, 1, 5]);

docs.title: Key types
docs.text: Type Description SortCriteria<T> Trait: compare(&self, a: &T, b: &T) -> Ordering by(f) Create from closure FnSortCriteria<F> Closure-based criteria

docs.title: Grouping
docs.text:
Group items by key, with deterministic sorted output:

use app_shell::domain_foundation::utilities::grouping::*;
use std::collections::HashMap;

let items = vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6];

// Group by parity (HashMap — unordered)
let groups: HashMap<bool, Vec<&i32>> = group_by(&items, |x| *x % 2 == 0);
assert_eq!(groups.get(&true).unwrap().len(), 3);  // 2, 4, 6
assert_eq!(groups.get(&false).unwrap().len(), 3); // 1, 3, 5

// Sorted output (BTreeMap — deterministic order)
let sorted_groups = group_sorted(&items, |x| *x % 2 == 0);
// false group first (false < true)

docs.title: Key types
docs.text: Type Description GroupCriteria<T> Trait with associated Key type group_by(items, f) Group by closure, returns HashMap group_sorted(items, f) Group by closure, returns BTreeMap (deterministic) group(items, criteria) Group by trait implementor

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Reusable rules and results:

use app_shell::domain_foundation::utilities::validation::*;

// Single rule
let r = rule(|x: &i32| {
    if *x >= 0 { ValidationResult::valid() }
    else { ValidationResult::invalid("must be positive") }
});

assert!(r.validate(&5).is_valid());
assert!(r.validate(&-1).is_invalid());

// Validate all items — returns only failures
let invalids = validate_all(&[1, -2, 3, -4], &r);
assert_eq!(invalids.len(), 2);

// Multi-rule validation — collect all failures
let rules: Vec<(&str, &ValidationRule<i32>)> = vec![
    ("positive", &r),
    ("small", &rule(|x: &i32| {
        if *x < 100 { ValidationResult::valid() }
        else { ValidationResult::invalid("must be < 100") }
    })),
];
let failures = validate_with_rules(&50, rules.iter().cloned());
assert!(failures.is_empty()); // 50 is positive and < 100

let failures = validate_with_rules(&-5, rules.iter().cloned());
assert_eq!(failures.len(), 1); // fails "positive"

docs.title: Key types
docs.text: Type Description ValidationResult Valid or Invalid { reason: String } ValidationRule<T> Trait: validate(&self, item: &T) -> ValidationResult rule(f) Create from closure validate_all(items, rule) Validate all items, return only failures validate_with_rules(item, rules) Validate one item against multiple rules

docs.title: Batch
docs.text:
Multi-object operations:

use app_shell::domain_foundation::utilities::batch::*;

// Closure-based
let mut items = vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
let op = operation(|items: &mut [i32]| {
    for item in items.iter_mut() {
        *item += 10;
    }
});
apply_batch(&op, &mut items);
assert_eq!(items, vec![11, 12, 13, 14, 15]);

// Trait-based
struct Double;
impl BatchOperation<i32> for Double {
    fn apply(&self, items: &mut [i32]) {
        for item in items.iter_mut() {
            *item *= 2;
        }
    }
}

let mut items = vec![1, 2, 3];
apply_batch(&Double, &mut items);
assert_eq!(items, vec![2, 4, 6]);

docs.title: Key types
docs.text: Type Description BatchOperation<T> Trait: apply(&self, items: &mut [T]) operation(f) Create from closure apply_batch(op, items) Apply operation to all items FnBatchOperation<F> Closure-based operation

docs.title: What Utilities Do NOT Do
docs.text:
Concern Owner Own the meaning of data Domain Engine Import environment types Never (generic T only) Persist state Domain Engine / App Engine Handle UI rendering UI Layer Define business rules Domain Engine

Utilities are pure functions — they process data supplied to them and return results. They don't own or persist anything.

docs.title: Domain Engine Integration
docs.text: The DomainEngine is the composition root that wraps all 7 environments with App Engine history, events, signals, and transactions. It defines how operations are executed — not what they mean.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    DE[DomainEngine] --> ENV[7 Environments<br/>Canvas, Timeline, Layers, NodeGraph, Table, Document, Scene]
    DE --> HIST[HistoryStore<br/>undo/redo, transactions]
    DE --> TX[TransactionManager<br/>begin/commit/rollback]
    DE --> EVT[EventBus<br/>publish events]
    DE --> SIG[SignalBus<br/>emit signals]
    DE --> DIRTY[Dirty Tracking<br/>mark_saved / is_dirty]
    DE --> COMP[Compound Operations<br/>cross-environment undo]
    DE --> CMD[Command Handlers<br/>Canvas, Timeline, Layers]

docs.title: Environment Access
docs.text:
Each environment is owned by the DomainEngine and accessible via getters:

Method Type Description canvas() &Canvas Canvas2D environment timeline() &Timeline Timeline environment layers() &Layers Layers environment node_graph() &NodeGraph NodeGraph environment table() &Table Table environment document() &Document TextEditor environment scene() &Scene Viewport3D environment history() &HistoryStore App Engine history event_bus() &EventBus App Engine event bus events() &[Event] Accumulated events for inspection transaction_manager() &TransactionManager App Engine transaction manager

docs.title: Execute Operations
docs.text:
Each environment has its own execute_* method:

// Canvas2D
engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create {
    transform: Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(10.0, 20.0)),
})?;

// Timeline
engine.execute_timeline(TimelineOperation::CreateTrack)?;

// Layers
engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::CreateLayer {
    name: "Background".to_string(),
})?;

// NodeGraph
engine.execute_node_graph(NodeGraphOperation::CreateNode {
    name: "Source".to_string(),
    transform: Transform::identity(),
})?;

// Table
engine.execute_table(TableOperation::InsertRow { name: None })?;

// TextEditor
engine.execute_text_editor(TextEditorOperation::Insert {
    position: Position::new(0),
    text: "hello".to_string(),
})?;

// Viewport3D
engine.execute_viewport_3d(Viewport3DOperation::Create {
    transform: Transform3D::identity(),
})?;

docs.title: What each execute_* method does
docs.text:
1. Applies the operation to the environment (via operation.apply(&mut env))
  2. Creates a HistoryEntry with the operation name
  3. If in a transaction, marks the entry with .with_transaction(tx_id)
  4. Appends to HistoryStore
  5. Publishes an Event via EventBus (e.g., "canvas.object.created")
  6. Emits a Signal via SignalBus (if configured, e.g., "canvas.object.created")
  7. If the operation fails and a transaction is active, auto-rolls back the entire transaction

docs.title: Backward compatibility
docs.text:
execute() is a backward-compatible alias for execute_canvas() that returns Result<CanvasOutcome, CanvasError> (not DomainError):

// Old API (still works)
let outcome = engine.execute(CanvasOperation::Create { ... })?;

// New API (returns DomainError for cross-environment consistency)
let outcome = engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create { ... })?;

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text:
Group multiple operations into a single undoable unit:

engine.begin_transaction();
engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create { transform: Transform::identity() })?;
engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::CreateLayer { name: "Base".into() })?;
engine.execute_timeline(TimelineOperation::CreateTrack)?;
engine.commit_transaction();

// One undo reverses all three operations
engine.undo()?;

docs.title: Transaction lifecycle
docs.text: Method Description begin_transaction() Start a transaction, returns TransactionId commit_transaction() End the transaction (entries remain in history, undo as one unit) rollback_transaction() Undo all operations in the transaction, remove entries from history in_transaction() Whether a transaction is active

docs.title: How undo works with transactions
docs.text:
The HistoryStore checks transaction_id on entries. When undo() is called:

  • If the entry has a transaction_id, all entries with the same id are undone as one unit
  • If no transaction_id, only that single entry is undone

docs.title: Auto-rollback on error
docs.text:
If execute_* fails while a transaction is active, the DomainEngine automatically rolls back the transaction:

engine.begin_transaction();
engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create { transform: Transform::identity() })?;

// This fails (object doesn't exist)
let err = engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Remove {
    id: ObjectId::from_raw(999),
}).unwrap_err();

// Transaction was auto-rolled back
assert!(!engine.in_transaction());
assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0); // Created object was undone

docs.title: Compound Operations
docs.text:
Cross-environment compound operations with nesting support:

let tx = engine.begin_compound();

engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create { transform: Transform::identity() })?;
engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::CreateLayer { name: "Group".into() })?;

// Nested compound
let tx2 = engine.begin_compound();
engine.execute_timeline(TimelineOperation::CreateTrack)?;
engine.execute_timeline(TimelineOperation::InsertClip { ... })?;
engine.commit_compound();

engine.commit_compound();

// Undo reverses everything as one unit
engine.undo()?;
Method Description begin_compound() Start (or nest) a compound operation commit_compound() End (or unnest) a compound operation rollback_compound() Roll back all operations in the compound

Compound operations use TransactionManager internally. The compound_depth counter supports nesting. Undo reverses all operations in the outermost compound as one unit.

docs.title: Dirty Tracking
docs.text:
Track whether the document has unsaved changes:

engine.mark_saved();
assert!(!engine.is_dirty());

engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create { transform: Transform::identity() })?;
assert!(engine.is_dirty());  // Unsaved change

engine.mark_saved();
assert!(!engine.is_dirty());

engine.undo()?;
assert!(engine.is_dirty());  // Undo creates unsaved state

is_dirty() compares saved_position with history.position(). Call mark_saved() after persisting state to any backend.

docs.title: Undo / Redo
docs.text:
// Execute 3 operations
engine.execute_canvas(Create { ... })?;
engine.execute_canvas(Move { ... })?;
engine.execute_canvas(Transform { ... })?;

// Undo all 3
engine.undo()?;  // undo transform
engine.undo()?;  // undo move
engine.undo()?;  // undo create
assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);

// Redo all 3
engine.redo()?;  // redo create
engine.redo()?;  // redo move
engine.redo()?;  // redo transform
assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 1);

docs.title: Undo implementation
docs.text:
Undo uses the position-based approach:

  1. Record position_before = history.position()
  2. Call history.undo() — returns count of undone entries
  3. Record position_after
  4. For each undone canvas operation (indices pos_after..pos_before in reverse), call executed_canvas[i].undo(&mut canvas)

docs.title: Undo publishes events
docs.text:
Both undo() and redo() publish events and emit signals:

  • undo() publishes "domain.undo" event + signal
  • redo() publishes "domain.redo" event + signal

docs.title: Events and Signals
docs.text:
Every execute_* call publishes:

Channel What Purpose EventBus Event::new("canvas.object.created") For logging, history, plugins SignalBus Signal::new("canvas.object.created") For real-time UI refresh

The SignalBus is optional — configure it via with_signal_bus():

use std::sync::Arc;
use app_shell::app_engine::SignalBus;

let signal_bus = Arc::new(SignalBus::new());
let engine = DomainEngine::new()
    .with_signal_bus(signal_bus);

Events are also accumulated in engine.events() for inspection in tests:

engine.execute_canvas(Create { ... })?;
engine.execute_canvas(Move { ... })?;
engine.undo()?;

// 2 execute events + 1 undo event = 3 total
assert_eq!(engine.events().len(), 3);

docs.title: Undo History Limit
docs.text:
let engine = DomainEngine::new()
    .with_max_history(100);  // Max 100 undo entries

When max_history > 0, the DomainEngine checks the history size after each operation. If the limit is exceeded, the oldest entries should be trimmed.

Known limitation

The App Engine's HistoryStore does not have a truncate_old method. The limit is checked but cannot be enforced without modifying the App Engine. A future HistoryStore update would add this capability.

docs.title: Construction
docs.text:
// Default — no signal bus, unlimited history
let engine = DomainEngine::new();

// With signal bus
let engine = DomainEngine::new()
    .with_signal_bus(Arc::new(SignalBus::new()));

// With history limit
let engine = DomainEngine::new()
    .with_max_history(100);

// Both
let engine = DomainEngine::new()
    .with_signal_bus(signal_bus)
    .with_max_history(100);

docs.title: Example: Multi-Environment Application
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_engine::DomainEngine;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::*;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::layers::*;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::timeline::*;

let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();

// Compound: create canvas object + layer + timeline clip
engine.begin_compound();

let obj_id = match engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create {
    transform: Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(100.0, 100.0)),
}).unwrap() {
    CanvasOutcome::Created { id } => id,
    _ => unreachable!(),
};

engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::CreateLayer {
    name: "Animation".to_string(),
}).unwrap();

let track = engine.timeline().track_ids()[0];
engine.execute_timeline(TimelineOperation::InsertClip {
    track_id: track,
    start: Time::new(0.0),
    duration: Duration::new(10.0),
}).unwrap();

engine.commit_compound();

// All three undo as one unit
engine.undo().unwrap();
assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);
assert_eq!(engine.layers().len(), 0);

docs.title: What DomainEngine Does NOT Do
docs.text:
Concern Owner Define application-specific object types Domain Engine (the real one, built on this) Define domain rules (e.g., "width must be positive") Domain Engine Render anything UI Layer Handle user input UI Layer Persist state to files App Engine (HistoryStore backend) Define what events mean Domain Engine / UI Layer

The DomainEngine in the foundation is a demonstration — it proves the architecture works. A real Domain Engine (built by the application) defines what objects mean, what rules they follow, and what operations are valid.

docs.title: App Engine Integration
docs.text: How the Domain Foundation connects to the App Engine's execution infrastructure: commands, history, events, signals, and transactions.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    DE[DomainEngine] -->|uses| HIST[HistoryStore]
    DE -->|uses| TX[TransactionManager]
    DE -->|uses| EVT[EventBus]
    DE -->|uses| SIG[SignalBus]

    CH[Command Handlers] -->|register with| CE[CommandExecutor]
    CE -->|dispatches| DE

    AE[AppEngine / AppRuntime] -->|owns| CE
    AE -->|owns| HIST
    AE -->|owns| TX
    AE -->|owns| EVT
    AE -->|owns| SIG

The DomainEngine uses App Engine subsystems through their public APIs. The App Engine never imports domain types — it only knows about Command, HistoryEntry, Event, and Signal.

docs.title: App Engine Subsystems Used
docs.text:
Subsystem How DomainEngine uses it HistoryStore append(entry) for each operation, undo() / redo() for undo/redo, remove_transaction(tx_id) for rollback TransactionManager begin() / commit() / rollback() for multi-step undo EventBus publish(&Event) on every operation and undo/redo SignalBus emit(&Signal) on every operation (if configured) CommandExecutor register(definition, handler) to register domain command handlers

All HistoryStore methods take &self (they use Mutex internally), so the DomainEngine doesn't need &mut for history operations.

docs.title: Command Handlers
docs.text:
Domain operations can be registered as App Engine commands, allowing the App Engine's CommandExecutor to dispatch them:

flowchart LR
    USER[User / API / Plugin] -->|creates Command| CE[CommandExecutor]
    CE -->|looks up handler| REG[Registry]
    REG -->|calls| HANDLER[CommandHandler]
    HANDLER -->|applies| ENV[Environment]
    HANDLER -->|records| HIST[HistoryStore]
    HANDLER -->|publishes| EVT[EventBus]

docs.title: Available command handlers
docs.text: Handler Definition ID Environment CanvasCommandHandler "canvas.operation" Canvas2D TimelineCommandHandler "timeline.operation" Timeline LayersCommandHandler "layers.operation" Layers

docs.title: Registering a command handler
docs.text:
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use app_shell::app_engine::*;
use app_shell::domain_engine::operations::CanvasCommandHandler;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::*;

// 1. Create shared environment state
let canvas = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Canvas::new()));

// 2. Create handler wrapping the shared state
let handler = CanvasCommandHandler::new(Arc::clone(&canvas));

// 3. Register with the App Engine's command executor
let mut engine: AppEngine = AppEngine::new()?;
engine.command_executor_mut().register(
    CanvasCommandHandler::definition(),
    Box::new(handler),
)?;

// 4. Execute a command through the App Engine
let cmd = Command::new(
    "canvas.operation",
    CommandContext::new(ExecutionId::new()),
    CommandInput::new(CanvasOperation::Create {
        transform: Transform::identity(),
    }),
);
let result = engine.execute_command(&cmd)?;
assert!(result.is_success());

// 5. Verify the canvas was modified
let canvas_guard = canvas.lock().unwrap();
assert_eq!(canvas_guard.len(), 1);

docs.title: How the handler works
docs.text:
The CommandHandler trait takes &self (immutable), but applying operations needs &mut. The solution: the handler wraps Arc<Mutex<Environment>>:

impl CommandHandler for CanvasCommandHandler {
    fn execute(
        &self,
        input: &CommandInput,
        _context: &CommandContext,
        engine: &EngineRef,
    ) -> Result<CommandResult, CommandError> {
        // 1. Extract the operation from typed input
        let operation = input
            .get::<CanvasOperation>()
            .ok_or_else(|| CommandError::ExecutionFailed("expected CanvasOperation".into()))?
            .clone();

        // 2. Apply to the shared canvas (lock + mutate)
        let outcome = {
            let mut canvas = self.canvas.lock()
                .map_err(|e| CommandError::ExecutionFailed(format!("lock: {e}")))?;
            operation.clone()
                .apply(&mut canvas)
                .map_err(|e| CommandError::ExecutionFailed(e.to_string()))?
        };

        // 3. Record in history via EngineRef
        engine.history_store.append(
            HistoryEntry::new("canvas.operation").undoable(),
        );

        // 4. Publish event via EngineRef
        engine.event_bus.publish(
            &Event::new("canvas.object.created").with_source("canvas_handler"),
        );

        // 5. Return the outcome as the command result
        Ok(CommandResult::success_with(outcome))
    }
}

docs.title: EngineRef
docs.text:
EngineRef is a read-only bundle of App Engine subsystems passed to handlers:

pub struct EngineRef<'a> {
    pub event_bus: &'a EventBus,
    pub signal_bus: &'a SignalBus,
    pub resource_manager: &'a ResourceManager,
    pub config_store: &'a ConfigStore,
    pub preferences: &'a Preferences,
    pub state_manager: &'a StateManager<LifecycleState>,
    pub command_executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
    pub scheduler: &'a Scheduler,
    pub history_store: &'a HistoryStore,
}

Handlers can: - Publish events (engine.event_bus.publish(...)) - Emit signals (engine.signal_bus.emit(...)) - Append history entries (engine.history_store.append(...)) - Load resources (engine.resource_manager.load(...)) - Submit tasks (engine.scheduler.submit(...))

The handler cannot: - Register new commands (the executor is &, not &mut) - Modify state directly (state manager is read-only) - Access the Domain Engine (the App Engine doesn't know about it)

docs.title: How operations are recorded
docs.text:
Each execute_* call on the DomainEngine creates a HistoryEntry:

let mut entry = HistoryEntry::new("canvas.create")
    .undoable();

// If in a transaction, mark the entry
if let Some(tx_id) = self.active_transaction {
    entry = entry.with_transaction(tx_id);
}

self.history.append(entry);

docs.title: Undo/redo
docs.text:
The DomainEngine calls history.undo() / history.redo() and then reverses/re-applies the canvas operations using the ExecutedCanvasOperation parallel list.

For non-canvas environments (Timeline, Layers, etc.), only the HistoryStore position changes — the actual environment state reversal must be handled by the Domain Engine (the current implementation only reverses Canvas2D operations).

docs.title: Transaction removal
docs.text:
rollback_transaction() calls history.remove_transaction(tx_id):

pub fn remove_transaction(&self, tx_id: TransactionId) {
    let mut entries = self.entries.lock().unwrap();
    entries.retain(|e| e.transaction_id() != Some(tx_id));
    let mut pos = self.position.lock().unwrap();
    *pos = pos.min(entries.len());
}

All entries with the given transaction id are removed, and the position is clamped.

docs.title: Event publication
docs.text:
fn publish(&mut self, event_name: &str, signal_name: &str) {
    let event = Event::new(event_name).with_source("domain_engine");
    self.event_bus.publish(&event);
    self.events.push(event);  // Also accumulate for inspection

    if let Some(ref sb) = self.signal_bus {
        sb.emit(&Signal::new(signal_name).with_source("domain_engine"));
    }
}

docs.title: Event naming convention
docs.text:
Operation Event name Signal name Create canvas object canvas.object.created canvas.object.created Move canvas object canvas.object.moved canvas.object.moved Remove canvas object canvas.object.removed canvas.object.removed Create track timeline.track.created timeline.track.created Insert clip timeline.clip.inserted timeline.clip.inserted Create layer layers.layer.created layers.layer.created Undo domain.undo domain.undo Redo domain.redo domain.redo

Events use a hierarchical dot-separated naming convention: <environment>.<entity>.<action>.

docs.title: SignalBus Integration
docs.text:
Signals are emitted alongside events for real-time UI updates:

Characteristic EventBus SignalBus Delivery May be delayed (priority queue) Immediate (synchronous) Use case Logging, history, plugins UI refresh, cursor update Required? Always Optional (with_signal_bus())

Configure the SignalBus:

let signal_bus = Arc::new(SignalBus::new());
let engine = DomainEngine::new()
    .with_signal_bus(signal_bus);

UI components subscribe to signals for immediate visual feedback:

signal_bus.subscribe("canvas.object.moved", Box::new(move |_signal| {
    // Redraw immediately
    request_redraw();
}));

docs.title: Full Integration Example
docs.text:
use app_shell::app_engine::*;
use app_shell::domain_engine::DomainEngine;
use app_shell::domain_engine::operations::CanvasCommandHandler;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::*;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

// 1. Create shared canvas
let canvas = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Canvas::new()));

// 2. Create and register command handler
let handler = CanvasCommandHandler::new(Arc::clone(&canvas));
let mut engine: AppEngine = AppEngine::new()?;
engine.command_executor_mut().register(
    CanvasCommandHandler::definition(),
    Box::new(handler),
)?;

// 3. Start the engine
engine.initialize()?;
engine.start()?;

// 4. Execute a command through the App Engine
let cmd = Command::new(
    "canvas.operation",
    CommandContext::new(ExecutionId::new()),
    CommandInput::new(CanvasOperation::Create {
        transform: Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(10.0, 20.0)),
    }),
);
let result = engine.execute_command(&cmd)?;
assert!(result.is_success());

// 5. Verify
let canvas_guard = canvas.lock().unwrap();
assert_eq!(canvas_guard.len(), 1);
assert_eq!(
    canvas_guard.iter().next().unwrap().transform.translation,
    Vec2::new(10.0, 20.0),
);

// 6. History was recorded
assert_eq!(engine.history_store().position(), 1);

// 7. Shutdown
engine.stop()?;
engine.dispose()?;

docs.title: What the App Engine Does NOT Know
docs.text:
Concept Known? Why Canvas2D ❌ The App Engine only knows Command, HistoryEntry, Event CanvasOperation ❌ Passed as CommandInput (type-erased via Any) ObjectId ❌ Never appears in App Engine types Transform, Vec2 ❌ Never imported by App Engine Timeline, Layers, etc. ❌ All domain types are opaque to the App Engine Domain rules ❌ The App Engine provides infrastructure; meaning stays in the Domain Engine

The CommandInput carries the operation as Box<dyn Any + Send>. The App Engine never inspects it — it passes it to the registered CommandHandler which knows how to extract and apply it.

docs.title: Operations & Undo
docs.text: Every environment follows the same value-type operation pattern: an Operation enum describes what to do, an Outcome enum carries what happened (with enough state to reverse it), and apply() connects the two.

docs.title: Operation Pattern
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    OP[MyOperation] -->|apply| ENV[MyEnvironment]
    ENV --> OUT[MyOutcome]
    OUT -->|undo data| UNDO[ExecutedOperation.undo]
    OUT -->|redo data| REDO[ExecutedOperation.redo]
// Operation — value-type intent (Clone, Debug, PartialEq)
pub enum CanvasOperation {
    Create { transform: Transform },
    Move { id: ObjectId, translation: Vec2 },
    Remove { id: ObjectId },
    // ...
}

// Outcome — result with undo data (Clone, Debug, PartialEq)
pub enum CanvasOutcome {
    Created { id: ObjectId },
    Moved { id: ObjectId, previous: Transform },
    Removed { object: Object },
    // ...
}

// Apply — connects operation to environment
impl CanvasOperation {
    pub fn apply(self, canvas: &mut Canvas) -> Result<CanvasOutcome, CanvasError>;
}

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
1. Operations are values — they can be cloned, compared, serialized, stored, and replayed.
  2. Outcomes carry undo state — each outcome variant includes enough data to construct the inverse operation.
  3. apply() is the only mutation path — the environment can be mutated directly (e.g., canvas.create_object()) but the operation system is the undoable path.
  4. Operations don't execute infrastructure — no history, no events, no signals. That's the DomainEngine's job.

docs.title: Undo Data per Outcome
docs.text:
Each outcome variant carries specific state needed to reverse the operation:

Outcome Undo data Undo action Created { id } id Remove the created object Moved { id, previous } previous: Transform set_transform(id, previous) Transformed { id, previous } previous: Transform set_transform(id, previous) Removed { object } object: Object insert_object(object) (preserves original id) MovedToFront { id, previous_index } previous_index: usize reorder(id, previous_index) MovedToBack { id, previous_index } previous_index: usize reorder(id, previous_index) MovedForward { id, previous_index } previous_index: usize reorder(id, previous_index) MovedBackward { id, previous_index } previous_index: usize reorder(id, previous_index) Reordered { id, previous_index } previous_index: usize reorder(id, previous_index) Duplicated { source, new_id } new_id remove_object(new_id) Cleared { count } (none) Cannot undo without storing all objects

docs.title: ExecutedCanvasOperation
docs.text:
The ExecutedCanvasOperation pairs an operation with its outcome, providing undo() and redo() methods:

pub struct ExecutedCanvasOperation {
    operation: CanvasOperation,
    outcome: CanvasOutcome,
}

impl ExecutedCanvasOperation {
    pub fn execute(canvas: &mut Canvas, operation: CanvasOperation)
        -> Result<Self, CanvasError>;

    pub fn undo(&self, canvas: &mut Canvas) -> Result<(), CanvasError>;
    pub fn redo(&self, canvas: &mut Canvas) -> Result<CanvasOutcome, CanvasError>;

    pub fn history_entry(&self) -> HistoryEntry;
    pub fn event(&self) -> Event;
}

docs.title: Undo implementation
docs.text:
pub fn undo(&self, canvas: &mut Canvas) -> Result<(), CanvasError> {
    match &self.outcome {
        CanvasOutcome::Created { id } => {
            canvas.remove_object(*id)?;
        }
        CanvasOutcome::Moved { id, previous } => {
            canvas.set_transform(*id, *previous)?;
        }
        CanvasOutcome::Removed { object } => {
            canvas.insert_object(*object);  // Restores original id
        }
        CanvasOutcome::MovedToFront { id, previous_index } => {
            canvas.reorder(*id, *previous_index)?;
        }
        CanvasOutcome::Duplicated { new_id, .. } => {
            canvas.remove_object(*new_id)?;
        }
        CanvasOutcome::Cleared { .. } => {
            // Cannot undo without storing all objects
        }
        // ...
    }
    Ok(())
}

docs.title: Redo implementation
docs.text:
Redo re-applies the original operation. For most operations, this is just self.operation.clone().apply(canvas). But Create is special:

pub fn redo(&self, canvas: &mut Canvas) -> Result<CanvasOutcome, CanvasError> {
    match &self.operation {
        CanvasOperation::Create { transform } => {
            // Use insert_object (not create_object) to preserve the original id
            let id = match &self.outcome {
                CanvasOutcome::Created { id } => *id,
                _ => unreachable!(),
            };
            canvas.insert_object(Object::new(id, *transform));
            Ok(self.outcome.clone())
        }
        _ => self.operation.clone().apply(canvas),
    }
}

Why insert_object instead of create_object? Because create_object assigns a new id from the counter. After undo (which removed the object but didn't reset the counter), create_object would give a different id. Any subsequent operations referencing the original id would fail. insert_object restores the object with its original id.

docs.title: Z-Order Undo
docs.text:
Z-order operations (MoveToFront, MoveToBack, MoveForward, MoveBackward, Reorder) carry previous_index:

// Apply captures the current index before moving
CanvasOperation::MoveToFront { id } => {
    let current = canvas.draw_order().iter()
        .position(|oid| *oid == id)
        .ok_or(CanvasError::ObjectNotFound { id })?;
    canvas.move_to_front(id)?;
    Ok(CanvasOutcome::MovedToFront { id, previous_index: current })
}

// Undo restores to the previous position
CanvasOutcome::MovedToFront { id, previous_index } => {
    canvas.reorder(*id, *previous_index)?;
}

All five z-order operations use reorder(id, previous_index) for undo.

docs.title: DomainEngine Undo/Redo
docs.text:
The DomainEngine maintains a parallel Vec<ExecutedCanvasOperation> synced with HistoryStore::position():

flowchart TD
    EXEC[execute_canvas] -->|1. apply| ENV[Canvas]
    EXEC -->|2. create HistoryEntry| HIST[HistoryStore]
    EXEC -->|3. push to executed_canvas| VEC[Vec<ExecutedCanvasOperation>]
    EXEC -->|4. publish event| EVT[EventBus]

    UNDO[undo] -->|1. history.undo| HIST
    UNDO -->|2. for each undone index| VEC
    UNDO -->|3. executed.undo| ENV
    UNDO -->|4. publish domain.undo| EVT

docs.title: Undo algorithm
docs.text:
pub fn undo(&mut self) -> Result<usize, DomainError> {
    let pos_before = self.history.position();
    let result = self.history.undo();
    let count = result.count();
    let pos_after = self.history.position();

    // Reverse canvas operations from pos_after to pos_before
    for i in (pos_after..pos_before).rev() {
        if let Some(executed) = self.executed_canvas.get(i) {
            executed.undo(&mut self.canvas)?;
        }
    }

    self.publish("domain.undo", "domain.undo");
    Ok(count)
}

docs.title: Redo algorithm
docs.text:
pub fn redo(&mut self) -> Result<usize, DomainError> {
    let pos_before = self.history.position();
    let result = self.history.redo();
    let count = result.count();
    let pos_after = self.history.position();

    // Re-apply canvas operations from pos_before to pos_after
    for i in pos_before..pos_after {
        if let Some(executed) = self.executed_canvas.get(i) {
            executed.redo(&mut self.canvas)?;
        }
    }

    self.publish("domain.redo", "domain.redo");
    Ok(count)
}

docs.title: Truncation on new operation
docs.text:
When a new operation is executed after undo, the redo stack must be cleared:

pub fn execute_canvas(&mut self, operation: CanvasOperation) -> Result<CanvasOutcome, DomainError> {
    let pos = self.history.position();
    self.executed_canvas.truncate(pos);  // Clear redo stack
    // ...
}

The HistoryStore::append() also truncates its entries (if position < entries.len()), so both stay in sync.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text:
Transactions group multiple operations into a single undoable unit via HistoryEntry::with_transaction(tx_id):

flowchart LR
    TX[begin_transaction] --> EXEC1[execute op 1]
    EXEC1 --> EXEC2[execute op 2]
    EXEC2 --> EXEC3[execute op 3]
    EXEC3 --> COMMIT[commit_transaction]

    UNDO[undo] -->|reverses all 3| ENV

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. begin_transaction() calls TransactionManager::begin(), stores the TransactionId, and records transaction_start_position.
  2. Each execute_* call creates a HistoryEntry with .with_transaction(tx_id).
  3. commit_transaction() calls TransactionManager::commit(). The entries stay in history but are linked.
  4. undo() calls HistoryStore::undo() which checks transaction_id — if present, it undoes all entries with the same id in one call.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
rollback_transaction() undoes all canvas operations from transaction_start_position to current position, then removes the entries from history:

pub fn rollback_transaction(&mut self) -> Option<TransactionId> {
    let tx_id = self.active_transaction;
    self.active_transaction = None;
    let result = self.transaction_manager.rollback();
    if let Some(tx_id) = tx_id {
        // Undo canvas operations
        let current_pos = self.history.position();
        for i in (self.transaction_start_position..current_pos).rev() {
            if let Some(executed) = self.executed_canvas.get(i) {
                let _ = executed.undo(&mut self.canvas);
            }
        }
        // Remove from history
        self.history.remove_transaction(tx_id);
        // Truncate executed list
        let new_pos = self.history.position();
        self.executed_canvas.truncate(new_pos);
    }
    result
}

docs.title: Compound Operations
docs.text:
Compound operations wrap transactions for cross-environment grouping:

let tx = engine.begin_compound();
engine.execute_canvas(Create { ... })?;
engine.execute_layers(CreateLayer { ... })?;
engine.execute_timeline(InsertClip { ... })?;
engine.commit_compound();

// Undo reverses all three as one unit
engine.undo()?;
Method Description begin_compound() Start (or nest deeper) a compound operation commit_compound() End (or unnest) — when depth reaches 0, commits the transaction rollback_compound() Roll back all operations in the compound

Nesting: compound_depth counter supports nested compounds. The outermost commit triggers commit_transaction().

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text: Limitation Description Undo only reverses Canvas2D The executed_canvas parallel list only stores Canvas operations. Timeline, Layers, etc. record in HistoryStore but their state isn't reversed on undo. A real Domain Engine would extend this to all environments. Cleared outcome can't undo Clear operations don't store removed objects. Undo is a no-op. A real Domain Engine would store all objects in the outcome or an external list. HistoryStore can't truncate old The undo history limit checks but can't actually remove old entries (no truncate_old method on HistoryStore).

docs.title: Serialization
docs.text: The Domain Foundation supports optional serialization via serde behind a feature flag. All serializable types have conditional derives; non-serializable types (closures, Mutex, lifetimes) use #[serde(skip)].

docs.title: Enabling Serialization
docs.text:
[dependencies]
app_shell = { path = "path/to/AppShell", features = ["serde"] }

The serde feature adds serde as a dependency and enables Serialize/Deserialize derives on all eligible types.

docs.title: Newtypes (with serde(transparent))
docs.text:
Newtypes wrap a single value. transparent tells serde to serialize the inner value directly:

#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(transparent))]
pub struct ObjectId(u64);
Newtype Inner type ObjectId u64 TrackId u64 ClipId u64 (has raw + track fields — not transparent) KeyframeId u64 LayerId u64 NodeId u64 PortId u64 EdgeId u64 RowId u64 ColumnId u64 ObjectId3D u64 Position u32 Time f64 Duration f64 RelationId u64 Tag String

docs.title: Structs and enums
docs.text:
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Transform {
    pub translation: Vec2,
    pub rotation: f64,
    pub scale: Vec2,
}

#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum CanvasOperation {
    Create { transform: Transform },
    Move { id: ObjectId, translation: Vec2 },
    Remove { id: ObjectId },
    // ...
}

docs.title: Environment containers
docs.text:
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Default)]
pub struct Canvas {
    objects: HashMap<ObjectId, Object>,
    draw_order: Vec<ObjectId>,
    next_id: u64,
}

All fields are serializable because HashMap, Vec, and u64 implement Serialize/Deserialize.

docs.title: What's NOT Serializable
docs.text: Type Reason Solution EffectFn (Arc<dyn Fn...>) Closures can't be serialized #[serde(skip, default = "default_effect")] RelationRegistry.next_id AtomicU64 doesn't implement Serialize #[serde(skip)] HistoryStore Uses Mutex<Vec<...>> Not serializable (App Engine type) EventBus Contains handler boxes Not serializable (App Engine type) SignalBus Contains callback boxes Not serializable (App Engine type) DomainEngine Contains EventBus, HistoryStore, etc. Not serializable EvaluationEngine<'a> Lifetime-bound Not serializable EvaluationContext<'a> Lifetime-bound Not serializable SourcedValueStore<S> Generic, not concrete Not serializable FnCriteria<F> Contains closure Not serializable FnSortCriteria<F> Contains closure Not serializable FnRule<F> Contains closure Not serializable FnBatchOperation<F> Contains closure Not serializable

docs.title: RelationDefinition: Custom Default
docs.text:
RelationDefinition has an effect: EffectFn field that can't be serialized. Serde's #[serde(skip)] requires Default, but Arc<dyn Fn...> doesn't implement Default. The solution: a custom default function.

#[cfg(feature = "serde")]
fn default_effect() -> EffectFn {
    Arc::new(|_| EffectOutcome::NoChange)
}

#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct RelationDefinition {
    pub source: Endpoint,
    pub target: Endpoint,
    pub trigger: Trigger,
    pub propagation: PropagationMode,
    pub priority: i32,
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip, default = "default_effect"))]
    pub effect: EffectFn,
}

When deserializing a RelationDefinition, the effect field is filled with a no-op closure. The Domain Engine must re-register the real effect after deserialization.

docs.title: Round-Trip Tests
docs.text:
#[cfg(feature = "serde")]
#[test]
fn canvas_roundtrip() {
    let mut canvas = Canvas::new();
    canvas.create_object(Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(1.0, 2.0)));
    canvas.create_object(Transform::from_translation(Vec3::new(3.0, 4.0)));

    let json = serde_json::to_string(&canvas).unwrap();
    let restored: Canvas = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(canvas, restored);
}

docs.title: What round-trip tests verify
docs.text: Test What it checks canvas_roundtrip Canvas objects, draw_order, next_id survive timeline_roundtrip Tracks, clips, keyframes, interpolation survive table_structure_roundtrip Rows, columns survive (cells don't — see limitation) document_roundtrip Text and char_count survive

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text: Limitation Reason Workaround Table's HashMap<CellId, CellValue> can't serialize to JSON serde_json requires string keys; CellId is a struct Custom serializer, or use a different format (bincode, msgpack) Table's HashMap<CellId, CellId> (merged_cells) Same reason Same workaround RelationDefinition::effect deserializes as no-op Closures can't be serialized Re-register the effect closure after deserialization RelationRegistry::next_id skipped on deserialize AtomicU64 can't be serialized The registry re-issues ids from 0 after deserialization; existing RelationIds may collide if not remapped

docs.title: Using with serde_json
docs.text:
#[cfg(feature = "serde")]
fn save_canvas(canvas: &Canvas) -> String {
    serde_json::to_string(canvas).unwrap()
}

#[cfg(feature = "serde")]
fn load_canvas(json: &str) -> Canvas {
    serde_json::from_str(json).unwrap()
}

Add serde_json as a dev-dependency for round-trip tests:

[dev-dependencies]
serde_json = "1"

docs.title: Using with Binary Formats
docs.text:
For formats that support non-string keys (like bincode), the Table limitation doesn't apply:

[dependencies]
bincode = "1"

let bytes = bincode::serialize(&table).unwrap();
let restored: Table = bincode::deserialize(&bytes).unwrap();
assert_eq!(table, restored);

#[test]

    engine.undo().unwrap();

docs.title: Concurrency Tests
docs.text:
Verify Send + Sync bounds and thread-safe shared mutation:

#[test]
fn canvas_is_send_sync() {
    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
    assert_send_sync::<Canvas>();
}

#[test]
fn canvas_shared_across_threads() {
    let canvas = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Canvas::new()));
    let handles: Vec<_> = (0..4).map(|i| {
        let canvas = Arc::clone(&canvas);
        thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut c = canvas.lock().unwrap();
            c.create_object(Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(i as f64, i as f64)));
        })
    }).collect();
    for h in handles { h.join().unwrap(); }
    assert_eq!(canvas.lock().unwrap().len(), 4);
}

docs.text:
Use proptest to verify invariants across random inputs:

proptest! {
    #[test]
    fn insert_then_delete_restores_text(
        original in "[a-z]{0,50}",
        pos in 0u32..50,
        inserted in "[a-z]{0,20}"
    ) {
        let mut doc = Document::from_str(&original);
        let len = doc.len();
        if pos <= len {
            doc.insert(Position::new(pos), &inserted).unwrap();
            let inserted_len = inserted.chars().count() as u32;
            doc.delete(Range::new(
                Position::new(pos),
                Position::new(pos + inserted_len),
            )).unwrap();
            prop_assert_eq!(doc.text(), original);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn undo_redo_preserves_canvas_state(ops in prop::collection::vec(canvas_op_strategy(), 1..10)) {
        let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();
        // Execute, undo all, redo all, verify same state
    }
}

docs.title: App Engine Lifecycle Test
docs.text:
Full AppEngine lifecycle with DomainEngine:

#[test]
fn app_engine_lifecycle_works() {
    let mut engine = AppEngine::new().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(engine.state(), LifecycleState::Created);

    engine.initialize().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(engine.state(), LifecycleState::Initialized);

    engine.start().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(engine.state(), LifecycleState::Running);

    assert!(engine.history_store().is_empty());

    engine.stop().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(engine.state(), LifecycleState::Stopped);

    engine.dispose().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(engine.state(), LifecycleState::Disposed);
}

docs.title: Struct literal in match
docs.text:
Never write match Enum::Variant { fields }.method() { ... } — the parser can't disambiguate the {. Bind to a variable first:

// WRONG — won't compile
let id = match CanvasOperation::Create { transform }.apply(&mut canvas).unwrap() { ... };

// CORRECT
let outcome = CanvasOperation::Create { transform }.apply(&mut canvas).unwrap();
let id = match outcome {
    CanvasOutcome::Created { id } => id,
    _ => unreachable!(),
};

Variant Fields When How to handle TrackNotFound { id: TrackId } Operation on a non-existent track Check timeline.contains_track(id) ClipNotFound { id: ClipId } Operation on a non-existent clip Check timeline.clip(id).is_some() KeyframeNotFound { id: KeyframeId } Remove or modify a non-existent keyframe Check clip's keyframes before operating ClipOverlap { id, conflicting_with } Insert or move a clip that would overlap an existing clip on the same track Check overlap with clip.overlaps(other) or catch the error and inform the user InvalidDuration { seconds: f64 } A clip with zero or negative duration was provided Validate duration before inserting InvalidSplitPoint { time: Time } Split point is outside the clip's range or at its boundary Ensure clip.start < at_time < clip.end() InvalidTrackIndex { index, track_count } move_track with an out-of-range index Check track_ids().len() before moving 
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum TimelineError {
    TrackNotFound { id: TrackId },
    ClipNotFound { id: ClipId },
    KeyframeNotFound { id: KeyframeId },

    InvalidDuration { seconds: f64 },
    InvalidSplitPoint { time: Time },

}

Variant Fields When How to handle NodeNotFound { id: NodeId } Operation on a non-existent node Check graph.contains_node(id) PortNotFound { id: PortId } Operation on a non-existent port Check graph.port(id).is_some() EdgeNotFound { id: EdgeId } Disconnect a non-existent edge Check graph.edge(id).is_some() NoCanvasObject { id: NodeId } Spatial operation (move/transform) on a node without a canvas object Check node.canvas_object.is_some() before spatial operations SourceNotOutput { id: PortId } connect where the source port is not Output direction Ensure the source port has PortDirection::Output TargetNotInput { id: PortId } connect where the target port is not Input direction Ensure the target port has PortDirection::Input SameNode — connect where source and target are on the same node Use different nodes for source and target TypeMismatch { source_type, target_type } connect where port type names don't match Ensure both ports have the same type_name DuplicateEdge { source, target } connect where an edge already exists between these ports Check graph.is_connected(source, target) before connecting CanvasError { source: CanvasError } A Canvas2D operation failed (e.g., canvas object not found) Check the inner CanvasError CycleInGraph — topological_sort detected a cycle in the graph Remove edges that form cycles before sorting MaxInputsExceeded { port, max } connect would exceed the target port's max_inputs limit Check graph.input_edge_count(port) < port.max_inputs before connecting 
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum NodeGraphError {
    NodeNotFound { id: NodeId },
    PortNotFound { id: PortId },
    EdgeNotFound { id: EdgeId },
    NoCanvasObject { id: NodeId },
    SourceNotOutput { id: PortId },
    TargetNotInput { id: PortId },
    SameNode,
    TypeMismatch { source_type: String, target_type: String },
    DuplicateEdge { source: PortId, target: PortId },
    CanvasError { source: CanvasError },
    CycleInGraph,
    MaxInputsExceeded { port: PortId, max: u32 },
}
