docs.title: Domain Engine
docs.text:
domain_engine::DomainError

Combined error type wrapping all environment errors:

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum DomainError {
    Canvas(CanvasError),
    Timeline(TimelineError),
    Layers(LayersError),
    NodeGraph(NodeGraphError),
    Table(TableError),
    TextEditor(TextEditorError),
    Viewport3D(Viewport3DError),
}

docs.title: Conversions
docs.text:
Each environment error implements From<EnvError> for DomainError:

let err: DomainError = CanvasError::ObjectNotFound { id }.into();

docs.title: Auto-rollback
docs.text: When execute_* fails while a transaction is active, the DomainEngine automatically rolls back the transaction. The error is still returned to the caller.

docs.title: Matching on DomainError
docs.text:
match engine.execute_canvas(op) {
    Ok(outcome) => { /* success */ },
    Err(DomainError::Canvas(CanvasError::ObjectNotFound { id })) => {
        eprintln!("Object not found: {}", id);
    },
    Err(e) => {
        eprintln!("Other error: {}", e);
    },
}

docs.title: Backward-compatible execute()
docs.text:
The execute() method (alias for execute_canvas()) returns Result<CanvasOutcome, CanvasError> (not DomainError) for backward compatibility with existing tests:

let err = engine.execute(CanvasOperation::Remove { id: fake_id }).unwrap_err();
assert!(matches!(err, CanvasError::ObjectNotFound { .. }));

docs.title: Check before operating
docs.text:
// Pattern 1: Check before operating
if canvas.contains(id) {
    canvas.set_translation(id, Vec2::new(10.0, 20.0))?;
}

// Pattern 2: Operate and handle error
match canvas.set_translation(id, Vec2::new(10.0, 20.0)) {
    Ok(previous) => { /* success */ },
    Err(CanvasError::ObjectNotFound { id }) => {
        // Object was removed — skip or recreate
    },
}

docs.title: DomainEngine auto-rollback
docs.text:
engine.begin_transaction();
match engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Move { id, translation }) {
    Ok(_) => { /* continue */ },
    Err(e) => {
        // Transaction was auto-rolled back by check_auto_rollback
        // Canvas is back to its pre-transaction state
        eprintln!("Failed: {}", e);
    },
}

[dependencies]

docs.title: 2. Create a DomainEngine
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_engine::DomainEngine;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::*;

let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();

// Create a canvas object
let id = engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create {
    transform: Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(100.0, 200.0)),
}).unwrap();

// Move it
engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Move {
    id,
    translation: Vec2::new(50.0, 50.0),
}).unwrap();

// Undo — restores the original position
engine.undo().unwrap();
assert_eq!(
    engine.canvas().get(id).unwrap().transform.translation,
    Vec2::new(100.0, 200.0),
);

docs.title: 3. Use Multiple Environments
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::timeline::*;

// Create a timeline
engine.execute_timeline(TimelineOperation::CreateTrack).unwrap();
let track = engine.timeline().track_ids()[0];

engine.execute_timeline(TimelineOperation::InsertClip {
    track_id: track,
    start: Time::new(0.0),
    duration: Duration::new(10.0),
}).unwrap();

// Query: what clips are active at time 5.0?
let active = engine.timeline().clips_at(Time::new(5.0));
assert_eq!(active.len(), 1);

use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::layers::*;

// Create a layer hierarchy
engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::CreateLayer {
    name: "Background".to_string(),
}).unwrap();
let root = engine.layers().roots()[0];

engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::CreateChild {
    parent: root,
    name: "Shapes".to_string(),
}).unwrap();

// Hide the root — children become effectively invisible
engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::SetVisibility {
    id: root,
    visible: false,
}).unwrap();
assert!(!engine.layers().effective_visibility(
    engine.layers().roots()[0]
));

use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::text_editor::*;

// Edit text
engine.execute_text_editor(TextEditorOperation::Insert {
    position: Position::new(0),
    text: "Hello, World!".to_string(),
}).unwrap();

assert_eq!(engine.document().text(), "Hello, World!");
assert_eq!(engine.document().len(), 13);

// Find text
let matches = engine.document().find_all("o");
assert_eq!(matches.len(), 2);

docs.title: 4. Transactions
docs.text:
Group multiple operations into a single undoable unit:

engine.begin_transaction();

engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create {
    transform: Transform::identity(),
}).unwrap();
engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create {
    transform: Transform::identity(),
}).unwrap();

engine.commit_transaction();

// Undo reverses both creations as one unit
engine.undo().unwrap();
assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);

docs.title: 5. Compound Operations (Cross-Environment)
docs.text:
// Group operations across different environments
engine.begin_compound();

engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create {
    transform: Transform::identity(),
}).unwrap();
engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::CreateLayer {
    name: "Group".to_string(),
}).unwrap();
engine.execute_timeline(TimelineOperation::CreateTrack).unwrap();

engine.commit_compound();

// One undo reverses all three
engine.undo().unwrap();
assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);
assert_eq!(engine.layers().len(), 0);

use app_shell::app_engine::{EventBus, EventHandler, Event};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

// Subscribe to events
struct PrintHandler;
impl EventHandler for PrintHandler {

docs.title: 7. Relations
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_foundation::relations::*;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::relations::definition::*;
use std::sync::Arc;

// Create a registry
let mut registry = RelationRegistry::new();

// Define: A.property0 → B.property0 (copy value, cascading)
let src = Endpoint::source(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0));
let tgt = Endpoint::target(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0));

registry.register(
    RelationDefinitionBuilder::new(src, tgt)
        .priority(10)
        .propagation(PropagationMode::Cascading)
        .effect(Arc::new(|ctx: &EffectContext| {
            EffectOutcome::Apply(ctx.source_value.clone())
        }))
        .build(),
);

// Propagate a change
let mut ctx = EvaluationContext::new(&registry);
ctx.set_value(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0), PropertyValue::Int(42));

let steps = ctx.propagate_from(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0)).unwrap();
assert_eq!(steps.len(), 1);

// Target received the value
assert_eq!(
    ctx.get_value(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0)),
    &PropertyValue::Int(42),
);

use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use app_shell::app_engine::*;
use app_shell::domain_engine::operations::CanvasCommandHandler;

// Create shared canvas
let canvas = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Canvas::new()));

// Create and register handler
let handler = CanvasCommandHandler::new(Arc::clone(&canvas));
let mut app_engine: AppEngine = AppEngine::new().unwrap();
app_engine.command_executor_mut().register(
    CanvasCommandHandler::definition(),
    Box::new(handler),
).unwrap();

app_engine.initialize().unwrap();
app_engine.start().unwrap();

// Execute via App Engine's command system
let cmd = Command::new(
    "canvas.operation",
    CommandContext::new(ExecutionId::new()),
    CommandInput::new(CanvasOperation::Create {
        transform: Transform::identity(),
    }),
);
let result = app_engine.execute_command(&cmd).unwrap();
assert!(result.is_success());

app_engine.stop().unwrap();
app_engine.dispose().unwrap();

//! Measurement environment: distance annotations on a 2D plane.

use super::annotation::Annotation;
use super::error::MeasurementError;
use crate::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::Vec2;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fmt;

/// Stable, opaque identifier for a measurement annotation.
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(transparent))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct MeasurementId(u64);

impl MeasurementId {
    pub fn from_raw(raw: u64) -> Self {
        Self(raw)
    }

    pub fn as_raw(self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for MeasurementId {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "measurement#{}", self.0)
    }
}

/// Headless measurement environment.
///
/// Stores distance annotations keyed by stable [`MeasurementId`]s.
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Default)]
pub struct Measurement {
    annotations: HashMap<MeasurementId, Annotation>,
    next_id: u64,
}

impl Measurement {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.annotations.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.annotations.is_empty()
    }

    pub fn contains(&self, id: MeasurementId) -> bool {
        self.annotations.contains_key(&id)
    }

    pub fn get(&self, id: MeasurementId) -> Option<&Annotation> {
        self.annotations.get(&id)
    }

    pub fn get_mut(&mut self, id: MeasurementId) -> Option<&mut Annotation> {
        self.annotations.get_mut(&id)
    }

    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Annotation> {
        self.annotations.values()
    }

    pub fn create(&mut self, start: Vec2, end: Vec2, label: String) -> MeasurementId {
        let id = MeasurementId::from_raw(self.next_id);
        self.next_id += 1;
        self.annotations.insert(id, Annotation::new(id, start, end, label));
        id
    }

    pub fn insert(&mut self, annotation: Annotation) -> MeasurementId {
        let id = annotation.id;
        if id.as_raw() >= self.next_id {
            self.next_id = id.as_raw() + 1;
        }
        self.annotations.insert(id, annotation);
        id
    }

    pub fn remove(&mut self, id: MeasurementId) -> Result<Annotation, MeasurementError> {
        self.annotations
            .remove(&id)
            .ok_or(MeasurementError::NotFound { id })
    }

    pub fn rename(&mut self, id: MeasurementId, label: String) -> Result<String, MeasurementError> {
        let ann = self.annotations
            .get_mut(&id)
            .ok_or(MeasurementError::NotFound { id })?;
        let previous = ann.label.clone();
        ann.label = label;
        Ok(previous)
    }

    pub fn move_endpoints(
        &mut self,
        id: MeasurementId,
        start: Vec2,
        end: Vec2,
    ) -> Result<(Vec2, Vec2), MeasurementError> {
        let ann = self.annotations
            .get_mut(&id)
            .ok_or(MeasurementError::NotFound { id })?;
        let prev = (ann.start, ann.end);
        ann.start = start;
        ann.end = end;
        Ok(prev)
    }

    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.annotations.clear();
    }
}

/// Iterate over annotations.
impl<'a> IntoIterator for &'a Measurement {
    type Item = &'a Annotation;
    type IntoIter = std::collections::hash_map::Values<'a, MeasurementId, Annotation>;

    fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {
        self.annotations.values()
    }
}

//! Measurement operations: value-type intents with undo data.

use super::annotation::Annotation;
use super::error::MeasurementError;
use super::measurement::{Measurement, MeasurementId};
use crate::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::Vec2;

/// A measurement operation.
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum MeasurementOperation {
    Create { start: Vec2, end: Vec2, label: String },
    Remove { id: MeasurementId },
    Rename { id: MeasurementId, label: String },
    MoveEndpoints { id: MeasurementId, start: Vec2, end: Vec2 },
    Clear,
}

/// Outcome of a successful operation.
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum MeasurementOutcome {
    Created { id: MeasurementId },
    Removed { annotation: Annotation },
    Renamed { id: MeasurementId, previous_label: String },
    Moved { id: MeasurementId, previous_start: Vec2, previous_end: Vec2 },
    Cleared { count: usize },
}

impl MeasurementOperation {
    pub fn apply(self, env: &mut Measurement) -> Result<MeasurementOutcome, MeasurementError> {
        match self {
            MeasurementOperation::Create { start, end, label } => {
                let id = env.create(start, end, label);
                Ok(MeasurementOutcome::Created { id })
            }
            MeasurementOperation::Remove { id } => {
                let annotation = env.remove(id)?;
                Ok(MeasurementOutcome::Removed { annotation })
            }
            MeasurementOperation::Rename { id, label } => {
                let previous_label = env.rename(id, label)?;
                Ok(MeasurementOutcome::Renamed { id, previous_label })
            }
            MeasurementOperation::MoveEndpoints { id, start, end } => {
                let (prev_start, prev_end) = env.move_endpoints(id, start, end)?;
                Ok(MeasurementOutcome::Moved {
                    id,
                    previous_start: prev_start,
                    previous_end: prev_end,
                })
            }
            MeasurementOperation::Clear => {
                let count = env.len();
                env.clear();
                Ok(MeasurementOutcome::Cleared { count })
            }
        }
    }
}

use crate::domain_foundation::environments::measurement::{
    Measurement, MeasurementError, MeasurementOperation, MeasurementOutcome,

pub struct DomainEngine {
    // ... existing fields ...
    measurement: Measurement,  // ← ADD

// In new():
measurement: Measurement::new(),

// Add getter:
pub fn measurement(&self) -> &Measurement { &self.measurement }

// Add execute method:
pub fn execute_measurement(
    &mut self,
    operation: MeasurementOperation,
) -> Result<MeasurementOutcome, DomainError> {
    let outcome = operation.clone().apply(&mut self.measurement)
        .map_err(|e| {
            let err: DomainError = e.into();
            self.check_auto_rollback(&err);
            err
        })?;

    let name = match &operation {
        MeasurementOperation::Create { .. } => "measurement.create",
        MeasurementOperation::Remove { .. } => "measurement.remove",
        MeasurementOperation::Rename { .. } => "measurement.rename",
        MeasurementOperation::MoveEndpoints { .. } => "measurement.move",
        MeasurementOperation::Clear => "measurement.clear",
    };
    let mut entry = HistoryEntry::new(name).undoable();
    if let Some(tx_id) = self.active_transaction {
        entry = entry.with_transaction(tx_id);
    }
    self.history.append(entry);

    let event_name = match &outcome {
        MeasurementOutcome::Created { .. } => "measurement.created",
        MeasurementOutcome::Removed { .. } => "measurement.removed",
        MeasurementOutcome::Renamed { .. } => "measurement.renamed",
        MeasurementOutcome::Moved { .. } => "measurement.moved",
        MeasurementOutcome::Cleared { .. } => "measurement.cleared",
    };
    let signal_name = match &outcome {
        MeasurementOutcome::Created { .. } => "measurement.created",
        MeasurementOutcome::Removed { .. } => "measurement.removed",
        _ => "measurement.changed",
    };
    self.publish(event_name, signal_name);

    Ok(outcome)
}

use crate::app_engine::capabilities::engine_ref::EngineRef;
use crate::app_engine::commands::command::CommandInput;
use crate::app_engine::commands::command_context::CommandContext;
use crate::app_engine::commands::command_definition::CommandDefinition;
use crate::app_engine::commands::command_executor::CommandHandler;
use crate::app_engine::commands::command_result::CommandResult;
use crate::app_engine::errors::command_error::CommandError;
use crate::app_engine::events::event::Event;
use crate::app_engine::history::history_entry::HistoryEntry;
use crate::domain_foundation::environments::measurement::{
    Measurement, MeasurementOperation,
};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

pub struct MeasurementCommandHandler {
    measurement: Arc<Mutex<Measurement>>,
}

impl MeasurementCommandHandler {
    pub fn new(measurement: Arc<Mutex<Measurement>>) -> Self {
        Self { measurement }
    }

    pub fn definition() -> CommandDefinition {
        CommandDefinition::new(
            "measurement.operation",
            "Measurement Operation",
            "Applies a MeasurementOperation to the measurement environment.",
        )
    }
}

impl CommandHandler for MeasurementCommandHandler {
    fn execute(
        &self,
        input: &CommandInput,
        _ctx: &CommandContext,
        engine: &EngineRef,
    ) -> Result<CommandResult, CommandError> {
        let op = input
            .get::<MeasurementOperation>()
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                CommandError::ExecutionFailed("expected MeasurementOperation".into())
            })?
            .clone();

        let outcome = {
            let mut env = self.measurement.lock()
                .map_err(|e| CommandError::ExecutionFailed(format!("lock: {e}")))?;
            op.clone()
                .apply(&mut env)
                .map_err(|e| CommandError::ExecutionFailed(e.to_string()))?
        };

        engine.history_store.append(
            HistoryEntry::new("measurement.operation").undoable(),
        );
        engine.event_bus.publish(
            &Event::new("measurement.operation").with_source("measurement_handler"),
        );

        Ok(CommandResult::success_with(outcome))
    }
}

docs.title: Adding Operations & Undo
docs.text:
This guide shows how to add new Operation/Outcome variant pairs to an existing environment, update all dependent code, and ensure undo/redo works correctly.

We'll add a SetColor operation to Canvas2D as a concrete example.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[1. Add to Operation enum] --> B[2. Add to Outcome enum]
    B --> C[3. Add apply arm]
    C --> D[4. Add undo/redo to ExecutedCanvasOperation]
    D --> E[5. Update DomainEngine name helpers]
    E --> F[6. Update CommandHandler match arms]
    F --> G[7. Add tests]

docs.title: Step 1: Add to Operation Enum
docs.text:
In src/domain_foundation/environments/canvas_2d/operations.rs, add the new variant:

pub enum CanvasOperation {
    // ... existing variants ...
    MoveToFront { id: ObjectId },
    MoveToBack { id: ObjectId },
    // ...
    Clear,

    // ↓ NEW
    /// Set the color of an object.
    SetColor { id: ObjectId, color: String },
}

docs.title: Step 2: Add to Outcome Enum
docs.text:
Add the corresponding outcome variant with undo data:

pub enum CanvasOutcome {
    // ... existing variants ...
    Cleared { count: usize },

    // ↓ NEW
    /// Color was set. `previous_color` is the old color (empty string if none).
    ColorSet { id: ObjectId, previous_color: String },
}

docs.title: Undo data checklist
docs.text:
Ask yourself: "What does undo need to restore?"

Operation What changed What undo needs Outcome field SetColor Object's color Previous color previous_color: String Move Translation Previous transform previous: Transform Remove Object deleted The object itself object: Object Create Object created The id to remove id: ObjectId

Rule: Every outcome variant must carry enough state to construct the inverse operation.

docs.title: Step 3: Add apply Arm
docs.text:
In the impl CanvasOperation block, add the match arm:

impl CanvasOperation {
    pub fn apply(self, canvas: &mut Canvas) -> Result<CanvasOutcome, CanvasError> {
        match self {
            // ... existing arms ...

            // ↓ NEW
            CanvasOperation::SetColor { id, color } => {
                // Need to get the previous color before setting the new one.
                // This requires a method on Canvas or Object.
                let obj = canvas.get_mut(id)
                    .ok_or(CanvasError::ObjectNotFound { id })?;
                let previous_color = obj.color.clone();  // Assuming Object has a color field
                obj.color = color;
                Ok(CanvasOutcome::ColorSet { id, previous_color })
            }
        }
    }
}

Object needs the field

If Object doesn't have a color field, you need to add it first: 

pub struct Object {
    pub id: ObjectId,
    pub transform: Transform,
    pub color: String,  // ← ADD
}
And update Object::new to initialize it.

docs.title: Step 4: Update ExecutedCanvasOperation

docs.title: Undo
docs.text:
pub fn undo(&self, canvas: &mut Canvas) -> Result<(), CanvasError> {
    match &self.outcome {
        // ... existing arms ...

        // ↓ NEW
        CanvasOutcome::ColorSet { id, previous_color } => {
            let obj = canvas.get_mut(*id)
                .ok_or(CanvasError::ObjectNotFound { id: *id })?;
            obj.color = previous_color.clone();
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

docs.title: Redo
docs.text:
For most operations, redo re-applies the original operation. SetColor is simple enough:

pub fn redo(&self, canvas: &mut Canvas) -> Result<CanvasOutcome, CanvasError> {
    match &self.operation {
        CanvasOperation::Create { transform } => {
            // Special case: use insert_object to preserve id
            // ...
        }

        // ↓ NEW (falls through to default)
        _ => self.operation.clone().apply(canvas),
    }
}

If SetColor is in the _ arm, it's handled automatically. Only Create needs special redo handling (via insert_object).

When adding a new operation, these files need updates:

# File What to add 1 environments/xxx/operations.rs Operation variant + Outcome variant + apply arm 2 environments/xxx/object.rs (or model file) New field on the data struct (if needed) 3 domain_engine/operations/canvas_operations.rs undo arm + check redo (usually falls through to _) + history_entry arm + event arm 4 domain_engine/mod.rs event_name_for_canvas_outcome arm + signal_name_for_canvas_outcome arm 5 domain_engine/operations/canvas_command_handler.rs entry_name match arm + event_name match arm 6 tests/.../canvas_2d_operations_test.rs Operation test + undo test + error test

docs.title: Undo Data Patterns
docs.text: Pattern When to use Example Return previous value Property mutation Moved { previous: Transform } Return removed entity Deletion Removed { object: Object } Return created id Creation Created { id: ObjectId } Return previous index Reordering Reordered { previous_index: usize } Return count Clear/bulk Cleared { count: usize } No undo data When undo isn't possible Cleared { count } (can't restore without storing all objects)

docs.title: Redo Patterns
docs.text: Pattern When to use Example Re-apply original operation Most operations _ => self.operation.clone().apply(canvas) Use insert (not create) Create operations canvas.insert_object(Object::new(id, transform)) No-op Operations that can't be redone Cleared (no stored objects)

docs.title: 1. Forgetting a match arm
docs.text: Rust's exhaustive match will catch this — but only in files that match on the enum. Check: - apply() in operations.rs - undo() in canvas_operations.rs - history_entry() in canvas_operations.rs - event() in canvas_operations.rs - Name helpers in domain_engine/mod.rs - Match arms in canvas_command_handler.rs

docs.title: 2. Not returning enough undo data
docs.text: If undo can't fully reverse the operation, the outcome doesn't carry enough state. Ask: "What was the state BEFORE the operation?"

docs.title: 3. Struct literal in match scrutinee
docs.text:
Never write match Foo::Variant { fields }.method() { ... }. Bind to a variable first:

// WRONG
let id = match CanvasOperation::SetColor { id, color }.apply(&mut canvas).unwrap() { ... };

// CORRECT
let outcome = CanvasOperation::SetColor { id, color }.apply(&mut canvas).unwrap();
let id = match outcome { ... };

docs.title: Creating a New Utility
docs.text:
This guide walks through creating a complete utility from scratch — trait, closure wrapper, free functions, re-exports, and tests.

We'll build a Mapping utility: transforms items from one type to another via a developer-supplied function.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[1. Directory structure] --> B[2. Trait definition]
    B --> C[3. Closure wrapper]
    C --> D[4. Free functions]
    D --> E[5. mod.rs re-exports]
    E --> F[6. Update utilities/mod.rs]
    F --> G[7. Tests]

docs.title: Orthogonality Rules
docs.text:
Before creating a utility, ensure it follows these rules:

  1. Operates over generic T — no imports from environments or relations.
  2. Environments do not import utilities — a Canvas2D doesn't know mapping exists.
  3. Does not own data meaning — it processes data supplied to it.
  4. Individually usable — a Domain Engine chooses whether to compose it.
  5. No mandatory dependencies — importing the utility module must not make it required by any environment.

If your utility needs to know about Canvas2D objects, it's not a utility — it's domain logic that belongs in a Domain Engine.

docs.title: Step 1: Directory Structure
docs.text:
src/domain_foundation/utilities/
└── mapping/
    ├── mod.rs          # Module declarations and re-exports
    └── mapper.rs      # Mapper trait, FnMapper, free functions

docs.title: mapper.rs
docs.text:
//! Mapping utility: transform items from one type to another.

/// A criterion that transforms an item of type `T` into type `U`.
///
/// Implementations are composable. The Domain Engine provides
/// the mapping function; the utility provides the mechanism.
pub trait Mapper<T, U> {
    /// Transform `item` into a new value.
    fn map(&self, item: &T) -> U;
}

docs.title: Step 3: Closure Wrapper
docs.text:
Add to mapper.rs:

/// Closure-based mapper.
pub struct FnMapper<F, P = (), R = ()> {
    f: F,
    _marker: std::marker::PhantomData<fn(&P) -> R>,
}

impl<F, P, R> FnMapper<F, P, R>
where
    F: Fn(&P) -> R,
{
    pub fn new(f: F) -> Self {
        Self {
            f,
            _marker: std::marker::PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

impl<T, U, F> Mapper<T, U> for FnMapper<F, T, U>
where
    T: ?Sized,
    F: Fn(&T) -> U,
{
    fn map(&self, item: &T) -> U {
        (self.f)(item)
    }
}

impl<F, P, R> std::fmt::Debug for FnMapper<F, P, R> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "FnMapper(..)")
    }
}

docs.title: Step 4: Free Functions
docs.text:
Add to mapper.rs:

/// Create a mapper from a closure.
pub fn mapper<T, U, F: Fn(&T) -> U>(f: F) -> FnMapper<F, T, U> {
    FnMapper::new(f)
}

/// Map all items in a slice, returning owned values.
pub fn map_all<T, U, M: Mapper<T, U>>(items: &[T], mapper: &M) -> Vec<U> {
    items.iter().map(|item| mapper.map(item)).collect()
}

/// Map a single item.
pub fn map_one<T, U, M: Mapper<T, U>>(item: &T, mapper: &M) -> U {
    mapper.map(item)
}

/// Map and filter: only keep non-None results.
pub fn map_filter<T, U, M: Mapper<T, Option<U>>>(items: &[T], mapper: &M) -> Vec<U> {
    items
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|item| mapper.map(item))
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn mapper_works_with_environment_data() {
    use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::{
        Canvas, Object, Transform, Vec2,
    };

    let mut canvas = Canvas::new();
    canvas.create_object(Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(10.0, 20.0)));
    canvas.create_object(Transform::from_translation(Vec2::new(30.0, 40.0)));

    // Map Canvas2D objects to position strings — without importing mapping into Canvas2D
    let objects: Vec<Object> = canvas.iter().copied().collect();
    let positions = map_all(&objects, &mapper(|obj: &Object| {
        format!("{:.1}, {:.1}", obj.transform.translation.x, obj.transform.translation.y)
    }));

    assert_eq!(positions.len(), 2);
    assert!(positions.contains(&"10.0, 20.0".to_string()));
    assert!(positions.contains(&"30.0, 40.0".to_string()));
}

docs.title: Using the Utility with Environment Data
docs.text:
The key pattern: the Domain Engine bridges environments and utilities:

// Domain Engine code (not foundation code)

use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::Object;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::utilities::mapping::*;

fn collect_positions(canvas: &Canvas) -> Vec<String> {
    let objects: Vec<Object> = canvas.iter().copied().collect();
    map_all(&objects, &mapper(|obj: &Object| {
        format!("{}, {}", obj.transform.translation.x, obj.transform.translation.y)
    }))
}

The Canvas2D environment doesn't know mapping exists. The mapping utility doesn't know Canvas2D exists. The Domain Engine bridges them.

docs.title: When to Create a Utility vs Domain Engine Code
docs.text:
Criterion Utility Domain Engine code Works with any T ✅ ❌ (specific types) No imports from environments ✅ ❌ (imports environment types) Reusable across applications ✅ ❌ (application-specific) Generic trait + closure wrapper ✅ ❌ (concrete logic) Could be published as a separate crate ✅ ❌

If your code only makes sense for one application (e.g., "format Canvas2D objects for display"), it's Domain Engine code, not a utility.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• Directory structure created (utilities/mapping/)
  • utilities/mod.rs updated with pub mod mapping;
  • Trait: Mapper<T, U>
  • Closure wrapper: FnMapper<F>
  • Free functions: mapper(), map_all(), map_one(), map_filter()
  • mod.rs re-exports
  • Tests: basic + struct + environment data
  • main.rs updated with test module
  • No imports from environments or relations in utility code

docs.title: Creating Relation Definitions
docs.text:
This guide shows how to define relations between properties, write effect closures, set priorities and propagation modes, register them, and evaluate changes.

We'll define a "width affects position" relation: when object A's width changes, object B's x-position updates to stay aligned.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[1. Define endpoints] --> B[2. Write effect closure]
    B --> C[3. Set trigger, propagation, priority]
    C --> D[4. Register with RelationRegistry]
    D --> E[5. Populate ValueStore]
    E --> F[6. Propagate from changed source]
    F --> G[7. Read results]

docs.title: Key Concept: Mechanism vs Meaning
docs.text:
Layer Responsibility Foundation Store, find, evaluate, propagate relations Domain Engine Define which relations exist, what changes, what effect occurs

The relation system never inspects what an effect closure does. It calls the closure and applies the outcome.

docs.title: Step 1: Define Endpoints
docs.text:
Endpoints identify which property on which object is the source and target:

use app_shell::domain_foundation::relations::*;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::relations::definition::*;

// Object A, property 0 (e.g., "width")
let source = Endpoint::source(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0));

// Object B, property 0 (e.g., "x_position")
let target = Endpoint::target(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0));

PropertyId is opaque — the foundation doesn't know what "width" or "x_position" means. The Domain Engine maps its environment's properties to PropertyId values.

docs.title: Mapping environment objects to PropertyIds
docs.text:
// Domain Engine code: map Canvas2D objects to relation properties
fn width_property(obj_id: ObjectId) -> PropertyId {
    PropertyId::new(obj_id, 0)   // property index 0 = "width"
}

fn x_position_property(obj_id: ObjectId) -> PropertyId {
    PropertyId::new(obj_id, 1)   // property index 1 = "x_position"
}

The foundation doesn't know these mappings. The Domain Engine maintains them.

docs.title: Step 2: Write the Effect Closure
docs.text:
The effect closure receives an EffectContext and returns an EffectOutcome:

use std::sync::Arc;

let effect: EffectFn = Arc::new(|ctx: &EffectContext| {
    // ctx.source_value is the new value of the source property
    // ctx.target_value is the current value of the target property

    // "When width changes, set B's x_position to the same value"
    EffectOutcome::Apply(ctx.source_value.clone())
});

docs.title: What the closure receives
docs.text:
pub struct EffectContext<'a> {
    pub relation_id: RelationId,
    pub source: &'a PropertyId,
    pub target: &'a PropertyId,
    pub source_value: &'a PropertyValue,   // New source value
    pub target_value: &'a PropertyValue,   // Current target value
}

docs.title: Effect outcomes
docs.text: Outcome When to use Behavior Apply(value) Compute and write a new target value Value written to store, cascade if Cascading NoChange Decide not to change the target Nothing happens, no cascade Invalidate Mark target as dirty without computing Step recorded, cascade if Cascading

docs.title: Example: conditional effect
docs.text:
// Only propagate if the source value is positive
let effect = Arc::new(|ctx: &EffectContext| {
    if let PropertyValue::Int(v) = ctx.source_value {
        if *v > 0 {
            EffectOutcome::Apply(PropertyValue::Int(*v + 10))
        } else {
            EffectOutcome::NoChange
        }
    } else {
        EffectOutcome::NoChange
    }
});

docs.title: Example: derived value
docs.text:
// Target = source * 2 + target's current value
let effect = Arc::new(|ctx: &EffectContext| {
    match (ctx.source_value, ctx.target_value) {
        (PropertyValue::Int(src), PropertyValue::Int(tgt)) => {
            EffectOutcome::Apply(PropertyValue::Int(src * 2 + tgt))
        }
        _ => EffectOutcome::NoChange,
    }
});

docs.title: Example: invalidation (lazy recomputation)
docs.text:
// Don't compute the new value — just mark the target as dirty
let effect = Arc::new(|_ctx: &EffectContext| {
    EffectOutcome::Invalidate
});

A later relation with Trigger::OnInvalidation can compute the actual value.

docs.title: Step 3: Set Trigger, Propagation, Priority
docs.text:
Use the builder:

let definition = RelationDefinitionBuilder::new(source, target)
    .trigger(Trigger::OnChange)           // Fire when source changes
    .propagation(PropagationMode::Direct)  // Don't cascade
    .priority(10)                          // Fire before priority-0 relations
    .effect(effect)
    .build();

docs.title: Trigger options
docs.text: Trigger When the relation fires OnChange Any time the source property value changes OnInitialSet Only the first time the source is set OnInvalidation When the source is marked dirty (via Invalidate outcome)

docs.title: Propagation options
docs.text:
Mode Behavior Direct Apply effect to target, stop Cascading Apply effect, then re-evaluate relations whose source is the target

Use Cascading when changing the target should trigger further relations. Use Direct when the target is a leaf (no relations read from it).

docs.title: Priority
docs.text:
Higher priority fires first when multiple relations share the same source:

// Priority 100 fires before priority 0
// If both write to the same target, the lower priority (last to fire) wins
.priority(100)

docs.title: Step 4: Register
docs.text:
let mut registry = RelationRegistry::new();
let relation_id = registry.register(definition);

// The registry stores the definition and indexes it by source/target
// for fast lookup during evaluation
assert!(registry.contains(relation_id));
assert_eq!(registry.len(), 1);

docs.title: Step 5: Populate the Value Store
docs.text:
The EvaluationContext owns a ValueStore. Set the current property values before propagating:

let mut ctx = EvaluationContext::new(&registry);

// Set the source's new value
ctx.set_value(
    PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0),  // Object A, property 0
    PropertyValue::Int(42),                // New width
);

// Set the target's current value (needed for the effect closure)
ctx.set_value(
    PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0),  // Object B, property 0
    PropertyValue::Int(0),                // Current x_position
);

docs.title: Step 6: Propagate
docs.text:
let steps = ctx.propagate_from(
    PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0),  // The changed source
).unwrap();

// steps: Vec<PropagationStep>
// Each step has: relation_id, target, outcome
assert_eq!(steps.len(), 1);
assert!(matches!(steps[0].outcome, EffectOutcome::Apply(_)));

docs.title: Step 7: Read Results
docs.text:
After propagation, read the updated target value:

let target_value = ctx.get_value(
    PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0),
);
assert_eq!(target_value, &PropertyValue::Int(42));

If you implement PropertyValueSink, the evaluation engine can write results directly back to your Domain Engine state:

impl PropertyValueSink for MyDomainState {
    fn set_property_value(&mut self, property: PropertyId, value: PropertyValue) {
        // Write to actual environment state
        if property.property == 0 {
            // It's the "width" property — update the canvas object
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Cascading Example
docs.text:
Define a chain: A → B → C:

// A.p0 → B.p0 (cascading, copy value)
registry.register(
    RelationDefinitionBuilder::new(
        Endpoint::source(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0)),
        Endpoint::target(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0)),
    )
    .propagation(PropagationMode::Cascading)
    .effect(Arc::new(|ctx| EffectOutcome::Apply(ctx.source_value.clone())))
    .build(),
);

// B.p0 → C.p0 (cascading, add 1)
registry.register(
    RelationDefinitionBuilder::new(
        Endpoint::source(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0)),
        Endpoint::target(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(3), 0)),
    )
    .propagation(PropagationMode::Cascading)
    .effect(Arc::new(|ctx| {
        if let PropertyValue::Int(v) = ctx.source_value {
            EffectOutcome::Apply(PropertyValue::Int(*v + 1))
        } else {
            EffectOutcome::NoChange
        }
    }))
    .build(),
);

// Propagate: A=100 → B=100 → C=101
ctx.set_value(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0), PropertyValue::Int(100));
ctx.set_value(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0), PropertyValue::Int(0));
ctx.set_value(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(3), 0), PropertyValue::Int(0));

let steps = ctx.propagate_from(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0)).unwrap();
assert_eq!(steps.len(), 2);
assert_eq!(ctx.get_value(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(2), 0)), &PropertyValue::Int(100));
assert_eq!(ctx.get_value(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(3), 0)), &PropertyValue::Int(101));

docs.title: Batch Propagation
docs.text:
When multiple properties change at once, batch them:

ctx.begin_batch();
ctx.set_value(prop_a, PropertyValue::Int(42));
ctx.set_value(prop_b, PropertyValue::Text("hello".into()));

let steps = ctx.commit_batch().unwrap();
// Both changes propagated, deduplicated (each source fires once)

Use rollback_batch() to discard accumulated changes without propagating.

docs.title: Bridging Environment State
docs.text:
For tight integration, implement PropertyValueSource on your Domain Engine state:

use app_shell::domain_foundation::relations::evaluation::PropertyValueSource;

struct DomainState {
    canvas: Canvas,
}

impl PropertyValueSource for DomainState {
    fn get_property_value(&self, property: PropertyId) -> PropertyValue {
        // Map PropertyId to actual environment state
        let obj = self.canvas.get(/* map to ObjectId */);
        match property.property {
            0 => PropertyValue::Float(/* obj width */),
            1 => PropertyValue::Float(/* obj x_position */),
            _ => PropertyValue::None,
        }
    }
}

Use SourcedValueStore to let the evaluation engine read from your state:

use app_shell::domain_foundation::relations::evaluation::SourcedValueStore;

let store = SourcedValueStore::new(domain_state);
let value = store.get(PropertyId::new(ObjectId::new(1), 0));
// Reads from domain_state.get_property_value(...)

docs.title: Serialization Note
docs.text:
RelationDefinition's effect field is #[serde(skip, default = "default_effect")]. When deserializing, the effect is a no-op closure. The Domain Engine must re-register the real effect after loading:

// After deserialization
let mut registry: RelationRegistry = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();

// Re-register effects (the definitions are there, but effects are no-ops)
for id in registry.relations_ids() {
    let def = registry.get_definition(id).unwrap();
    let real_effect = my_effect_for(def.source, def.target);
    registry.update_effect(id, real_effect);  // Hypothetical method
}

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• Endpoints defined (Endpoint::source / Endpoint::target)
  • Effect closure written (returns EffectOutcome)
  • Trigger set (OnChange, OnInitialSet, OnInvalidation)
  • Propagation mode set (Direct or Cascading)
  • Priority set (if multiple relations share a source)
  • Definition built via RelationDefinitionBuilder
  • Registered with RelationRegistry
  • Values populated in EvaluationContext
  • propagate_from() called
  • Results read from get_value()
  • Tests written (propagation, cascade, cycle, batch)

docs.title: Creating Command Handlers
docs.text:
This guide shows how to create an App Engine CommandHandler for a new environment, bridging domain operations to the App Engine's command execution, history, and event systems.

We'll create a TableCommandHandler as a concrete example.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    USER[User / API / Plugin] -->|Command| CE[CommandExecutor]
    CE -->|dispatches| CH[CommandHandler]
    CH -->|extracts op from| CI[CommandInput]
    CH -->|applies to| ENV[Environment]
    CH -->|records in| HIST[HistoryStore]
    CH -->|publishes| EVT[EventBus]
    CH -->|returns| CR[CommandResult]

docs.title: What is a Command Handler?
docs.text:
A CommandHandler is the bridge between the App Engine's generic command system and a specific environment. It:

  1. Receives a CommandInput containing a type-erased operation
  2. Extracts the operation (e.g., TableOperation)
  3. Applies it to the environment (via Arc<Mutex<Env>>)
  4. Records a HistoryEntry via EngineRef
  5. Publishes an Event via EngineRef
  6. Returns a CommandResult with the outcome

The App Engine's CommandExecutor dispatches commands by name to registered handlers. The App Engine never inspects the operation — it passes the CommandInput opaquely.

docs.title: The CommandHandler Trait
docs.text:
pub trait CommandHandler: Send + Sync {
    fn execute(
        &self,
        input: &CommandInput,
        context: &CommandContext,
        engine: &EngineRef,
    ) -> Result<CommandResult, CommandError>;
}
Parameter Type Purpose input &CommandInput Type-erased operation payload context &CommandContext Execution context (session, etc.) engine &EngineRef Read-only access to App Engine subsystems

The trait takes &self (immutable), so handlers must use interior mutability (Arc<Mutex<Env>>) to mutate the environment.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Handler Struct
docs.text:
// src/domain_engine/operations/table_command_handler.rs

use crate::app_engine::capabilities::engine_ref::EngineRef;
use crate::app_engine::commands::command::CommandInput;
use crate::app_engine::commands::command_context::CommandContext;
use crate::app_engine::commands::command_definition::CommandDefinition;
use crate::app_engine::commands::command_executor::CommandHandler;
use crate::app_engine::commands::command_result::CommandResult;
use crate::app_engine::errors::command_error::CommandError;
use crate::app_engine::events::event::Event;
use crate::app_engine::history::history_entry::HistoryEntry;
use crate::domain_foundation::environments::table::{
    Table, TableOperation, TableOutcome,
};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

pub struct TableCommandHandler {
    table: Arc<Mutex<Table>>,
}

impl TableCommandHandler {
    pub fn new(table: Arc<Mutex<Table>>) -> Self {
        Self { table }
    }

    pub fn definition() -> CommandDefinition {
        CommandDefinition::new(
            "table.operation",
            "Table Operation",
            "Applies a TableOperation to the table environment.",
        )
    }
}

docs.title: Step 2: Implement CommandHandler
docs.text:
impl CommandHandler for TableCommandHandler {
    fn execute(
        &self,
        input: &CommandInput,
        _context: &CommandContext,
        engine: &EngineRef,
    ) -> Result<CommandResult, CommandError> {
        // 1. Extract the operation from typed input
        let operation = input
            .get::<TableOperation>()
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                CommandError::ExecutionFailed(
                    "expected TableOperation in CommandInput".to_string(),
                )
            })?
            .clone();

        // 2. Apply to the shared table (lock + mutate)
        let outcome = {
            let mut table = self
                .table
                .lock()
                .map_err(|e| CommandError::ExecutionFailed(format!("table lock: {e}")))?;
            operation
                .clone()
                .apply(&mut table)
                .map_err(|e| CommandError::ExecutionFailed(e.to_string()))?
        };

        // 3. Record in history via EngineRef
        let entry_name = match &operation {
            TableOperation::InsertRow { .. } => "table.insert_row",
            TableOperation::InsertColumn { .. } => "table.insert_column",
            TableOperation::RemoveRow { .. } => "table.remove_row",
            TableOperation::RemoveColumn { .. } => "table.remove_column",
            TableOperation::SetCellValue { .. } => "table.set_cell_value",
            TableOperation::ClearCell { .. } => "table.clear_cell",
            TableOperation::MoveRow { .. } => "table.move_row",
            TableOperation::MoveColumn { .. } => "table.move_column",
            TableOperation::RenameRow { .. } => "table.rename_row",
            TableOperation::RenameColumn { .. } => "table.rename_column",
            TableOperation::MergeCells { .. } => "table.merge_cells",
            TableOperation::UnmergeCells { .. } => "table.unmerge_cells",
            TableOperation::ClearTable => "table.clear",
        };
        engine
            .history_store
            .append(HistoryEntry::new(entry_name).undoable());

        // 4. Publish event via EngineRef
        let event_name = match &outcome {
            TableOutcome::RowInserted { .. } => "table.row.inserted",
            TableOutcome::ColumnInserted { .. } => "table.column.inserted",
            TableOutcome::RowRemoved { .. } => "table.row.removed",
            TableOutcome::ColumnRemoved { .. } => "table.column.removed",
            TableOutcome::CellValueSet { .. } => "table.cell.value_set",
            TableOutcome::CellCleared { .. } => "table.cell.cleared",
            TableOutcome::RowMoved { .. } => "table.row.moved",
            TableOutcome::ColumnMoved { .. } => "table.column.moved",
            TableOutcome::RowRenamed { .. } => "table.row.renamed",
            TableOutcome::ColumnRenamed { .. } => "table.column.renamed",
            TableOutcome::CellsMerged => "table.cells.merged",
            TableOutcome::CellsUnmerged => "table.cells.unmerged",
            TableOutcome::TableCleared => "table.cleared",
        };
        engine
            .event_bus
            .publish(&Event::new(event_name).with_source("table_command_handler"));

        // 5. Return the outcome as the command result
        Ok(CommandResult::success_with(outcome))
    }
}

docs.title: Step 3: Register the Handler
docs.text:
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use app_shell::app_engine::*;
use app_shell::domain_engine::operations::TableCommandHandler;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::table::Table;

// 1. Create shared environment state
let table = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Table::new()));

// 2. Create handler
let handler = TableCommandHandler::new(Arc::clone(&table));

// 3. Register with the App Engine's command executor
let mut engine: AppEngine = AppEngine::new()?;
engine.command_executor_mut().register(
    TableCommandHandler::definition(),
    Box::new(handler),
)?;

// 4. Start the engine
engine.initialize()?;
engine.start()?;

// 5. Execute a command
let cmd = Command::new(
    "table.operation",
    CommandContext::new(ExecutionId::new()),
    CommandInput::new(TableOperation::InsertRow { name: Some("Header".to_string()) }),
);
let result = engine.execute_command(&cmd)?;
assert!(result.is_success());

// 6. Verify
let table_guard = table.lock().unwrap();
assert_eq!(table_guard.row_count(), 1);

docs.title: Step 4: Update operations/mod.rs
docs.text:
// src/domain_engine/operations/mod.rs

pub mod canvas_command_handler;
pub mod layers_command_handler;
pub mod table_command_handler;           // ← ADD
pub mod timeline_command_handler;

pub use canvas_command_handler::CanvasCommandHandler;
pub use layers_command_handler::LayersCommandHandler;
pub use table_command_handler::TableCommandHandler;  // ← ADD
pub use timeline_command_handler::TimelineCommandHandler;

docs.title: EngineRef Capabilities
docs.text:
The EngineRef passed to execute() provides read-only access to:

Subsystem Access What handlers can do history_store &HistoryStore Append entries (&self method via Mutex) event_bus &EventBus Publish events (&self method) signal_bus &SignalBus Emit signals (&self method) resource_manager &ResourceManager Load resources config_store &ConfigStore Read configuration preferences &Preferences Read user preferences state_manager &StateManager<LifecycleState> Read state command_executor &CommandExecutor Check definitions (can't register new — & not &mut) scheduler &Scheduler Submit tasks

Handlers cannot: - Register new commands (executor is &, not &mut) - Modify state directly (state manager is read-only) - Access the Domain Engine (App Engine doesn't know about it)

docs.title: Shared State Pattern
docs.text:
The handler wraps Arc<Mutex<Environment>>. The same Arc must be shared with the DomainEngine (if used) so both see the same state:

// Create shared state
let table = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Table::new()));

// Register handler with the App Engine
let handler = TableCommandHandler::new(Arc::clone(&table));
engine.command_executor_mut().register(
    TableCommandHandler::definition(),
    Box::new(handler),
)?;

// The DomainEngine can also use the same Arc (if needed)
// Or the handler can be the sole access point

docs.title: Lock error handling
docs.text:
If the Mutex is poisoned (a previous thread panicked while holding the lock), lock() returns Err:

let mut table = self.table.lock()
    .map_err(|e| CommandError::ExecutionFailed(format!("table lock: {e}")))?;

The App Engine's panic isolation (catch_unwind) prevents panics from propagating, but a handler's panic inside the lock would still poison it. Convert to a CommandError and return it.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
#[test]
fn table_command_handler_executes_insert() {
    use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
    use app_shell::app_engine::commands::command::*;
    use app_shell::app_engine::commands::command_executor::CommandExecutor;
    use app_shell::app_engine::*;
    use app_shell::domain_engine::operations::TableCommandHandler;
    use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::table::*;

    let table = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Table::new()));
    let handler = TableCommandHandler::new(Arc::clone(&table));

    let mut executor = CommandExecutor::new();
    executor
        .register(TableCommandHandler::definition(), Box::new(handler))
        .unwrap();

    // Verify definition
    assert_eq!(TableCommandHandler::definition().id().as_str(), "table.operation");
    assert_eq!(TableCommandHandler::definition().name(), "Table Operation");

    // Apply operation directly (bypassing command executor for simplicity)
    let mut table_guard = table.lock().unwrap();
    let outcome = TableOperation::InsertRow { name: Some("Test".to_string()) }
        .apply(&mut table_guard)
        .unwrap();
    drop(table_guard);

    let table_guard = table.lock().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(table_guard.row_count(), 1);
}

docs.title: Available Command Handlers
docs.text:
Handler Definition ID Environment CanvasCommandHandler "canvas.operation" Canvas2D TimelineCommandHandler "timeline.operation" Timeline LayersCommandHandler "layers.operation" Layers

Follow the same pattern to create handlers for NodeGraph, Viewport3D, Table, and TextEditor.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• Handler struct created with Arc<Mutex<Env>> field
  • definition() returns CommandDefinition with unique id
  • CommandHandler::execute() implemented
  • Operation extracted from CommandInput::get::<Operation>()
  • Environment locked and operation applied
  • HistoryEntry appended via engine.history_store
  • Event published via engine.event_bus
  • CommandResult::success_with(outcome) returned
  • operations/mod.rs updated with module + re-export
  • Handler tested (definition + execution)
  • All operation/outcome variants covered in match arms

docs.title: Composition Patterns
docs.text: This guide explains how to compose environments — when to do it, how to do it, and what to avoid. The only composition in the foundation is NodeGraph owning a Canvas2D, but the pattern generalizes.

docs.title: What Composition Is
docs.text:
Composition means one environment owns an instance of another environment and delegates some operations to it. The composing environment handles its own domain semantics; the composed environment handles a separate concern.

flowchart LR
    subgraph NG[NodeGraph]
        GRAPH[Graph state<br/>nodes, ports, edges]
        C2D[Canvas2D<br/>objects, transforms]
    end

    CREATE[create_node] -->|creates graph node| GRAPH
    CREATE -->|creates canvas object| C2D
    MOVE[move_node] -->|spatial only| C2D
    CONNECT[connect] -->|graph only| GRAPH

docs.title: What Composition Is NOT
docs.text: Pattern Why not Shared base trait Environments don't share a base. Each owns its types. Interface inheritance No Environment trait to implement. Mixin / trait composition Environments are concrete structs, not trait-based. Dynamic dispatch Composition is static (owned fields), not dynamic. Universal ObjectId Each environment has its own id type (ObjectId, TrackId, LayerId, etc.).

docs.title: When to Compose
docs.text:
Compose when:

  1. Two genuinely separate concerns exist — e.g., graph connectivity and spatial placement are different problems.
  2. One concern naturally owns the other — NodeGraph needs spatial placement; it owns a Canvas.
  3. Operations on one don't affect the other — moving a node doesn't change edges; connecting ports doesn't change positions.
  4. The composed environment is useful on its own — Canvas2D works independently of NodeGraph.

Don't compose when:

  • The "composition" is just sharing types (use the same types directly).
  • The two environments are always used together (consider merging).
  • One environment is just a helper (it's a utility, not a composition).

docs.title: Step 1: Own the Composed Environment
docs.text:
pub struct NodeGraph {
    nodes: HashMap<NodeId, Node>,
    ports: HashMap<PortId, Port>,
    edges: HashMap<EdgeId, Edge>,

    // ← COMPOSED: NodeGraph owns a Canvas2D instance
    canvas: Canvas,

    next_node_id: u64,
    next_port_id: u64,
    next_edge_id: u64,
}

docs.title: Step 2: Link Identities
docs.text:
Each node in the composing environment stores a reference to its spatial representation:

pub struct Node {
    pub id: NodeId,
    pub name: String,

    // ← LINK: references a Canvas2D ObjectId
    pub canvas_object: Option<ObjectId>,

    pub(crate) input_ports: Vec<PortId>,
    pub(crate) output_ports: Vec<PortId>,
}

The link is Option<ObjectId> because a node might not have spatial placement (purely logical node).

docs.title: Step 3: Delegate Operations
docs.text:
When creating a node, create both the graph entity and the spatial entity:

pub fn create_node(&mut self, name: String, transform: Transform) -> NodeId {
    let id = NodeId::from_raw(self.next_node_id);
    self.next_node_id += 1;

    // Create spatial representation (delegated to Canvas2D)
    let canvas_id = self.canvas.create_object(transform);

    // Create graph entity (owned by NodeGraph)
    let node = Node::new(id, name, Some(canvas_id));
    self.nodes.insert(id, node);
    id
}

When moving a node, delegate to Canvas2D:

pub fn move_node(&mut self, id: NodeId, translation: Vec2) -> Result<Transform, NodeGraphError> {
    let node = self.nodes.get(&id)
        .ok_or(NodeGraphError::NodeNotFound { id })?;

    // Delegate spatial operation to Canvas2D
    let obj_id = node.canvas_object
        .ok_or(NodeGraphError::NoCanvasObject { id })?;

    Ok(self.canvas.set_translation(obj_id, translation)?)
}

docs.title: Step 4: Separate Concerns
docs.text:
Graph operations don't touch the canvas; spatial operations don't touch the graph:

// Graph-only: connect ports — doesn't touch canvas
pub fn connect(&mut self, source: PortId, target: PortId) -> Result<EdgeId, NodeGraphError> {
    // ... validation ...
    let id = EdgeId::from_raw(self.next_edge_id);
    self.edges.insert(id, Edge::new(id, source, target));
    Ok(id)
    // No canvas involvement
}

// Spatial-only: move node — doesn't touch edges
pub fn move_node(&mut self, id: NodeId, translation: Vec2) -> Result<Transform, NodeGraphError> {
    // Only touches canvas, never touches edges or ports
}

docs.title: Step 5: Cascade Removes
docs.text:
When removing a node, cascade to both concerns:

pub fn remove_node(&mut self, id: NodeId) -> Result<NodeRemovedData, NodeGraphError> {
    let node = self.nodes.get(&id)
        .ok_or(NodeGraphError::NodeNotFound { id })?;

    // 1. Collect ports (graph concern)
    let port_ids: Vec<PortId> = node.input_ports.iter()
        .chain(node.output_ports.iter())
        .copied()
        .collect();

    // 2. Collect connected edges (graph concern)
    let edge_ids: Vec<EdgeId> = self.edges.iter()
        .filter(|(_, e)| port_ids.contains(&e.source) || port_ids.contains(&e.target))
        .map(|(eid, _)| *eid)
        .collect();

    // 3. Remove canvas object (spatial concern — delegated to Canvas2D)
    let canvas_object = match node.canvas_object {
        Some(obj_id) => Some(self.canvas.remove_object(obj_id)?),
        None => None,
    };

    // 4. Remove edges (graph concern)
    let mut removed_edges = Vec::new();
    for eid in &edge_ids {
        if let Some(e) = self.edges.remove(eid) {
            removed_edges.push(e);
        }
    }

    // 5. Remove ports (graph concern)
    let mut removed_ports = Vec::new();
    for pid in &port_ids {
        if let Some(p) = self.ports.remove(pid) {
            removed_ports.push(p);
        }
    }

    // 6. Remove node (graph concern)
    let removed_node = self.nodes.remove(&id)
        .ok_or(NodeGraphError::NodeNotFound { id })?;

    Ok(NodeRemovedData {
        node: removed_node,
        ports: removed_ports,
        edges: removed_edges,
        canvas_object,
    })
}

docs.title: Step 6: Expose the Composed Environment
docs.text:
Provide a getter so external code can inspect spatial state:

/// Borrow the internal Canvas2D (read-only).
pub fn canvas(&self) -> &Canvas {
    &self.canvas
}

This allows tests and Domain Engines to verify spatial state without going through NodeGraph methods.

docs.title: Step 7: Clear Both
docs.text:
pub fn clear(&mut self) {
    self.nodes.clear();
    self.ports.clear();
    self.edges.clear();
    self.canvas.clear();  // ← Clear composed environment too
}

docs.title: Example: Composing Timeline into a New Environment
docs.text:
Suppose you want a Storyboard environment that composes Timeline for temporal editing plus its own panel layout:

pub struct Storyboard {
    panels: HashMap<PanelId, Panel>,
    timeline: Timeline,  // ← Composed

    next_panel_id: u64,
}

pub struct Panel {
    pub id: PanelId,
    pub name: String,
    pub clip_id: Option<ClipId>,  // ← Link to Timeline
}

impl Storyboard {
    pub fn create_panel(&mut self, name: String) -> PanelId {
        let id = PanelId::from_raw(self.next_panel_id);
        self.next_panel_id += 1;
        self.panels.insert(id, Panel::new(id, name));
        id
    }

    pub fn link_to_clip(&mut self, panel_id: PanelId, clip_id: ClipId) -> Result<(), StoryboardError> {
        let panel = self.panels.get_mut(&panel_id)
            .ok_or(StoryboardError::PanelNotFound { id: panel_id })?;
        panel.clip_id = Some(clip_id);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn timeline(&self) -> &Timeline {
        &self.timeline  // ← Expose composed environment
    }

    pub fn timeline_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Timeline {
        &mut self.timeline
    }
}

The Storyboard handles panel layout; the Timeline handles temporal organization. They're separate concerns linked by clip_id.

docs.title: 1. Shared base trait
docs.text:
// ❌ DON'T
pub trait Environment {
    fn len(&self) -> usize;
    fn clear(&mut self);
}

impl Environment for Canvas { ... }
impl Environment for Timeline { ... }

Canvas2D's len() counts objects; Timeline's counts tracks. Forcing them into a shared trait creates a meaningless abstraction.

docs.title: 2. Universal identity
docs.text:
// ❌ DON'T
pub struct UniversalObjectId(u64);

// Canvas, Timeline, Layers all use UniversalObjectId

Each environment has different identity semantics. ObjectId and TrackId are different types on purpose.

docs.title: 3. Coupled operations
docs.text:
// ❌ DON'T
// Moving a node also changes graph connectivity
pub fn move_node_and_reconnect(&mut self, id: NodeId, pos: Vec2) {
    self.canvas.set_translation(id.canvas_object, pos);
    self.edges.reconnect_based_on_proximity(pos);  // ← Coupling!
}

Spatial and graph operations should be separate. Coupling them makes the composition fragile.

docs.title: 4. Importing the composed environment's types externally
docs.text:
// ❌ DON'T
// External code needs to know NodeGraph uses Canvas2D internally
let transform = graph.canvas().get(obj_id).unwrap().transform;

Instead, provide dedicated methods:

// ✅ DO
let transform = graph.node_transform(node_id)?;

docs.title: Testing Composition
docs.text:
Test that spatial and graph operations are independent:

#[test]
fn move_node_doesnt_affect_graph() {
    let mut graph = NodeGraph::new();
    let a = graph.create_node("A".into(), Transform::identity());
    let b = graph.create_node("B".into(), Transform::identity());
    let out_a = graph.add_output_port(a, "out".into(), "f".into()).unwrap();
    let in_b = graph.add_input_port(b, "in".into(), "f".into()).unwrap();
    graph.connect(out_a, in_b).unwrap();

    let edge_count_before = graph.edge_count();

    // Move a node — should NOT affect edges
    graph.move_node(a, Vec2::new(100.0, 100.0)).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(graph.edge_count(), edge_count_before);
}

#[test]
fn connect_doesnt_affect_spatial() {
    let mut graph = NodeGraph::new();
    let a = graph.create_node("A".into(), Transform::identity());
    let b = graph.create_node("B".into(), Transform::identity());

    let transform_before = graph.node_transform(a).unwrap();

    let out_a = graph.add_output_port(a, "out".into(), "f".into()).unwrap();
    let in_b = graph.add_input_port(b, "in".into(), "f".into()).unwrap();
    graph.connect(out_a, in_b).unwrap();

    // Connecting should NOT change spatial state
    assert_eq!(graph.node_transform(a).unwrap(), transform_before);
}

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• Owning environment has a field of the composed type
  • Linking field on the composing type (Option<ComposedId>)
  • Create operation delegates to composed environment
  • Spatial operations delegate to composed environment
  • Graph/domain operations don't touch composed environment
  • Remove cascades to both concerns
  • Clear cascades to both concerns
  • Getter exposes composed environment (pub fn composed(&self) -> &Composed)
  • Tests verify independence of concerns

docs.title: Adding Serde Support
docs.text: This guide shows how to add serialization support to new or existing types in the Domain Foundation, including newtypes, structs, enums, and non-serializable fields.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[1. Enable serde feature] --> B[2. Add derive to newtypes]
    B --> C[3. Add derive to structs]
    C --> D[4. Add derive to enums]
    D --> E[5. Handle non-serializable fields]
    E --> F[6. Write round-trip tests]

docs.title: Enabling the Serde Feature
docs.text:
The Domain Foundation uses a Cargo feature flag for optional serde support:

# Cargo.toml
[features]
serde = ["dep:serde"]

[dependencies]
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"], optional = true }

When the serde feature is enabled, all types with conditional derives gain Serialize and Deserialize. When disabled, serde is not compiled — zero overhead.

docs.title: Conditional Derive Pattern
docs.text:
All serde derives use #[cfg_attr] so they're only active with the feature:

#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct MyType {
    pub field: i32,
}

Without the feature: only Debug, Clone, PartialEq are derived. With the feature: all four are derived.

docs.title: Step 1: Newtypes — serde(transparent)
docs.text:
Newtypes wrap a single value. Use transparent to serialize the inner value directly (not as a struct with one field):

#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(transparent))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct MyId(u64);

docs.title: JSON before and after
docs.text:
// Without transparent (treats as struct):
{"0": 42}

// With transparent (treats as inner value):
42

docs.title: When to use transparent
docs.text: Type Use transparent? Reason ObjectId(u64) ✅ Single field, serialize as u64 TrackId(u64) ✅ Same Position(u32) ✅ Same Time(f64) ✅ Same ClipId { raw: u64, track: TrackId } ❌ Multiple fields, serialize as struct CellId { row: RowId, column: ColumnId } ❌ Multiple fields

docs.title: Step 2: Structs — Derive on the Struct
docs.text:
For structs with public or private fields:

#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Default)]
pub struct MyEnvironment {
    objects: HashMap<MyId, MyObject>,  // Private field — serde accesses within module
    order: Vec<MyId>,
    next_id: u64,
}

Serde can access private fields within the same module (it generates code inside the module). No special attributes needed for private fields.

docs.title: Step 3: Enums — Derive on the Enum
docs.text:
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum MyOperation {
    Create { transform: MyTransform },
    Remove { id: MyId },
    Clear,
}

Each variant serializes as a struct with a tag:

// Create
{"Create": {"transform": {"translation": {"x": 1.0, "y": 2.0}, "rotation": 0.0, "scale": {"x": 1.0, "y": 1.0}}}}

// Remove
{"Remove": {"id": 0}}

// Clear
"Clear"

docs.title: Step 4: Non-Serializable Fields
docs.text: Some fields can't be serialized. Use #[serde(skip)] or #[serde(skip, default = "function")]:

docs.title: Closures (Arc<dyn Fn...>)
docs.text:
Closures can't be serialized. Skip the field and provide a custom default:

#[cfg(feature = "serde")]
fn default_effect() -> EffectFn {
    Arc::new(|_| EffectOutcome::NoChange)
}

#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct RelationDefinition {
    pub source: Endpoint,
    pub target: Endpoint,
    pub trigger: Trigger,
    pub propagation: PropagationMode,
    pub priority: i32,

    // ← Skip on serialize, use no-op on deserialize
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip, default = "default_effect"))]
    pub effect: EffectFn,
}

docs.title: AtomicU64
docs.text:
AtomicU64 doesn't implement Serialize or Deserialize. Skip it:

#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct RelationRegistry {
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip))]
    next_id: AtomicU64,  // ← Not serialized; deserializes as default (0)

    definitions: HashMap<RelationId, RelationDefinition>,
    by_source: HashMap<PropertyId, Vec<RelationId>>,
    by_target: HashMap<PropertyId, Vec<RelationId>>,
    graph: DependencyGraph,
}

After deserialization, next_id is 0. If existing definitions have ids >= 0, the next register() call will advance next_id past them. This works as long as you register new relations after deserialization.

docs.title: Mutex
docs.text: Mutex<T> doesn't implement Serialize/Deserialize. Types containing Mutex (like HistoryStore, EventBus, SignalBus) are not serializable. Don't add serde derives to them.

docs.title: Step 5: Field-Level Attributes
docs.text: Attribute When to use Effect #[serde(skip)] Field can't be serialized Field uses Default on deserialize #[serde(skip, default = "fn")] Field can't be serialized and Default isn't suitable Field uses custom function on deserialize #[serde(rename = "name")] JSON field name should differ from Rust name Renames in JSON #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] Optional field, omit from JSON when None Smaller JSON output

docs.title: HashMap<CellId, CellValue> in Table
docs.text:
serde_json requires string keys. CellId is a struct ({ row: RowId, column: ColumnId }), not a string:

// This fails with serde_json:
let json = serde_json::to_string(&table).unwrap();
// Error: "key must be a string"

Workarounds:

  1. Use bincode (binary format, supports struct keys):
[dev-dependencies]
bincode = "1"

let bytes = bincode::serialize(&table).unwrap();
let restored: Table = bincode::deserialize(&bytes).unwrap();
assert_eq!(table, restored);

  1. Custom serializer (convert CellId to a string like "r1c2")

  2. Skip the field (serialize only structure, not cells):

#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip))]
cells: HashMap<CellId, CellValue>,

docs.title: RelationDefinition::effect deserializes as no-op
docs.text:
Closures can't be serialized. After deserialization, effect is Arc::new(|_| EffectOutcome::NoChange). The Domain Engine must re-register the real effect:

// After deserializing a RelationRegistry
for id in registry.relation_ids() {
    let def = registry.get_definition(id).unwrap();
    let real_effect = my_effect_for(&def.source, &def.target);
    // Re-register with the real effect
    registry.unregister(id);
    registry.register(
        RelationDefinitionBuilder::new(def.source, def.target)
            .trigger(def.trigger)
            .propagation(def.propagation)
            .priority(def.priority)
            .effect(real_effect)
            .build(),
    );
}

docs.title: Step 6: Round-Trip Tests
docs.text:
Add serde_json as a dev-dependency:

[dev-dependencies]
serde_json = "1"

Create tests/domain_foundation_tests/serde_roundtrip_test.rs:

#[cfg(feature = "serde")]
#[test]
fn my_type_roundtrip() {
    let original = MyType { /* ... */ };

    let json = serde_json::to_string(&original).unwrap();
    let restored: MyType = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(original, restored);
}

docs.title: Update main.rs
docs.text:
#[cfg(feature = "serde")]
mod serde_roundtrip_test;

docs.title: What to test
docs.text: Type What survives round-trip Environment container All fields (objects, order, next_id) Operation enum All variants Outcome enum All variants with undo data Id newtypes The inner value Transform / Vec2 All components Error enum All variants

docs.title: Test with PartialEq
docs.text:
Round-trip tests rely on PartialEq to verify equality. Ensure the type derives PartialEq:

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]  // ← Required for assert_eq!
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
pub struct MyType { ... }

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
// Id newtype
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(transparent))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct MyId(u64);

// Data struct
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct MyObject {
    pub id: MyId,
    pub name: String,
    pub value: f64,
}

// Operation enum
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum MyOperation {
    Create { name: String, value: f64 },
    Remove { id: MyId },
    Clear,
}

// Outcome enum
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum MyOutcome {
    Created { id: MyId },
    Removed { object: MyObject },
    Cleared { count: usize },
}

// Container with non-serializable field
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Default)]
pub struct MyEnvironment {
    objects: HashMap<MyId, MyObject>,
    next_id: u64,
    // No Mutex, no AtomicU64, no closures — all serializable
}

// Error enum
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MyError {
    NotFound { id: MyId },
}

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• serde feature added to Cargo.toml (if new crate/module)
  • #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(...))] on every serializable type
  • #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(transparent))] on newtypes with single field
  • #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip))] on AtomicU64 fields
  • #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip, default = "fn"))] on closure fields
  • PartialEq derived on all types (for round-trip tests)
  • serde_json added as dev-dependency
  • Round-trip test added to serde_roundtrip_test.rs
  • main.rs updated with #[cfg(feature = "serde")] mod serde_roundtrip_test;
  • Known limitations documented (HashMap with struct keys, closure fields)
