docs.title: Writing Tests
docs.text: This guide covers the testing conventions, patterns, and categories used throughout the Domain Foundation. Follow these patterns when adding tests for new environments or operations.

docs.title: Test Organization
docs.text:
All Domain Foundation tests live under tests/domain_foundation_tests/ as submodules of a single test binary:

tests/
└── domain_foundation_tests/
    ├── main.rs                    ← Entry point: declares all submodules
    ├── canvas_2d_test.rs          ← Model tests
    ├── canvas_2d_operations_test.rs
    ├── ...
    ├── concurrency_test.rs
    ├── proptest_test.rs
    ├── stress_test.rs
    └── serde_roundtrip_test.rs

docs.title: Adding a new test file
docs.text:
1. Create tests/domain_foundation_tests/my_thing_test.rs
  2. Add mod my_thing_test; to main.rs
// tests/domain_foundation_tests/main.rs

mod canvas_2d_test;
mod canvas_2d_operations_test;
mod my_thing_test;  // ← ADD

docs.title: File naming convention
docs.text: Test files use the _test suffix: canvas_2d_test.rs, relation_propagation_test.rs. The module name in main.rs matches without the .rs extension.

docs.title: 1. Model Tests
docs.text:
Verify the environment's types, queries, and constraints:

#[test]
fn create_returns_unique_ids() {
    let mut env = MyEnvironment::new();
    let a = env.create(/* ... */);
    let b = env.create(/* ... */);
    assert_ne!(a, b);
}

#[test]
fn remove_returns_object() {
    let mut env = MyEnvironment::new();
    let id = env.create(/* ... */);
    let removed = env.remove(id).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(removed.id, id);
}

#[test]
fn clear_preserves_id_counter() {
    let mut env = MyEnvironment::new();
    let first = env.create(/* ... */);
    env.clear();
    let second = env.create(/* ... */);
    assert_ne!(first, second);  // Ids don't collide
}

docs.title: 2. Operation Tests
docs.text:
Verify each operation variant, error cases, and composition:

#[test]
fn create_operation_adds_object() {
    let mut env = MyEnvironment::new();
    let outcome = MyOperation::Create { /* ... */ }
        .apply(&mut env)
        .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(outcome, MyOutcome::Created { .. }));
    assert_eq!(env.len(), 1);
}

#[test]
fn operation_on_missing_id_fails() {
    let mut env = MyEnvironment::new();
    let fake_id = MyId::from_raw(999);
    let err = MyOperation::Remove { id: fake_id }
        .apply(&mut env)
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(err, MyError::NotFound { .. }));
}

#[test]
fn sequence_of_operations_composes() {
    let mut env = MyEnvironment::new();
    // Execute multiple operations
    MyOperation::Create { /* ... */ }.apply(&mut env).unwrap();
    MyOperation::Create { /* ... */ }.apply(&mut env).unwrap();
    // Verify final state
    assert_eq!(env.len(), 2);
}

docs.title: 3. Integration Tests (DomainEngine + App Engine)
docs.text:
Verify undo/redo, transactions, events:

#[test]
fn undo_restores_state() {
    let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();
    let id = match engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create { /* ... */ }).unwrap() {
        CanvasOutcome::Created { id } => id,
        _ => unreachable!(),
    };
    engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Move { id, /* ... */ }).unwrap();

    engine.undo().unwrap();  // Undo move
    assert_eq!(engine.canvas().get(id).unwrap().transform.translation, Vec2::new(0.0, 0.0));
}

#[test]
fn transaction_undoes_all_at_once() {
    let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();
    engine.begin_transaction();
    engine.execute_canvas(Create { /* ... */ }).unwrap();
    engine.execute_canvas(Create { /* ... */ }).unwrap();
    engine.commit_transaction();

    engine.undo().unwrap();  // Undoes both
    assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);
}

docs.title: 4. Composition Tests
docs.text:
Verify architectural boundaries:

#[test]
fn my_env_works_without_others() {
    let mut env = MyEnvironment::new();
    let id = env.create(/* ... */);
    assert!(env.contains(id));
}

#[test]
fn composed_env_separate_concerns() {
    let mut graph = NodeGraph::new();
    let n = graph.create_node("N".into(), Transform::identity());

    // Spatial operation doesn't affect graph
    graph.move_node(n, Vec2::new(50.0, 50.0)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(graph.edge_count(), 0);  // No edges affected
}

docs.title: 5. Concurrency Tests
docs.text:
Verify Send + Sync and thread-safe access:

#[test]
fn my_env_is_send_sync() {
    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
    assert_send_sync::<MyEnvironment>();
}

#[test]
fn my_env_shared_across_threads() {
    let env = Arc::new(Mutex::new(MyEnvironment::new()));
    let handles: Vec<_> = (0..4).map(|i| {
        let env = Arc::clone(&env);
        thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut e = env.lock().unwrap();
            e.create(/* ... */);
        })
    }).collect();
    for h in handles { h.join().unwrap(); }
    assert_eq!(env.lock().unwrap().len(), 4);
}

docs.title: 6. Property-Based Tests (proptest)
docs.text:
Verify invariants across random inputs:

use proptest::prelude::*;

proptest! {
    #[test]
    fn create_then_remove_preserves_empty(
        count in 0u32..20u32
    ) {
        let mut env = MyEnvironment::new();
        let mut ids = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..count {
            ids.push(env.create(/* ... */));
        }
        for id in &ids {
            env.remove(*id).unwrap();
        }
        prop_assert!(env.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn undo_redo_preserves_state(
        ops in prop::collection::vec(create_op_strategy(), 1..10)
    ) {
        let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();
        let len_before = engine.canvas().len();
        for op in &ops {
            let _ = engine.execute(op.clone());
        }
        let len_after = engine.canvas().len();
        // Undo all
        while engine.can_undo() { engine.undo().unwrap(); }
        // Redo all
        while engine.can_redo() { engine.redo().unwrap(); }
        prop_assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), len_after);
    }
}

docs.title: The Struct-Literal-in-Match Rule
docs.text:
Most common test compilation error

Never write match Foo::Variant { fields }.method() { ... }.

The parser sees match EXPR { and can't tell if the { is the struct literal or the match body.

docs.title: Wrong
docs.text:
// ❌ Won't compile
let id = match MyOperation::Create { name: "x".into() }
    .apply(&mut env)
    .unwrap()
{
    MyOutcome::Created { id } => id,
    _ => unreachable!(),
};

docs.title: Correct
docs.text:
// ✅ Bind to a variable first
let outcome = MyOperation::Create { name: "x".into() }
    .apply(&mut env)
    .unwrap();
let id = match outcome {
    MyOutcome::Created { id } => id,
    _ => unreachable!(),
};

This is the most common compilation error in the Domain Foundation test suite. Always bind the .apply().unwrap() result to a variable before matching.

docs.title: Using PartialEq for Assertions
docs.text:
All environment containers derive PartialEq. Use assert_eq! for value comparisons:

#[test]
fn partial_eq_works() {
    let mut a = Canvas::new();
    let mut b = Canvas::new();

    a.create_object(Transform::identity());
    b.create_object(Transform::identity());

    assert_eq!(a, b);  // Same content, same next_id
}

docs.title: When PartialEq fails
docs.text:
Two canvases with the same objects but different next_id are not equal:

let mut a = Canvas::new();
a.create_object(Transform::identity());  // next_id = 1
a.create_object(Transform::identity());  // next_id = 2
a.clear();                               // next_id still 2

let mut b = Canvas::new();
b.create_object(Transform::identity());  // next_id = 1

// a is empty (len=0), b has 1 object, but next_id differs
assert_ne!(a, b);  // a.next_id=2, b.next_id=1

docs.text:
When PartialEq fails due to next_id or id differences, compare specific fields:

assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len());
assert_eq!(a.get(id).unwrap().transform, b.get(id).unwrap().transform);

docs.title: Integrating with DomainEngine
docs.text:
This guide shows how to add a new environment to the DomainEngine — adding the field, getter, execute_* method, name helpers, error variant, and tests.

We'll use the Measurement environment from 01-creating-environment.md as a concrete example.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[1. Add environment field] --> B[2. Add DomainError variant]
    B --> C[3. Add From impl]
    C --> D[4. Add getter]
    D --> E[5. Add execute_xxx method]
    E --> F[6. Add name helpers]
    F --> G[7. Update new() and Default]
    G --> H[8. Add tests]

docs.title: What the DomainEngine Does
docs.text:
The DomainEngine wraps each environment with:

  1. History recording — every operation creates a HistoryEntry
  2. Event publication — every operation publishes an Event via EventBus
  3. Signal emission — every operation emits a Signal via SignalBus (if configured)
  4. Transaction support — entries marked with TransactionId for compound undo
  5. Auto-rollback — if execute_* fails during a transaction, the transaction is rolled back
  6. Dirty tracking — mark_saved() / is_dirty() based on history position

The DomainEngine does not define what operations mean — that's the environment's job via operation.apply(&mut env).

docs.title: Step 1: Add Environment Field
docs.text:
In src/domain_engine/mod.rs, add the field to the DomainEngine struct:

pub struct DomainEngine {
    // ... existing environments ...
    canvas: Canvas,
    timeline: Timeline,
    layers: Layers,
    node_graph: NodeGraph,
    table: Table,
    document: Document,
    scene: Scene,

    measurement: Measurement,  // ← ADD

    // ... App Engine integration ...
    history: HistoryStore,
    transaction_manager: TransactionManager,
    event_bus: EventBus,
    signal_bus: Option<Arc<SignalBus>>,
    active_transaction: Option<TransactionId>,
    transaction_start_position: usize,
    executed_canvas: Vec<ExecutedCanvasOperation>,
    saved_position: usize,
    max_history: usize,
    compound_depth: usize,
    events: Vec<Event>,
}

Add the import at the top of the file:

use crate::domain_foundation::environments::measurement::{
    Measurement, MeasurementError, MeasurementOperation, MeasurementOutcome,
};

docs.text:
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum DomainError {
    Canvas(CanvasError),
    Timeline(TimelineError),
    Layers(LayersError),
    NodeGraph(NodeGraphError),
    Table(TableError),
    TextEditor(TextEditorError),
    Viewport3D(Viewport3DError),

    Measurement(MeasurementError),  // ← ADD
}

docs.title: Step 3: Add From Impl
docs.text:
impl From<MeasurementError> for DomainError {
    fn from(e: MeasurementError) -> Self {
        Self::Measurement(e)
    }
}

Update the Display impl:

impl std::fmt::Display for DomainError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            DomainError::Canvas(e) => write!(f, "canvas: {e}"),
            DomainError::Timeline(e) => write!(f, "timeline: {e}"),
            // ... existing ...
            DomainError::Measurement(e) => write!(f, "measurement: {e}"),  // ← ADD
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Step 4: Add Getter
docs.text:
impl DomainEngine {
    // ... existing getters ...

    /// Measurement environment access.
    pub fn measurement(&self) -> &Measurement {
        &self.measurement
    }
}

docs.title: Step 5: Add execute_measurement Method
docs.text:
This is the core integration. Follow the same pattern as all other execute_* methods:

impl DomainEngine {
    // ... existing execute_* methods ...

    /// Execute a measurement operation with history, events, and signals.
    pub fn execute_measurement(
        &mut self,
        operation: MeasurementOperation,
    ) -> Result<MeasurementOutcome, DomainError> {
        // 1. Apply the operation to the environment
        let outcome = operation.clone().apply(&mut self.measurement)
            .map_err(|e| {
                let err: DomainError = e.into();
                self.check_auto_rollback(&err);  // Auto-rollback if in transaction
                err
            })?;

        // 2. Create a history entry
        let name = measurement_op_name(&operation);
        let mut entry = HistoryEntry::new(name).undoable();

        // 3. Mark with transaction id if active
        if let Some(tx_id) = self.active_transaction {
            entry = entry.with_transaction(tx_id);
        }
        self.history.append(entry);

        // 4. Publish event and emit signal
        self.publish(
            measurement_outcome_event(&outcome),
            measurement_outcome_signal(&outcome),
        );

        Ok(outcome)
    }
}

docs.title: What each step does
docs.text: Step What Why 1. Apply operation.apply(&mut env) Execute the operation on the environment 1b. Error map_err + check_auto_rollback If in transaction, rollback on failure 2. History HistoryEntry::new(name).undoable() Record for undo/redo 3. Transaction .with_transaction(tx_id) Group entries for compound undo 4. Publish self.publish(event_name, signal_name) Notify EventBus + SignalBus + accumulate

docs.title: Step 6: Add Name Helpers
docs.text:
Add private functions that map operations and outcomes to event/signal name strings:

fn measurement_op_name(op: &MeasurementOperation) -> &'static str {
    match op {
        MeasurementOperation::Create { .. } => "measurement.create",
        MeasurementOperation::Remove { .. } => "measurement.remove",
        MeasurementOperation::Rename { .. } => "measurement.rename",
        MeasurementOperation::MoveEndpoints { .. } => "measurement.move",
        MeasurementOperation::Clear => "measurement.clear",
    }
}

fn measurement_outcome_event(outcome: &MeasurementOutcome) -> &'static str {
    match outcome {
        MeasurementOutcome::Created { .. } => "measurement.created",
        MeasurementOutcome::Removed { .. } => "measurement.removed",
        MeasurementOutcome::Renamed { .. } => "measurement.renamed",
        MeasurementOutcome::Moved { .. } => "measurement.moved",
        MeasurementOutcome::Cleared { .. } => "measurement.cleared",
    }
}

fn measurement_outcome_signal(outcome: &MeasurementOutcome) -> &'static str {
    match outcome {
        MeasurementOutcome::Created { .. } => "measurement.created",
        MeasurementOutcome::Removed { .. } => "measurement.removed",
        _ => "measurement.changed",
    }
}

docs.title: Naming conventions
docs.text: Level Format Example History entry <env>.<action> measurement.create Event <env>.<entity>.<action> measurement.created Signal Same as event (or <env>.changed) measurement.created

docs.title: Step 8: Tests
docs.text:
Add to tests/domain_foundation_tests/domain_operation_integration_test.rs:

#[test]
fn execute_measurement_through_domain_engine() {
    use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::measurement::*;
    use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::Vec2;

    let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();

    let outcome = engine.execute_measurement(MeasurementOperation::Create {
        start: Vec2::new(0.0, 0.0),
        end: Vec2::new(10.0, 0.0),
        label: "Distance A".to_string(),
    }).unwrap();

    match outcome {
        MeasurementOutcome::Created { id } => {
            assert!(engine.measurement().contains(id));
        }
        other => panic!("expected Created, got {other:?}"),
    }

    // Event was published
    assert_eq!(engine.events().len(), 1);

    // History was recorded
    assert_eq!(engine.history().position(), 1);

    // Undo removes the measurement
    engine.undo().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(engine.measurement().len(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn execute_measurement_error_auto_rollback() {
    use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::measurement::*;

    let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();

    engine.begin_transaction();
    engine.execute_measurement(MeasurementOperation::Create {
        start: Vec2::new(0.0, 0.0),
        end: Vec2::new(5.0, 0.0),
        label: "Test".to_string(),
    }).unwrap();

    // This fails — measurement doesn't exist
    let err = engine.execute_measurement(MeasurementOperation::Remove {
        id: MeasurementId::from_raw(999),
    }).unwrap_err();

    assert!(matches!(err, DomainError::Measurement(MeasurementError::NotFound { .. })));

    // Transaction was auto-rolled back
    assert!(!engine.in_transaction());
    assert_eq!(engine.measurement().len(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn measurement_dirty_tracking() {
    use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::measurement::*;
    use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::Vec2;

    let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();
    engine.mark_saved();
    assert!(!engine.is_dirty());

    engine.execute_measurement(MeasurementOperation::Create {
        start: Vec2::zero(),
        end: Vec2::new(1.0, 0.0),
        label: "x".to_string(),
    }).unwrap();

    assert!(engine.is_dirty());

    engine.mark_saved();
    assert!(!engine.is_dirty());
}

docs.title: Undo limitation
docs.text: The current DomainEngine only reverses Canvas2D state on undo (via the executed_canvas parallel list). For other environments, the HistoryStore position changes but the environment state isn't reversed. A real Domain Engine would extend this pattern to all environments.

docs.title: Cross-Environment Operations
docs.text: This guide shows how to group operations across multiple environments into a single undoable unit using compound operations.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    COMP[begin_compound] --> EXEC1[execute_canvas<br/>Create object]
    EXEC1 --> EXEC2[execute_layers<br/>Create layer]
    EXEC2 --> EXEC3[execute_timeline<br/>Insert clip]
    EXEC3 --> COMMIT[commit_compound]

    UNDO[undo] -->|reverses all 3| ENV1[Canvas cleared]
    UNDO -->|reverses all 3| ENV2[Layers cleared]
    UNDO -->|reverses all 3| ENV3[Timeline cleared]

A compound operation groups multiple execute_* calls across different environments. Undo reverses all of them as a single unit. This is useful when a user action logically spans multiple environments — e.g., "create a shape" might create a canvas object, a layer, and a timeline keyframe.

docs.title: Transactions vs Compound Operations
docs.text:
Feature Transaction Compound Purpose Group operations for undo Same, with nesting API begin_transaction() / commit_transaction() begin_compound() / commit_compound() Nesting Not supported Supported (compound_depth counter) Rollback rollback_transaction() rollback_compound() Implementation Uses TransactionManager directly Wraps transactions with depth counter

Compound operations use transactions internally. The compound_depth counter allows nesting: the outermost commit_compound triggers the actual commit_transaction.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
use app_shell::domain_engine::DomainEngine;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::canvas_2d::*;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::layers::*;
use app_shell::domain_foundation::environments::timeline::*;

let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();

// Start a compound operation
engine.begin_compound();

// Execute across multiple environments
engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create {
    transform: Transform::identity(),
}).unwrap();

engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::CreateLayer {
    name: "Shape Layer".to_string(),
}).unwrap();

engine.execute_timeline(TimelineOperation::CreateTrack).unwrap();

// Commit — all three are now one undoable unit
engine.commit_compound();

// Verify state
assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 1);
assert_eq!(engine.layers().len(), 1);
assert_eq!(engine.timeline().track_count(), 1);

// One undo reverses ALL three
engine.undo().unwrap();

assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);
assert_eq!(engine.layers().len(), 0);
assert_eq!(engine.timeline().track_count(), 0);

docs.title: begin_compound
docs.text:
pub fn begin_compound(&mut self) -> TransactionId {
    self.compound_depth += 1;
    if self.compound_depth == 1 {
        // Outermost compound — start a transaction
        self.begin_transaction();
    }
    self.active_transaction.unwrap()
}

Each execute_* call during the compound creates a HistoryEntry with .with_transaction(tx_id).

docs.title: commit_compound
docs.text:
pub fn commit_compound(&mut self) -> Option<TransactionId> {
    if self.compound_depth > 0 {
        self.compound_depth -= 1;
        if self.compound_depth == 0 {
            // Outermost compound — commit the transaction
            self.commit_transaction()
        } else {
            // Nested — just return the active tx id
            self.active_transaction
        }
    } else {
        None
    }
}

docs.title: Undo
docs.text:
When undo() is called, the HistoryStore checks the transaction_id on entries. If present, it undoes all entries with the same id in one call.

// HistoryStore::undo() behavior:
// - If entry has transaction_id → undo all entries with that id
// - If entry has no transaction_id → undo just that one entry

docs.title: Nested Compounds
docs.text:
let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();

// Outer compound
engine.begin_compound();

engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create {
    transform: Transform::identity(),
}).unwrap();

// Inner compound (nested)
engine.begin_compound();

engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::CreateLayer {
    name: "Inner 1".to_string(),
}).unwrap();

engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::CreateLayer {
    name: "Inner 2".to_string(),
}).unwrap();

engine.commit_compound();  // Inner compound ends (depth back to 1)

engine.execute_timeline(TimelineOperation::CreateTrack).unwrap();

engine.commit_compound();  // Outer compound ends (depth back to 0)

// All operations (canvas + 2 layers + timeline) undo as one unit
engine.undo().unwrap();

assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);
assert_eq!(engine.layers().len(), 0);
assert_eq!(engine.timeline().track_count(), 0);

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
rollback_compound() discards all operations in the compound:

engine.begin_compound();

engine.execute_canvas(Create { ... }).unwrap();
engine.execute_layers(CreateLayer { ... }).unwrap();

// Something went wrong — rollback
engine.rollback_compound();

assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);
assert_eq!(engine.layers().len(), 0);
assert!(!engine.in_transaction());

rollback_compound(): 1. Sets compound_depth = 0 2. Calls rollback_transaction() which: - Undoes canvas operations from transaction_start_position to current position - Removes transaction entries from HistoryStore - Truncates executed_canvas to the new position

docs.title: Auto-Rollback on Error
docs.text:
If any execute_* fails during a compound, the entire compound is auto-rolled back:

engine.begin_compound();

engine.execute_canvas(Create { ... }).unwrap();  // Succeeds
engine.execute_layers(CreateLayer { ... }).unwrap();  // Succeeds

// This fails — layer doesn't exist
let err = engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::SetVisibility {
    id: LayerId::from_raw(999),
    visible: false,
}).unwrap_err();

// Auto-rollback happened
assert!(!engine.in_transaction());
assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);  // Canvas was undone
assert_eq!(engine.layers().len(), 0);  // Layers were undone

The check_auto_rollback() method is called inside every execute_* on error:

fn check_auto_rollback(&mut self, _error: &DomainError) {
    if self.active_transaction.is_some() {
        let _ = self.rollback_transaction();
    }
}

This also rolls back compounds (since compounds use transactions internally).

docs.title: Dirty Tracking with Compounds
docs.text:
engine.mark_saved();
assert!(!engine.is_dirty());

engine.begin_compound();
engine.execute_canvas(Create { ... }).unwrap();
engine.execute_layers(CreateLayer { ... }).unwrap();
engine.commit_compound();

assert!(engine.is_dirty());  // Compound created unsaved changes

// Undo the compound
engine.undo().unwrap();
assert!(engine.is_dirty());  // Undo also creates unsaved state (back to saved position)

is_dirty() compares saved_position with history.position(). A compound undo changes the position, so the document becomes dirty.

docs.title: Events with Compounds
docs.text:
Each execute_* call publishes an event immediately — there's no batching:

engine.begin_compound();
engine.execute_canvas(Create { ... }).unwrap();    // Event: canvas.object.created
engine.execute_layers(CreateLayer { ... }).unwrap();  // Event: layers.layer.created
engine.commit_compound();

assert_eq!(engine.events().len(), 2);  // Two events, one per operation

Undo publishes one additional event:

engine.undo().unwrap();  // Event: domain.undo
assert_eq!(engine.events().len(), 3);  // 2 execute + 1 undo

docs.title: When to Use Compounds
docs.text: Scenario Use compound? Why User drags a shape (move + update layer + record keyframe) ✅ One user action, multiple environment changes User creates a new project (many operations) ✅ Initialize multiple environments atomically User deletes an object (remove from canvas + remove layer + remove timeline clip) ✅ Related removals should undo together User types text ❌ Single environment, use regular execute_text_editor() User moves a single canvas object ❌ Single operation, no compound needed Importing a file (many operations) ✅ All-or-nothing — if import fails, rollback everything

docs.title: Testing Cross-Environment Operations
docs.text:
#[test]
fn compound_undoes_across_environments() {
    let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();

    engine.begin_compound();
    engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create {
        transform: Transform::identity(),
    }).unwrap();
    engine.execute_layers(LayersOperation::CreateLayer {
        name: "Test".to_string(),
    }).unwrap();
    engine.execute_timeline(TimelineOperation::CreateTrack).unwrap();
    engine.commit_compound();

    assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(engine.layers().len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(engine.timeline().track_count(), 1);

    // Undo all three as one unit
    engine.undo().unwrap();

    assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);
    assert_eq!(engine.layers().len(), 0);
    assert_eq!(engine.timeline().track_count(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn compound_rollback_discards_all() {
    let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();

    engine.begin_compound();
    engine.execute_canvas(Create { ... }).unwrap();
    engine.execute_layers(CreateLayer { ... }).unwrap();
    engine.rollback_compound();

    assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);
    assert_eq!(engine.layers().len(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn nested_compounds_undo_as_one() {
    let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();

    engine.begin_compound();
    engine.execute_canvas(Create { ... }).unwrap();

    engine.begin_compound();
    engine.execute_layers(CreateLayer { ... }).unwrap();
    engine.execute_layers(CreateLayer { ... }).unwrap();
    engine.commit_compound();  // Inner

    engine.execute_timeline(CreateTrack).unwrap();
    engine.commit_compound();  // Outer

    // Undo everything as one unit
    engine.undo().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);
    assert_eq!(engine.layers().len(), 0);
    assert_eq!(engine.timeline().track_count(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn auto_rollback_on_error_in_compound() {
    let mut engine = DomainEngine::new();

    engine.begin_compound();
    engine.execute_canvas(Create { ... }).unwrap();

    // Fail — triggers auto-rollback
    let _err = engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Remove {
        id: ObjectId::from_raw(999),
    }).unwrap_err();

    assert!(!engine.in_transaction());
    assert_eq!(engine.canvas().len(), 0);
}

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text: Limitation Description Undo only reverses Canvas2D state The executed_canvas parallel list only tracks Canvas operations. Timeline, Layers, etc. record in HistoryStore but their state isn't reversed. A real Domain Engine would extend this. No event batching Each execute_* publishes immediately. There's no "collect events and publish at compound commit." Compound depth not queryable No pub fn compound_depth(&self) -> usize method. Could be added if needed.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• begin_compound() called before the first execute_*
  • commit_compound() called after the last execute_*
  • Error handling: auto-rollback is automatic, but errors should be handled gracefully
  • Test: compound undo reverses all environments
  • Test: rollback discards all changes
  • Test: auto-rollback on error
  • Test: nested compounds undo as one unit

docs.title: Performance Guide
docs.text: This guide documents the time complexity of every key operation across all environments, caching strategies, and when to optimize.

docs.title: Document: Cached char_count
docs.text:
Document::len() is O(1) because it caches char_count: u32. All mutating methods update the cache:

Method Cache update insert(pos, text) char_count += text.chars().count() delete(range) char_count -= range.len() replace(range, text) char_count = char_count - removed + added clear() char_count = 0 replace_all(...) char_count = text.chars().count() (full recompute)

Without caching, every len() call would be O(n) via text.chars().count().

docs.title: Canvas: draw_order Vec
docs.text: The draw_order: Vec<ObjectId> provides O(1) draw-order access while objects: HashMap provides O(1) id lookup. Without the Vec, draw-order iteration would require sorting.

docs.title: HashMap vs BTreeSet Tradeoffs
docs.text:
Collection Used for Iteration order Lookup HashMap Object storage Unspecified O(1) Vec Draw order, row/column order, track order Defined O(n) for position, O(1) for index BTreeSet TagSet Sorted (deterministic) O(log n) HashMap Relation by_source/by_target Unspecified O(1) Vec Priority-sorted relations Priority order O(n)

BTreeSet is used for TagSet to guarantee deterministic iteration order (important for tests and UI display).

docs.title: Clone Costs
docs.text:
Operations and outcomes are Clone (required for history recording). The cost depends on the data:

Type Clone cost Notes CanvasOperation O(1) to O(n) Move is O(1); Create copies a Transform (Copy); Remove copies nothing CanvasOutcome O(1) to O(n) Moved copies a Transform (Copy); Removed clones an Object (Copy) TableOperation O(1) to O(n) SetCellValue clones CellValue (O(1) to O(n) for Text) TimelineOperation O(1) to O(n) InsertClip is O(1); Move is O(1)

Most clones are cheap because: - ObjectId, Transform, Vec2, Vec3 are Copy - Object and Object3D are Copy - String clones are O(n) but typically short

docs.title:
Arc vs Direct Ownership Pattern Used by Pros Cons Direct ownership DomainEngine Fast, no locking Can't share with command handlers Arc<Mutex<Env>> Command handlers Shareable across threads Lock overhead, potential poisoning

The DomainEngine owns environments directly. Command handlers wrap Arc<Mutex<Env>> so both the engine and handler see the same state.

For best performance, prefer the DomainEngine's execute_* methods over command handlers when you don't need the App Engine's command dispatch.

Spatial Indexing

objects_in_bounds() on Canvas2D and Viewport3D is O(n) — a linear scan. For large scenes (1000+ objects), consider adding a spatial index:

Index type Best for Complexity Quadtree (2D) Canvas2D with many static objects O(log n) query BVH (3D) Viewport3D with many objects O(log n) query Grid (2D) Uniform distribution O(1) query (fixed cell size)

The foundation doesn't include spatial indexes — they're application-specific. A Domain Engine wraps the environment and maintains an index alongside it.

When to Optimize Scenario Optimize? Why len() is O(n) ✅ Called frequently; cache the count objects_in_bounds is O(n) with <100 objects ❌ Linear scan is fine for small N objects_in_bounds is O(n) with 10K+ objects ✅ Add a spatial index remove_layer is O(n) for deep hierarchies Maybe BFS is acceptable for typical depths (<20) topological_sort is O(V+E) ❌ This is optimal; can't do better propagate_from is O(R×D) Maybe If R is large (100+ relations on one source), consider batching find_all is O(n×m) Maybe For very long documents, consider Boyer-Moore

Benchmarking

The foundation includes criterion benchmarks:

# Run all benchmarks
cargo bench

# Run specific benchmark
cargo bench -- canvas_create_100_objects
cargo bench -- document_len_1000_chars
cargo bench -- timeline_insert_50_clips
cargo bench -- relation_register_100

  • Hot-path operations are O(1) or O(log n)
  • No O(n²) operations in common paths

Migration Guide
docs.text: This guide covers how to handle changes to the Domain Foundation — adding new enum variants, adding fields to structs, deprecating APIs, and maintaining backward compatibility.

docs.title: Semver and Breaking Changes
docs.text:
The Domain Foundation follows semantic versioning:

Change type Version bump Breaking? New environment, utility, or method Minor (0.x.0) No New enum variant Minor No (with #[non_exhaustive]) New struct field with default Minor No (with #[serde(default)]) Remove or rename a type Major (x.0.0) Yes Change a method signature Major Yes Change enum variant structure Major Yes

docs.title: Adding New Enum Variants
docs.text: Adding a variant to CanvasOperation or CanvasOutcome is the most common change. It breaks all exhaustive match statements on the enum.

docs.title: Step 1: Mark enums as #[non_exhaustive]
docs.text:
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum CanvasOperation {
    Create { transform: Transform },
    Move { id: ObjectId, translation: Vec2 },
    // ...
    // Future variants can be added without breaking downstream matches
}

With #[non_exhaustive], downstream crates must include a _ arm in their match statements. This allows adding variants in minor versions.

docs.title: Step 2: Add the variant
docs.text:
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum CanvasOperation {
    // ... existing ...
    SetColor { id: ObjectId, color: String },  // ← NEW
}

docs.title: Step 3: Update all match arms
docs.text:
Search for every file that matches on the enum:

# Find all files that match on CanvasOperation
grep -rn "match.*CanvasOperation" src/ tests/

Update each match to include the new variant or a _ wildcard:

// In operations.rs apply()
match self {
    CanvasOperation::Create { .. } => { /* ... */ },
    CanvasOperation::SetColor { .. } => { /* ... */ },  // ← ADD
    // If #[non_exhaustive] is used, _ is required for downstream crates
}

// In domain_engine/mod.rs
fn event_name_for_canvas_outcome(outcome: &CanvasOutcome) -> &'static str {
    match outcome {
        // ... existing ...
        CanvasOutcome::ColorSet { .. } => "canvas.object.color_set",  // ← ADD
    }
}

docs.title: Files to update when adding a variant
docs.text: File What to update environments/xxx/operations.rs apply() method domain_engine/operations/canvas_operations.rs undo(), redo(), history_entry(), event() domain_engine/mod.rs Name helper functions domain_engine/operations/canvas_command_handler.rs Match arms tests/.../xxx_operations_test.rs New test for the variant

docs.title: Adding New Struct Fields
docs.text: Adding a field to an existing struct is breaking if the struct is constructed externally.

docs.title: Option A: Add with Default (backward compatible)
docs.text:
pub struct Object {
    pub id: ObjectId,
    pub transform: Transform,
    pub color: String,  // ← NEW
}

impl Object {
    pub fn new(id: ObjectId, transform: Transform) -> Self {
        Self {
            id,
            transform,
            color: String::new(),  // ← Default value
        }
    }
}

Existing code calling Object::new(id, transform) still works — color is set to default.

docs.title: Option B: Use a builder
docs.text:
pub struct Object {
    pub id: ObjectId,
    pub transform: Transform,
    pub color: String,
}

impl Object {
    pub fn new(id: ObjectId, transform: Transform) -> Self {
        Self { id, transform, color: String::new() }
    }

    pub fn with_color(mut self, color: String) -> Self {
        self.color = color;
        self
    }
}

docs.title: Serde compatibility
docs.text:
When adding a field, use #[serde(default)] so old serialized data can still be deserialized:

#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
pub struct Object {
    pub id: ObjectId,
    pub transform: Transform,
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub color: String,  // Old data without "color" field deserializes with default
}

docs.title: Step 1: Add #[deprecated] attribute
docs.text:
#[deprecated(note = "use execute_canvas() instead", since = "0.2.0")]
pub fn execute(&mut self, operation: CanvasOperation) -> Result<CanvasOutcome, CanvasError> {
    self.execute_canvas(operation).map_err(|e| match e {
        DomainError::Canvas(ce) => ce,
        _ => unreachable!(),
    })
}

docs.title: Step 2: Keep the old API working
docs.text: The deprecated method should call the new method internally. Don't remove it until a major version.

docs.title: Step 3: Update tests to use the new API
docs.text:
// Old (deprecated)
let outcome = engine.execute(CanvasOperation::Create { ... }).unwrap();

// New
let outcome = engine.execute_canvas(CanvasOperation::Create { ... }).unwrap();

docs.title: Step 4: Remove in next major version
docs.text: When bumping to a major version (e.g., 1.0.0), remove deprecated methods entirely.

docs.title: Adding New Environments
docs.text:
Adding a new environment is non-breaking — no existing code changes:

  1. Create the environment under environments/
  2. Add pub mod xxx; to environments/mod.rs
  3. Add the field, getter, and execute_xxx() to DomainEngine
  4. Add the DomainError variant
  5. Add tests

No existing match statements need updating because the new environment has its own types.

docs.title: Adding New Utilities
docs.text:
Adding a new utility is non-breaking:

  1. Create the utility under utilities/
  2. Add pub mod xxx; to utilities/mod.rs
  3. Add tests

No existing code changes — utilities are opt-in and don't modify environments.

docs.title: Adding serde derives to existing types
docs.text: Adding #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(...))] is non-breaking — without the feature, the attribute is a no-op.

docs.title: Changing field structure
docs.text:
If you change a field's type or structure:

Change Old serialized data Solution Add field Missing in old data #[serde(default)] Remove field Extra in old data Serde ignores unknown fields by default Rename field Different key name #[serde(rename = "old_name")] Change type Incompatible Custom deserialize_with or version field

docs.title: Version field pattern
docs.text:
For major structural changes, add a version field:

#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
pub struct CanvasV2 {
    #[serde(default = "default_version")]
    version: u32,
    objects: HashMap<ObjectId, Object>,
    draw_order: Vec<ObjectId>,
    next_id: u64,
}

fn default_version() -> u32 { 1 }

docs.title: Scenario 1: New operation variant added
docs.text:
Before: CanvasOperation has 6 variants
After:  CanvasOperation has 7 variants (added SetColor)

Affected files:
1. operations.rs — add apply arm
2. canvas_operations.rs — add undo/redo/history_entry/event arms
3. domain_engine/mod.rs — add name helper arms
4. canvas_command_handler.rs — add match arms
5. tests — add test for new variant

docs.title: Scenario 2: New field on a data struct
docs.text:
Before: Object has { id, transform }
After:  Object has { id, transform, color }

Affected files:
1. object.rs — add field, update new(), add with_color()
2. canvas.rs — update create_object (if it sets the field)
3. serde — add #[serde(default)] if applicable
4. tests — update assertions

docs.title: Scenario 3: Renaming a method
docs.text:
Before: engine.execute(op)
After:  engine.execute_canvas(op)

Steps:
1. Add execute_canvas() as the new method
2. Mark execute() as #[deprecated]
3. Make execute() call execute_canvas() internally
4. Update all internal callers to use execute_canvas()
5. Update tests to use execute_canvas()
6. In next major version, remove execute()

docs.title: Scenario 4: Removing an operation variant
docs.text:
Before: CanvasOperation has SetColor
After:  SetColor removed (color moved to a different system)

Steps:
1. Mark SetColor as #[deprecated]
2. In next major version, remove the variant
3. Update all match arms
4. Update tests

docs.title: Versioning Strategy
docs.text: Version When to bump Example Patch (0.0.x) Bug fixes, no API changes Fix undo bug Minor (0.x.0) New features, new variants, new environments Add Measurement environment Major (x.0.0) Breaking changes (remove types, change signatures) Remove deprecated execute()

docs.title: Checklist for Safe Changes
docs.text:
• New enum variants: add #[non_exhaustive] or update all match arms
  • New struct fields: provide default in new() + #[serde(default)]
  • Deprecated methods: add #[deprecated] + keep working + update tests
  • Serde changes: test round-trip with old and new format
  • All existing tests still pass
  • New tests added for new functionality
  • Documentation updated
